articles.title: A
articles.body:
## The letter sound

The letter name is spoken as the sound /a/. Its main sound is heard in the word (apă) /ˈa.pə/, which means water. This letter makes only one sound in Romanian.

## Mouth movements

Open your mouth wide and relax your lips. Keep your tongue low and flat on the floor of your mouth. Let your vocal cords vibrate freely as air flows out. Place a hand on your throat to feel the steady vibration.

## Reading the letter

This letter always represents the sound /a/ in all positions. It keeps this sound whether stressed or unstressed, as in the word (casă) /ˈka.sə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not narrow your mouth into the vowel of the English word cat. Keep your mouth opened wide, like the vowel sound in father.
articles.summary: The letter A is the first letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Ă
articles.body:
## The letter sound

This letter is called /ə/. Its main sound is the sound /ə/, heard in the word (ăsta) /ˈmə.r/, which means apple. This letter makes only one sound in Romanian.

## How to say it

Relax your tongue in the middle of your mouth. Keep your lips neutral and slightly open. Let the air flow freely without tension. Your voice vibrates. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /ə/ in every word position. You hear it stressed in the word (măr) /mər/. You also hear it unstressed at the end of the word (apă) /ˈa.pə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace this sound with the open vowel in the English word cat. Do not round your lips as you do in the English word fur. Keep your lips relaxed and completely still.
articles.summary: The letter Ă is a character in the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Â
articles.body:
## The letter name and sound

The name of this letter is the sound /ɨ/. It makes the vowel sound /ɨ/, as in the word (român) /roˈmɨn/, which means Romanian. This letter has only one sound in all words.

## Pronouncing this sound

Keep your lips relaxed and flat. Pull the middle of your tongue up toward the roof of your mouth. Do not push your tongue forward or pull it too far back. Let your vocal cords vibrate. Place two fingers on your throat to feel the steady vibration as you make this sound.

## Reading this letter

You see this letter only inside words, never at the beginning or at the very end. It always represents the single sound /ɨ/, as in the word (cânt) /kɨnt/.

## Avoiding common mistakes

Do not replace this vowel with the short vowel in the English word sit. Do not round your lips as you would for the vowel in soon. Keep your lips flat, pull your tongue slightly back, and make the sound deep inside your mouth.
articles.summary: The letter Â is a character in the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## Sound of letter B

The name of this letter is /b/. It always makes the sound /b/, as in the word (băiat) /bun/, which means good. This letter has only one sound in Romanian. It never changes its value across different words or positions.

## How to say it

Close both lips firmly to stop the flow of air. Let your vocal cords vibrate to produce voice. Then open your lips quickly so the trapped air bursts out. Put your hand on your throat. You can feel a steady vibration as the sound breaks out.

## Reading and spelling

This letter always keeps the sound /b/ in all standard positions. You hear it at the start of a word, as in (bun) /bun/. You also hear it clearly at the end of a word, as in (alb) /alb/.

## Mistakes to avoid

There is no real pitfall with this letter. It sounds just like the letter b in the ordinary English word book. Always remember to use your voice fully, even when the letter comes at the end of a word.
articles.summary: The letter B is a consonant in the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name sounds like /k/ or /tʃ/. Its main sound appears in (casă) /kasp/, which means house. This letter makes two sounds.

## Mouth and voice

Raise the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Block the air, then release it quickly without your voice. For the other sound, press your tongue behind your top front teeth. Push the air through as your tongue drops. Hold your hand on your neck to feel no vibration.

## Reading this letter

You pronounce the sound /k/ before consonants and before most vowels, as in (cald) /kald/. You pronounce the sound /tʃ/ when the letter stands before e or i, as in (ceai) /tʃaj/ and (cinci) /tʃintʃ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not add a strong puff of air. Keep the sound crisp, unlike the sound in kite. Never soften the letter into an s sound before front vowels.
articles.summary: The letter C is a consonant in the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## Letter sound

This letter is called /d/. It makes the sound /d/, like in the word (dorință) /dor/, which means longing. The letter always makes one single sound.

## Mouth movements

Place the tip of your tongue against the back of your top front teeth. Block the air completely. Then release your tongue as you vibrate your vocal cords. Touch your throat to feel that buzzing vibration.

## Reading rules

In all standard positions, this letter makes the sound /d/. You hear it clearly in the word (cald) /kald/.

## Common mistakes

Do not place your tongue behind the teeth on the upper gum like in English door. Keep the tip firmly against the back of your top front teeth instead.
articles.summary: The letter D is a consonant in the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is spoken as the sound /e/, that is a full vowel e. Its main sound is heard in (elefant) /ˈe.le.fant/, which means elephant. This letter makes three different sounds in Romanian words.

## How to say it

For the first sound, open your mouth halfway and spread your lips wide. Keep your tongue high and forward. For the second sound, begin with a quick glide before the main vowel. For the third sound, glide smoothly from this vowel toward the next vowel without stopping. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz steadily.

## Spelling rules

In most words, this letter makes the sound /e/, that is a full vowel e, as in (elev) /eˈlev/. At the start of personal pronouns and forms of the verb to be, it makes the sound /je/, as in (el) /jel/. When it glides into another vowel, it makes the sound /e̯/, that is a gliding vowel e, as in (seară) /ˈse̯a.rə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the simple vowel into a glide like the vowel sound in day. Keep your tongue steady and pure from start to finish. In basic pronouns, do not drop the initial glide like the start of elbow. Make sure you add the quick glide heard at the beginning of yes.
articles.summary: The letter E is the fifth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## The letter sound

This letter is called /f/. Its main sound is the sound /f/, heard in (floare) /flo̯a.re/, which means flower. The letter makes only one sound in Romanian.

## Pronouncing the letter

Touch your lower lip gently against your upper teeth. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap without using your voice. Place a hand on your throat to check that your vocal cords do not buzz.

## Reading the letter

This letter always makes the sound /f/ in all regular positions. You can hear it at the start of (foc) /fok/.

## Tips for learners

This sound is identical to the first sound in the English word fish. There is no real pitfall for this letter.
articles.summary: The letter F is the sixth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## The letter G

This letter is called /g/ or /dʒ/. Its main sound is heard in (gară) /ɡar/, which means train station. The letter makes two sounds in total.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Release the air with your voice on. For the second sound, press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Push air through while your vocal cords vibrate. Put your hand on your throat to feel the vibration.

## Reading the variants

You make the sound /ɡ/ before the letters a, ă, â, o, u, before consonants, or at the end of a word. You hear it in (gard) /ɡard/. You make the sound /dʒ/ before the letters e or i. You hear this sound in (ger) /dʒer/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not soften the hard sound before back vowels. Make sure you use your voice clearly, unlike the quiet sound in cat. Also, do not pronounce the soft sound like the sound in pleasure. Make a clean stop first, just like the sound in gem.
articles.summary: The letter G is the seventh letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## The letter haș

The letter name is spoken as the sound /h/, that is a standard h sound. Its main sound appears in the word (hartă) /harˈtə/, which means map. This letter produces three sounds in Romanian speech.

## How to say it

For the first sound, breathe out gently through an open mouth. Keep your tongue relaxed and let air whisper past your throat. For the next sound, push the middle of your tongue close to the hard roof. Force the air through that narrow gap. For the last sound, raise the back of your tongue toward the soft palate. Breathe out with light friction. Place a hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords stay completely still.

## Spelling rules

Before back vowels and at the start of most native words, say the sound /h/, that is a standard h sound, as in (horă) /ˈho.rə/. Before front vowels, pronounce the sound /ç/, that is a soft h sound, heard in (harnic) /ˈhar.nik/ and (hienă) /ˈhje.nə/. At the end of a word or before consonants, speak the sound /x/, like in (valah) /vaˈlah/ or (duh) /duh/.

## Comparing with English

English speakers often drop this letter because of words like hour or honest. In Romanian, you must always pronounce it clearly. The sound at the end of words is stronger than the sound in house. Do not make it silent like the h in vehicle. Move your tongue further back and push steady air through your mouth.
articles.summary: The letter H is the eighth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is the sound /i/ or /j/. Its main sound is the vowel sound /i/, as in the word (inimă) /iˈnel/, which means ring. This letter has three different sounds in total.

## How to say it

Spread your lips wide and raise the front of your tongue close to your roof. Let your vocal cords vibrate, and feel the buzz by touching your neck. For the second sound, glide your tongue quickly toward the roof while moving into another vowel. For the third sound, raise your tongue slightly without making a full vowel, releasing a brief breath.

## Where each sound occurs

As a standard full vowel, this letter sounds like the sound /i/, as in (inel) /iˈnel/. It sounds like the glide sound /j/ next to another vowel, as in (iarbă) /ˈjar.bə/. At the end of a word after consonants, it marks a short whisper sound /ʲ/, heard in (lupi) /lupʲ/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not replace the vowel with the short vowel in English bit. Keep your tongue high and tense, like the vowel in see. At the end of words, do not add an extra syllable. Never turn the final light mark into a full vowel sound.
articles.summary: The letter I is the ninth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Î
articles.body:
## The letter î

The letter name is spoken as the sound /ɨ/. It makes this sound in the word (înger) /ɨn.t͡seˈleɡ/, which means to understand. This letter has only one sound in Romanian.

## Pronouncing the sound

Pull your tongue straight back into the middle of your mouth. Keep your lips relaxed and spread flat. Let your voice hum steadily from your throat. Touch your neck with two fingers to feel the strong vibration.

## Reading this letter

This letter always keeps the same value. It makes the sound /ɨ/ in every position, as shown in the word (hotărî) /ho.təˈrɨ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace this vowel with the vowel in the English word sit. Do not make the sound in boot with circle lips either. Pull your tongue back, keep your lips flat, and make the sound deep inside your mouth.
articles.summary: The letter Î is the tenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The name of this letter is /ʒ/. It makes the sound /ʒ/, heard in (joc) /ʒos/, which means down or below. This letter has only one sound in Romanian.

## How to say it

Round your lips slightly and push them forward. Raise the front of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap. Vibrate your vocal cords at the same time. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the steady buzz.

## Reading rules

This letter always keeps its single sound. You pronounce it as the sound /ʒ/ in all native positions, like in the word (plajă) /ˈpla.ʒə/.

## Common mistakes

English speakers often replace this sound with the sound at the start of jam. Do not stop the air or add a hard front sound. Keep the air flowing smoothly without any sudden block, just like the middle consonant in the English word measure.
articles.summary: The letter J is the eleventh letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## Sound of letter K

The name of this letter is /k/. Its main sound is heard in (kilogram) /ˈki.lo/, which means kilo. This letter makes two sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly without using your vocal cords. For the second sound, make that same tap while raising the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Hold a hand to your throat to feel that your voice stays quiet.

## Reading and spelling

Before back vowels like a, o, u or consonants, this letter makes the sound /k/, that is a plain k sound, as in (karate) /kaˈra.te/. Before front vowels like e or i, it makes the sound /kʲ/, that is a softened k sound, as in (kilo) /ˈki.lo/.

## Common mistakes

Do not release a puff of air after this letter. You might say it like the strong start of king. Keep the sound dry, just like the k in skin.
articles.summary: The letter K is the twelfth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## The sound of el

The letter name is the sound /l/. It makes the sound /l/, like in the word (luna) /lup/, which means wolf. This letter has only one sound in Romanian.

## How to say it

Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with the tip of your tongue. Let the air flow smoothly around the sides of your tongue. Vibrate your vocal cords with your voice. You can feel your throat buzz when you touch it.

## Where it appears

This letter always makes the sound /l/ in all standard positions. You can hear it at the start of a word in (lup) /lup/. You also hear it before another consonant in the word (cald) /kald/.

## Common mistakes

Do not make a dark sound at the end of syllables like in the English word ball. Keep the back of your tongue down. Make a clear, light sound like in the English word leap every time.
articles.summary: The letter L is the twelfth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## The letter em

The letter name is (mare) /ˈma.mə/, which means mother. Its main sound is heard in that same word. This letter makes two distinct sounds in Romanian speech.

## Mouth movements

Close both lips together. Send air out through your nose while your voice hums. For the softened sound, press the middle of your tongue upward at the same time. You can feel your throat buzz with your fingers.

## Spelling rules

In most places, you pronounce the sound /m/, that is standard m. An example is (om) /om/. At the end of a word before short i, you say the sound /mʲ/, that is softened m. You hear this in the word (dormi) /dormʲ/.

## Common mistakes

This sound matches the English sound in moon. The softened sound is like the start of mute, but without a full vowel. Keep the lips fully shut until the sound ends.
articles.summary: The letter M is the thirteenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## Sound of letter N

The name of this letter is /n/. Its main sound is the sound /n/ as in the word (nor) /now/, which means night. This letter has two sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, place the tip of your tongue against your upper gum. Let the air pass through your nose while your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Keep the air flowing through your nose. Put a finger beside your nose to feel it vibrate.

## Reading rules

In most places, this letter makes the sound /n/ as in (nou) /now/. Before the letters c or g, it makes the sound /ŋ/ as in (bancă) /ˈbaŋ.kə/.

## Common mistakes

You may drop the nose airflow too early at the end of a word. Keep your tongue pressed firmly in place and let the sound ring clearly through your nose, just like in the English word sun.
articles.summary: The letter N is the fourteenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter name is the sound /o/, that is a pure full vowel. Its main sound is heard in the word (om) /om/, which means man or human. This Romanian letter has two sounds altogether.

## Pronunciation guide

For the full vowel, pull your tongue back and round your lips into an open circle. Let your vocal cords vibrate steadily. For the gliding sound, round your lips tightly and slide quickly into the next vowel. Place your hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Spelling rules

In most positions, the letter makes the sound /o/, that is a pure full vowel. You can hear this sound in (copil) /koˈpil/. Before another vowel, it turns into a quick gliding sound /o̯/, that is a short semivowel. You can hear this glide in (soare) /ˈso̯a.re/.

## Common mistakes

English speakers often turn this vowel into a diphthong, like the sound in boat or go. Keep your lips and jaw completely still until the sound finishes. Do not add a glide at the end.
articles.summary: The letter O is the fifteenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is the sound /p/, that is a plain p. Its main sound appears in the word (pâine) /pəˈmɨnt/, which means bread. This letter makes two distinct sounds in Romanian.

## Pronouncing each sound

Press your lips tightly together and stop the air. Release the air cleanly without using your voice. For the soft variant, press your lips together while raising your tongue toward the roof. Release the lips with a faint y sound. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel a short puff of air.

## When to use each

This letter usually makes the sound /p/, that is a plain p. You hear it before most vowels and consonants, as in (cap) /kap/. At the end of a word before a brief i, it becomes the sound /pʲ/, that is a soft p. You hear this soft form in (lupi) /lupʲ/.

## Avoiding common mistakes

Do not release a heavy puff of air when you start a word. In English words like pin, you blow out extra air. Keep the lips tight and make a crisp stop, like the sound in spin. For the soft ending, do not add a full extra vowel. Keep the closing sound short and quiet.
articles.summary: The letter P is the sixteenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is the sound /r/, that is a rolled r. Its main sound is the sound /r/, that is a rolled r, as in (rac) /rak/, which means crayfish. This letter has two sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, place your tongue tip against the tooth ridge behind your top teeth. Push air out so the tongue tip taps quickly against the ridge. To make the second sound, tap your tongue tip while raising the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Hold your hand against your throat to feel your voice buzz.

## Reading this letter

In all standard positions, this letter makes the sound /r/, that is a rolled r, as in (soare) /ˈso̯a.re/. At the end of a word after a consonant, it makes the sound /rʲ/, that is a softened rolled r, as in (membri) /ˈmem.brʲ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not use the English smooth sound heard in red. Tap the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper front teeth. Do not curl your tongue backward into your mouth.
articles.summary: The letter R is the seventeenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## The letter sound

The letter name is the sound /s/. It makes the sound /s/ in the word (soare) /ˈso̯a.re/, which means sun. This letter has only one sound in Romanian.

## How to say it

Put the tip of your tongue near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Leave a narrow space for the air to hiss through. Keep your lips slightly open. Blow air out steadily without using your voice. Touch your neck to check that your vocal cords do not vibrate.

## Spelling rules

This letter always makes the sound /s/ everywhere it appears. You hear it at the beginning of words and between vowels, as in the word (masă) /ˈma.sə/.

## Common mistakes

In English, this letter often turns into a buzzing sound between vowels, like in the word rose. In Romanian, never buzz it. Always keep it sharp and quiet, like the first sound in the English word sun.
articles.summary: The letter S is the eighteenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Ș
articles.body:
## Letter sound

This letter is called /ʃ/. It makes the sound /ʃ/, as in the word (școală) /ʃoˈsapte/, which means six. This letter has only one sound in Romanian.

## Mouth shape

Push your lips slightly forward. Raise the front of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Blow air gently over your tongue. Your vocal cords stay still. Hold your hand on your neck to feel that it does not vibrate.

## Spelling rules

This letter always makes the sound /ʃ/ everywhere it appears. At the beginning of a word, hear it in (șapte) /ˈʃap.te/. At the end of a word, hear it in (oraș) /oˈraʃ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse this letter with a regular s. It sounds like the English letters sh in the word ship, never like the sound in sun. Keep your lips pushed forward and make a steady rushing sound.
articles.summary: The letter Ș is the nineteenth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## The letter te

The letter is named /t/, that is a plain t sound. Its main sound is heard in (tren) /tata/, which means father, dad. This letter has two different sounds.

## How to say it

Touch the back of your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Release the air sharply without voice. For the soft variant, make this same touch while raising your tongue body toward the roof of your mouth. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel only a tiny puff of air.

## Spelling rules

In almost all positions, this letter makes the sound /t/, that is a plain t sound, as in (tată) /ˈta.tə/. At the end of a word before short final i, it makes the sound /tʲ/, that is a soft t sound, as in (băieți) /bəˈjetsʲ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not puff out a heavy breath like in the English word tea. Keep the release dry and crisp. Also, do not place your tongue behind your teeth on the gum ridge as in table. Press the tongue tip directly against the back of your top front teeth.
articles.summary: The letter T is the twentieth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Ț
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The name of this letter is pronounced /ts/. Its main sound is the sound /ts/, heard in the word (țară) /ˈtsa.rə/, which means country, land. This letter makes only one sound in standard Romanian.

## How to say it

Touch the roof of your mouth just behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Block the air completely for a moment. Then release the air sharply through a narrow gap while blowing. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. Place your hand on your neck to check that there is no buzzing vibration.

## Reading and spelling

This letter always produces the same sound in every standard position. You pronounce it as the sound /ts/ whenever you see it written, like in the word (băiat) /bəˈjat/. It does not change before any vowel or consonant.

## Common mistakes

Do not soften this consonant into the English sound in ship or chin. It is exactly like the sound in the middle of cats or pizza. Keep the initial stop crisp and release it straight into the hissing air. Never add a trailing breath or vowel at the end.
articles.summary: The letter Ț is the twenty-first letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## The letter name and sound

The name of this letter sounds like /u/. Its main sound is heard in the word (urs) /ˈu.nuls/, which means one. This letter makes two sounds.

## Mouth shape and air

Pull your tongue back and raise it high. Round your lips into a tight circle and vibrate your vocal cords. For the gliding sound, keep the same shape and glide quickly into another vowel. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration.

## Reading the variants

As a normal vowel, this letter makes the sound /u/, as in (unu) /ˈu.nu/. When this letter stands next to another vowel, it makes the gliding sound /w/, as in (nou) /now/.

## Common mistakes

Do not make this sound long like the vowel in moon. Keep the sound short and firm. Do not add an extra sound like in the English word you.
articles.summary: The letter U is the twenty-second letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter name is spoken as the sound /v/. It makes the sound /v/ as in the word (vino) /ˈvi.no/, which means come. This letter makes only one sound in standard words.

## How to say it

Touch your upper teeth gently to your lower lip. Push air out steadily while your vocal cords vibrate. Feel your throat buzz with your fingers.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /v/ in all standard positions. Hear it clearly in the word (val) /val/.

## Common mistakes

Do not swap this sound with the sound /w/ in water. Keep your top teeth firmly on your bottom lip. There is no other pitfall.
articles.summary: The letter V is the twenty-third letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## Sound of letter W

The name of this letter sounds like the sound /w/. Its primary sound is heard in (weekend) /ˈvi.kend/, meaning the days of rest. This letter has two sounds.

## Mouth movements

For the first sound, place your top teeth gently on your bottom lip. Push air through the small opening and vibrate your vocal cords. Touch your neck to feel that steady vibration. For the second sound, pull your tongue back into your mouth. Make a small tight circle with your lips. Push air smoothly while your voice hums.

## Reading rules

In borrowed words from German and older borrowings, this letter gives the sound /v/, as in (watt) /vat/. In newer words from modern English, it keeps the sound /w/, as in (web) /web/.

## Common pitfalls

Do not replace the sound /v/ with the sound in water. When a borrowed word demands the sound /v/, press your top teeth on your bottom lip firmly. Do not replace the sound /w/ with the sound in very. Keep your teeth completely away from your lips.
articles.summary: The letter W is the twenty-fourth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## The letter X

You call this letter by the sound /ks/ or /gz/. Its main sound is heard in (xilofon) /ekˈzamen/, which means exam. This letter makes two distinct sounds in Romanian.

## Pronouncing the letter

For the first sound, block air with the back of your tongue. Release it sharply, then hiss through your closed teeth without voice. For the second sound, make that same block and hiss, but turn your voice on. Touch your neck to feel strong vibration.

## Reading rules

Before quiet consonants or at the end of a word, say the sound /ks/. You hear this in (text) /tekst/. Between two vowels, say the sound /gz/. You hear this in (exemplu) /ekˈzemplu/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not soften this letter into the sound in English shoe or jazz. Keep the crisp stop sound first, exactly like the middle of English taxi or exact.
articles.summary: The letter X is the twenty-fifth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## The letter Y

The name of this letter is /j/ or /i/. Its main sound is heard in (yoga) /ˈjo.ɡo/, which means yoga. Romanian borrowed this letter for foreign words. It makes two sounds in total.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first sound, lift the middle of your tongue high toward the roof of your mouth. Keep your lips relaxed and let your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, spread your lips wide into a smile. Raise your tongue high and forward. Put a hand on your throat to feel the steady vibration.

## Reading the letter

This letter appears only in borrowed words. Before another vowel, it sounds like the sound /j/, as in (yankeu) /janˈkew/. When it acts as a vowel, it sounds like the sound /i/, as in (hobby) /ˈxo.bi/.

## Common pitfalls

This letter matches English habits very closely. Do not turn the vowel sound into the sound in happy. Keep the sound clear and steady, like the vowel in see.
articles.summary: The letter Y is the twenty-sixth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## The letter name and sound

The name of this letter is /z/. It makes the sound /z/, as in the word (zi) /ˈzɛ.bre/, which means zebra. This letter has only one sound in Romanian.

## How to say the sound

Bring your teeth close together. Place the tip of your tongue near the gum behind your top teeth. Push air through the narrow gap between your tongue and teeth. Make your vocal cords vibrate. You can touch your throat to feel a strong buzz.

## When to use this sound

The letter always sounds like /z/ in every position. You hear it at the start, in the middle, or at the end of a word. A clear example is (varză) /ˈvar.zə/.

## Common mistakes to avoid

This letter sounds just like the letter z in the English word zoo. Do not turn it into an unvoiced sound like the s in sun. Keep your vocal cords buzzing from the start.
articles.summary: The letter Z is the twenty-seventh letter of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## The letter name

The name of this letter is /k/. Its main sound is the sound /kwi.k‿step/, as in (quasar) /kwi.k‿step/, which means quickstep. The letter has only one sound in Romanian.

## Mouth movements

Raise the back of your tongue to touch the back of the roof of your mouth. Block the air completely. Release the air suddenly without any voice. Put your hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords do not vibrate.

## Reading rules

This letter appears only in foreign loanwords and names. It always makes the sound /k/, as in (Qatar) /kaˈtar/.

## Common mistakes

English words often puff air out after this sound. In Romanian, release the sound cleanly with no extra puff of air. Keep the sound crisp, just like the sound in the English word skin.
articles.summary: The letter Q is part of the Romanian alphabet.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## The letter A

You call this letter (A) /aː/. Its main sound is heard in the word (Apfel) /ˈapfəl/, which means apple. This letter makes two sounds in German.

## How to say it

For the first sound, drop your jaw wide. Keep your tongue low and flat. Let your voice flow freely with unshaped lips. For the second sound, open your mouth wide. Pull your tongue slightly back and hold the tone longer. You can place a hand on your throat to feel your vocal cords vibrate.

## Spelling rules

Before two consonants, the letter makes the sound /a/, that is a short open a. A good example is (Kamm) /kam/. In an open stressed syllable or before the letter h, it sounds long. There it makes the sound /aː/, that is a long held a, as in (Abend) /ˈaːbənt/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace the short vowel with the flat sound in the English word cat. Keep your mouth open wider and your tongue flat. Do not swallow the long sound into the vowel heard in father. Hold the sound clean without moving your tongue.
articles.summary: The letter name is A, as in the word Apfel.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## The letter Be

The letter (Be) /beː/ sounds like the start of (Buch) /buːx/, meaning book. This letter makes two different sounds in German.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, press your lips together tightly. Release a gentle puff of air while your voice hums. Touch your throat to feel that vibration. For the other sound, keep your lips in the exact same spot. Push the air out firmly without any voice. Your throat stays completely still.

## Spelling rules

At the start of a word or syllable before a vowel, you pronounce the sound /b/. You can hear this in (Ball) /bal/. At the end of a syllable or word, the sound changes to the sound /p/. You can hear this in (ab) /ap/, and also in (gelb) /ɡɛlp/.

## Common mistakes

At the end of words, you might want to use a soft voiced sound like in the English word club. Do not hum with your throat there. Make it completely quiet and crisp like the final sound in the English word tap.
articles.summary: The letter name is Be, as in the word Buch.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## The letter Ce

The German letter (Ce) /tseː/ usually sounds like the sound /k/. You hear it in the word (Computer) /kɔmˈpjuːtɐ/, which means an electronic machine. This letter produces three different sounds across borrowed words.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue against the roof. Release the trapped air sharply without your voice. For the second sound, touch the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Release the burst of air into a sharp hiss. For the third sound, keep your tongue close to your upper gum. Blow air forward with no voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel that it does not buzz.

## Spelling rules

You say the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, or u, or before consonants in borrowed words, as in (Café) /kaˈfeː/. You make the sound /ts/ before the front vowels e, i, ä, or ö in words from Latin, as in (Cent) /tsɛnt/. You use the soft sound /s/ in words from French before front vowels, as in (City) /ˈsɪti/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not pronounce the sound /ts/ as the simple English sound in see. Keep the sharp burst of air heard at the end of cats. Do not add a heavy puff of air when you say the sound /k/ after another consonant.
articles.summary: The letter name is Ce, as in the word Computer.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## The letter De

German names this letter (De) /deː/. Its main sound is heard in (Danke) /ˈdaŋkə/, which means thank you. This letter makes two different sounds in German.

## How to say De

Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Release the air while vibrating your vocal cords. Touch the same spot behind your upper teeth for the second sound. Release the air sharply without voice. Place a hand on your throat to feel the voice stop.

## Spelling rules for De

This letter makes the voiced sound /d/ at the beginning of a word or syllable. You hear this sound in (oder) /ˈoːdɐ/. It changes to the crisp sound /t/ at the end of a syllable or word. You hear this voiceless sound in (Bad) /baːt/ and in (und) /ʊnt/.

## Common mistakes with De

Do not voice the final sound like the end of bed. Stop your vocal cords and say a clean sound like the end of bet.
articles.summary: The letter name is De, as in the word Danke.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## The letter E

The letter (E) /eː/ is called (E) /eː/. Its main sound is heard in (Elefant) /eleˈfant/, which means elephant. This letter makes four distinct vowel sounds in German words.

## Pronouncing the letter

For the first sound, spread your lips wide and keep your tongue high and tense. For the second sound, drop your lower jaw slightly and relax your tongue. For the third sound, relax your entire mouth completely and make a very quick, weak vowel. For the fourth sound, open your mouth a bit wider and lower your tongue. Place your hand on your throat to feel your voice box vibrate for all four sounds.

## Spelling and sounds

In long stressed syllables or when doubled, it makes the sound /eː/ as in (Tee) /teː/. In short stressed syllables before several consonants, it makes the sound /ɛ/ as in (Bett) /bɛt/. In unstressed prefixes or word endings, it makes the sound /ə/, that is a weak central vowel, as in (bitte) /ˈbɪtə/. In unstressed endings before the letter r, it makes the sound /ɐ/, that is a short open vowel, as in (Mutter) /ˈmʊtɐ/.

## Avoiding common mistakes

Do not glide into an English sound like the vowel in day. Keep your tongue completely still from start to finish. Also, do not pronounce the unstressed ending like the strong vowel in pet. Keep it short and relaxed.
articles.summary: The letter name is E, as in the word Elefant.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## The letter Ef

The German letter (Ef) /ɛf/ makes the sound /f/. You hear it in the word (Fisch) /fɪʃ/, which means fish. This letter makes only one sound in German.

## Making the sound

Rest your top teeth lightly on your lower lip. Blow air gently through the gap. Do not use your voice. Touch your throat to feel that it does not buzz.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /f/ in every position. You hear it at the start of (finden) /ˈfɪndn̩/. You also hear it when written double, as in (Schiff) /ʃɪf/.

## Tips for English

This letter sounds just like the regular sound in the English word fall. There are no special traps with this sound in German.
articles.summary: The letter name is Ef, as in the word Fisch.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## The letter Ge

The letter is named (Ge) /ɡeː/. Its main sound is heard in the word (Garten) /ˈɡaʁtn̩/, which means garden. This letter makes four different sounds in the language.

## How to say it

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air with your voice. For the second sound, make the same movement without your voice. For the third sound, raise the middle of your tongue toward the hard roof. Blow air through the narrow gap. For the fourth sound, push your lips forward and make a gentle buzzing sound. Touch your throat to feel the voice.

## Spelling rules

At the start of a word or syllable, the letter makes the sound /ɡ/, like in (gut) /ɡuːt/. At the end of a word or syllable, it sounds like the sound /k/, as in (Tag) /taːk/. At the end of a word in the suffix with an i, it makes the soft sound /ç/, as in (könig) /ˈkøːnɪç/. In words borrowed from French, it makes the sound /ʒ/, like in (Garage) /ɡaˈʁaːʒə/.

## Common mistakes

At the end of a word, you might keep your voice on, as in the English word bag. Always end with a crisp sound like the k in back. In the ending with an i, do not make a hard k sound. Whisper air smoothly across the roof of your mouth instead.
articles.summary: The letter name is Ge, as in the word Garten.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## The letter Ha

The name of this letter is spoken as (Ha) /haː/. Its main sound is the sound /h/, as heard in the word (Haus) /haʊ̯s/, which means house. Across German words, this letter has two different pronunciations.

## Mouth and voice

To make the first sound, keep your mouth open and relax your tongue. Breathe out gently through your throat without using your vocal cords. Hold a hand before your lips to feel the warm puff of air. For the other sound, do not move your mouth at all. Keep your throat silent.

## Spelling rules

At the start of a word or a stressed syllable, it makes the sound /h/, as in (Hand) /hant/. After a vowel, you do not pronounce it, as in (sehen) /ˈzeːən/. There it only shows that the vowel is long.

## Tips for English

You already know the sound in the word hat. The main mistake is trying to pronounce it after a vowel. Do not make a breathing sound inside words like (fahren) /ˈfaːʁən/. Just stretch the vowel before it.
articles.summary: The letter name is Ha, as in the word Haus.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter (I) /iː/ is called (I) /iː/. Its most common sound is the sound /ɪ/, heard in the word (Insel) /ˈɪnzl̩/, which means island. This letter makes three different sounds in German speech.

## How to say it

For the first sound, open your mouth slightly and keep your tongue high. For the second sound, spread your lips wide and push your tongue higher forward. For the third sound, raise the middle of your tongue close to your roof. You can feel your vocal cords vibrate through every sound.

## Reading this letter

In closed syllables before two or more consonants, it sounds like the sound /ɪ/ in (bitte) /ˈbɪtə/. In open stressed syllables, it makes the long sound /iː/ in (Tiger) /ˈtiːɡɐ/. Before another vowel in borrowed words, it sounds like the sound /j/ in (Nation) /naˈtsi̯oːn/.

## Tips for English speakers

Do not turn the long vowel into a glide like the sound in see. Keep your tongue steady and your lips tense until the sound finishes. Do not drop the short vowel into a relaxed sound like the vowel in bit. Keep your tongue slightly higher and tighter.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## Letter Jot

The letter (Jot) /jɔt/ sounds mainly like the sound /j/. You hear it in the word (Jahr) /jaːɐ̯/, which means year. This letter has three different sounds in German.

## How to say it

For the first sound, raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof. Let air flow smoothly while your vocal cords vibrate. For the next sound, push your lips forward slightly. Bring your tongue near the upper gums and voice a smooth buzz. For the last sound, press your tongue behind your upper teeth, then release into that buzz. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration.

## Spelling rules

In native German words, the letter makes the sound /j/, as in (jung) /jʊŋ/. In words borrowed from French, it makes the sound /ʒ/, as in (Journalist) /ʒʊʁnaˈlɪst/. In loanwords from English, it makes the sound /dʒ/, as in (Job) /dʒɔp/.

## Common mistakes

Do not read native words with the English sound in jump. Say the sound as in yes instead. Keep your tongue relaxed and do not press it hard against the roof.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter Ka

The name of the letter is (Ka) /kaː/. It usually sounds like the sound /kʰ/, that is a k with a puff of air, as in (Kind) /kɪnt/, which means child. This letter has two sounds.

## Mouth movements

Press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release it with a sharp burst of breath, without using your vocal cords. For the second sound, release your tongue in the same place without that extra puff of air. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel the breath.

## Spelling patterns

Before a stressed vowel, you produce the sound /kʰ/, that is a k with a burst of breath, as in (Katze) /ˈkʰat͡sə/. In unstressed syllables or after s, you use the sound /k/, that is a k without breath, as in (Skelett) /skeˈlɛt/. At the end of a word, it also stays plain, as in (Fabrik) /faˈbʁiːk/.

## Common mistakes

You might forget the strong puff of air at the start of words. Do not pronounce it weakly like the soft sound in skip. Say it sharply with strong breath, just like the first sound in kite.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is (El) /ɛl/. Its main sound is the sound /l/ in the word (Lampe) /ˈlampə/, which means lamp. This letter makes only one sound in German.

## Making the sound

Press the tip of your tongue firmly against your upper gum ridge. Keep the back of your tongue low and flat. Let the air flow smoothly around the sides of your tongue. Your vocal cords vibrate. Put a hand on your throat to feel the gentle buzz.

## Reading the letter

This letter always makes the sound /l/ in German. You hear this sound at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end of words. Double letters also make this exact same sound, as in the word (Ball) /bal/.

## Common mistakes

At the end of an English word like ball, you raise the back of your tongue. In German, never raise the back of your tongue. Always keep your tongue flat and clear, exactly like the first sound in light.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter Em

You call this letter (Em) /ɛm/. Its sound is the sound /m/, as in the word (Mutter) /ˈmʊtɐ/, which means mother. This letter makes only one sound in German.

## How to say the sound

Press your lips gently together and breathe out through your nose. Turn on your voice so your vocal cords buzz. You can put your fingers on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Spelling and variants

This letter always makes the sound /m/. You hear it at the start, middle, or end of a word. A single letter or a double letter makes this exact sound, as in (Sommer) /ˈzɔmɐ/.

## Mistakes to avoid

This sound is identical to the sound in the English word man. There is no special trap or pitfall to avoid.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## The letter En

The German letter (En) /ɛn/ makes the main sound /n/, that is a standard n sound. You hear this sound in (Name) /ˈnaːmə/, which means name. This letter has three different sounds across German words.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your top teeth. Let the air flow through your nose with your voice turned on. For the second sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. For the third sound, keep the tongue tip on the ridge while the sound forms a whole beat. Feel the vibration in your nose with your fingers.

## Reading the variants

In most regular positions, this letter sounds like the standard sound /n/, that is a standard n sound, as in (nein) /naɪ̯n/ or (Sonne) /ˈzɔnə/. Before the sounds /k/ or /ɡ/, it sounds like /ŋ/, as in (danke) /ˈdaŋkə/. In unstressed word endings, it forms its own small beat as /n̩/, that is a syllabic n sound, as in (leben) /ˈleːbn̩/.

## Avoiding mistakes

You might insert an extra vowel sound before the final nasal ending. Do not say a vowel like the one in the English word fun before the last consonant. Keep your tongue pressed firmly against the ridge behind your teeth without opening your mouth again.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (O) /oː/ has two sounds. Its main sound is heard in (Obst) /oːpst/, which means fruit.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, pull your tongue back. Make a tight circle with your lips. Hold the sound steady and let your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, open your mouth wider and form a looser circle. Put a hand on your neck to feel the steady buzz.

## Spelling rules

The letter makes the long sound /oː/ in open syllables, like in (Sohn) /zoːn/. It makes the short open sound /ɔ/ in closed syllables, like in (offen) /ˈɔfn̩/.

## Common mistakes

You might glide the long vowel like the vowel sound in boat. Keep your lips in one circle without moving them at the end. For the short sound, do not spread your lips flat like in cot. Form an open circle with your lips instead.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## The letter Pe

The German name of this letter is (Pe) /peː/. Its main sound is heard in (Papa) /ˈpaːpa/, which means dad. This letter produces two sounds in German spoken words.

## Pronouncing Pe

Press your lips tightly together and block the air. Then release the air with a clear puff. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. For the other sound, press your lips together and pop them open without that puff of air. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel the breath.

## Spelling rules for Pe

At the start of a word, it makes the sound /pʰ/, that is an aspirated p. You hear this sound in (Post) /pʰɔst/. After the sound /s/ or in unstressed syllables, it makes the sound /p/, that is an unaspirated p. You hear this variant in (Sport) /ʃpɔʁt/.

## Common mistakes with Pe

Do not voice this letter like a b sound in boy. Keep your vocal cords completely still. At the start of words, remember to add a strong puff of air, just like in pet. In clusters after s, drop that puff of air, exactly as in spin.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## Sound of letter Qu

The name of this letter sounds like (Qu) /kuː/. Its main sound is heard in (Quelle) /ˈkvɛlə/, which means source or spring. This letter makes two sounds in German.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air sharply, then touch your lower lip to your upper teeth and turn your voice on. For the second sound, make only the crisp release of air without moving to the lip. Put your hand on your throat to feel it vibrate only during the voiced part.

## Spelling patterns

In native German words, you see this letter before the letter u, where it makes the sound /kv/ as in (Bequem) /bəˈkveːm/. In French loanwords, it makes the sound /k/ as in (Quiche) /kiːʃ/.

## Common learner errors

You might want to pronounce it like quick in English with both lips forming a circle. Do not use that sound. Use your upper front teeth and your lower lip instead, like the first sound in very.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## The letter Er

The letter (Er) /ɛʁ/ has two sounds. Its main sound is the consonant in (Rot) /ʁoːt/, which means red. You also hear it as a soft vowel at the end of syllables.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, pull the back of your tongue toward your throat. Push air through the small gap to make a gentle friction. Your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, relax your tongue and open your mouth slightly. Make a short, low vowel sound. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the vibration.

## Reading the letter

At the start of a word or between vowels, make the sound /ʁ/. You hear this in (hören) /ˈhøːʁən/. At the end of a syllable or after a long vowel, use the soft vowel sound /ɐ/. You hear this in (Uhr) /uːɐ̯/ and in (Vater) /ˈfaːtɐ/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not curl your tongue tip back like in the English word red. Keep your tongue tip resting down behind your lower front teeth instead. For the vowel sound at the end, do not make the hard ending of water. Keep your mouth relaxed and make a short, open sound.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## The letter Es

The letter (Es) /ɛs/ makes three different sounds. Its main sound is the sound /z/, heard in the word (Sonne) /ˈzɔnə/, which means sun.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth. Push air through and turn your voice on. For the next sound, keep the exact same tongue position, but switch your voice off. Feel your throat with your hand to check the buzz. For the third sound, push your lips forward and blow gently without voice.

## Reading the letter

Before a vowel at the start of a syllable, the letter makes the sound /z/, like in (Rose) /ˈʁoːzə/. At the end of a syllable or before a voiceless consonant, it sounds like the sound /s/, like in (Haus) /haʊ̯s/ or (Maske) /ˈmaskə/. Before the consonants p or t at the start of a syllable, it makes the sound /ʃ/, like in (Sport) /ʃpɔʁt/ or (Stadt) /ʃtat/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the letter at the start of words like the hissing sound in see. Use a voiced buzz like in zoo instead. When this letter stands before p or t at the beginning of words, remember to make the quiet sound in shoe.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Sound of letter Te

The name of this letter is (Te) /teː/. Its main sound is heard in (Tisch) /tɪʃ/, which means table. This letter makes two sounds.

## How to say it

Press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Release it sharply with a small puff of air without using your voice. For the second sound, release your tongue cleanly with no breath. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel the breath.

## Spelling rules

Before a stressed vowel, you say the sound /tʰ/, that is a breathed t, as in (Tag) /tʰaːk/. After an s sound, in unstressed spots, or in consonant clusters, you say the sound /t/, that is an unbreathed t. You hear this in (Stein) /ʃtaɪ̯n/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn this letter into an English flap between vowels as in water. Keep the release crisp and firm every time.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter U

The letter (U) /uː/ is called /uː/. Its main sound is heard in the word (Uhr) /uːɐ̯/, which means clock or watch. This letter makes two different sounds in German. Both sounds are simple vowels.

## How to say the letter U

For the long sound, pull your tongue back. Push your lips forward into a small, tight circle. Let your voice hum steadily. For the short sound, open your mouth a little wider. Relax your lips slightly. Keep your tongue pulled back. Put a finger before your lips to feel them push forward.

## Spelling rules for the letter U

Before a single consonant, you make a long sound. You can hear this in (gut) /ɡuːt/. Before two consonants, you make a short sound. You can hear this in (und) /ʊnt/.

## Mistakes to avoid with U

Do not let your lips glide into a w sound at the end. In the English word boot, your lips often move. Keep your lips completely still until the sound finishes. Also, do not start with a y sound like in the English word music.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## The letter Vau

The name of this letter is spoken as (Vau) /faʊ/. Its main sound is heard in the word (Vater) /ˈfaːtɐ/, which means father. This letter can make two different sounds in German words.

## Mouth shape and air

Place your top teeth lightly on your lower lip. Blow air through the narrow gap without any voice. For the other sound, keep the exact same position, but turn your voice on. Rest a hand on your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Reading the letter

In native German words and at the end of words, this letter makes the sound /f/. You hear this in the word (Vogel) /ˈfoːɡl̩/. In borrowed words from other languages, it makes the sound /v/. You hear this in the word (Vase) /ˈvaːzə/.

## Avoiding common mistakes

Do not read this letter as the sound in very when it begins native words. Think of the starting sound in the English word father. If you use your voice by mistake, blow plain air instead.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## The letter We

The letter (We) /veː/ is named with a long vowel. It makes the sound /v/ as in (Wasser) /ˈvasɐ/, which means water. This letter makes one single sound in German words. You will hear it clearly in many common words.

## How to say We

To make this sound, rest your upper front teeth lightly against your lower lip. Blow air gently through the small gap between them. Turn on your voice box so that you make a clear buzzing sound. Touch your throat with two fingers to feel the steady vibration.

## Spelling of We

This letter stands for the sound /v/ in almost every regular German word. It appears at the beginning of words and inside them. An example is the word (zwei) /tsvaɪ̯/. The spelling always gives this exact voiced sound.

## Common mistakes with We

Do not pronounce this letter like the first sound in the English word water. Your lips must never form a small round circle. Use the sound of the letter in the English word vine instead. Keep your upper teeth firmly against your lower lip.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## Sound of Ix

The letter (Ix) /ɪks/ makes the sound /ks/ in the word (Xylophon) /ksyloˈfoːn/, which means xylophone. This letter has two different sounds in spoken German.

## Pronouncing the letter

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to block the air. Release it sharply without voice, then hiss air through your front teeth. For the second sound, make that same back click with your voice on. Then push air through your teeth while vibrating your vocal cords. Place two fingers on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Reading rules

In almost all native German words and Greek loanwords, read this letter as the sound /ks/. You hear this in the word (Hexe) /ˈhɛksə/. In a few words borrowed from French or English, pronounce the voiced sound /gz/. You hear this pattern in the word (Examen) /ɛkˈzaːmən/.

## Common mistakes

At the start of words, do not turn this letter into a simple z sound. English words like xylophone use a z sound, but German keeps both parts sharp and clear. Say a crisp k sound first, then slide into the s sound.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## The letter Ypsilon

The German letter (Ypsilon) /ʏpsilɔn/ mostly makes the sound /j/, as in (Yoga) /ˈjoːɡa/, which means yoga. This letter makes four sounds in total.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, push your tongue high and forward while pursing your lips into a tight circle. For the second sound, relax your tongue slightly and keep your lips in a loose circle. For the third sound, raise your tongue near your roof and let air glide smoothly past. For the fourth sound, spread your lips wide and raise your tongue high. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz for each one.

## Reading the letter

In stressed open parts of Greek loanwords, it makes the sound /yː/, that is a long tight ue sound, as in (Typ) /tyːp/. In closed parts of Greek loanwords, it makes the sound /ʏ/, that is a short loose ue sound, as in (System) /zʏsˈteːm/. Before vowels in modern loanwords, it makes the sound /j/, as in (Yacht) /jaxt/. At the end of words or unstressed syllables, it makes the sound /i/, as in (Handy) /ˈhɛndi/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce Greek words with the flat vowel in bit or the glide in use. Purse your lips firmly into a circle while saying see. Do not change your lip shape while the vowel rings out.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (Zet) /tsɛt/ makes the sound /ts/ in the word (Zug) /tsuːk/, which means train. It has two sounds in German, but one sound is far more common. In borrowed words it sounds different. Listen carefully to how native speakers pronounce it in everyday speech.

## How to say it

To make the sound /ts/, press your tongue tip behind your upper teeth. Stop the breath, then release it into a sharp hiss. Do not use your voice. For the sound /z/, bring your teeth close together and blow air gently. Keep your vocal cords buzzing. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration on that second sound.

## Where each sound appears

In almost all German words, the letter sounds like /ts/. You hear this in the word (Zimmer) /ˈtsɪmɐ/. In recent loanwords borrowed from English, it keeps the original English sound /z/. You can hear this second pronunciation in the word (Zoom) /zuːm/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not pronounce this letter like the English letter z in zoo when reading German words. That soft buzzing sound is wrong for regular German vocabulary. Start with a firm t sound and slide instantly into an s sound. Think of the ending of the English word cats. Make the burst crisp and sudden.

articles.title: Ä
articles.body:
## The letter Ä

The letter (Ä) /ɛː/ is called (Ä) /ɛː/. Its main sound is heard in the word (Äpfel) /ˈɛpfəl/, which means apples. This letter makes two sounds.

## How to say Ä

For the first sound, drop your jaw slightly and spread your lips. Keep your tongue relaxed and low in the mouth. For the second sound, open your mouth wider and hold the vowel longer. Place your hand on your throat to feel continuous voice.

## Spelling of Ä

In a short, closed stressed syllable, it makes the sound /ɛ/, that is a short open vowel, as in (Hände) /ˈhɛndə/. In a long syllable with a single consonant, it makes the sound /ɛː/, that is a long open vowel, as in (Käse) /ˈkɛːzə/.

## Common mistakes with Ä

Do not turn the long sound into the vowel of day. Keep your tongue perfectly still without gliding into another sound. Do not replace the short sound with the vowel in cat.

articles.title: Ö
articles.body:
## The letter Ö

The letter (Ö) /øː/ is called /øː/, that is a long closed vowel. Its main sound is the long vowel /øː/, that is a long closed vowel, as in (Öl) /ʔøːl/, which means oil. This letter makes two different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, say the sound in see. Keep your tongue high and forward, then round your lips tightly. To make the second sound, say the sound in bed. Keep your tongue in that spot, then round your lips into an open circle. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz on both sounds.

## Spelling rules

This letter makes its long sound in open syllables or before a single consonant. An example is the word (schön) /ʃøːn/. It makes its short sound in closed syllables, especially before two consonants. An example is the word (öffnen) /ˈʔœfnən/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace these sounds with the vowel in bird or burn. Do not flatten your lips or glide into an r sound. Shape your lips into a tight circle first, and keep them still until the sound ends.

articles.title: Ü
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter (Ü) /yː/ is called (Ü) /yː/, that is a long close front vowel with circle lips. Its main sound is heard in the word (Übung) /ˈyːbʊŋ/, which means exercise, practice. This German letter makes two different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, place your tongue high and forward as for see. Push your lips tightly forward into a small circle, then hold the sound steady. For the second sound, pull your tongue slightly back and lower your jaw a little bit. Form a looser circle with your lips. Put a finger before your lips to check the push.

## When to use each sound

You make the sound /yː/, that is a long close front vowel with circle lips, in open or stressed syllables. The word (Tür) /tyːɐ̯/ shows this sound. You make the sound /ʏ/, that is a short close front vowel with circle lips, before double consonants or consonant clusters. The word (fünf) /fʏnf/ shows this second sound.

## Common mistakes to avoid

Do not replace the sound with the vowel of goose. For that English word your tongue pulls back, but German needs your tongue forward. Do not replace it with the vowel of see. Keep your lips pushed forward into a circle instead of spreading them wide.

articles.title: ß
articles.body:
## The letter Eszett

The German letter (Eszett) /ɛsˈtsɛt/ makes a sharp hissing sound. You hear it clearly in the word (Straße) /ˈʃtʁaːsə/, which means street. This letter always makes only one sound in standard German.

## Mouth shape

Bring your teeth close together and spread your lips slightly. Put your tongue tip near the bump behind your top teeth. Push air through the narrow gap. Do not use your voice. You can feel cool air on your hand in front of your lips.

## Spelling rules

This letter always stands for the sound /s/. It appears only after long vowels, as in (groß) /ɡʁoːs/. It also appears after two vowels said together, as in (fleißig) /ˈflaɪ̯sɪç/. It never stands at the start of a word.

## Common mistakes

Do not buzz this sound like the letter in zoo. Keep your vocal cords completely still. It sounds just like the double letter in grass. It also looks like a capital letter B, but you never pronounce it like bad.

articles.title: А
articles.body:
## The letter a

The letter (а) /a/ has the name (а) /a/. Its main sound is heard in the word (арбуз) /ɐrˈbus/, which means watermelon. This letter makes three different sounds.

## Pronouncing the letter

For the first sound, open your mouth wide. Keep your tongue low and flat, with your lips relaxed. For the next sound, close your jaw slightly and keep your tongue relaxed. For the last sound, keep your mouth barely open and your tongue centered. Place your hand on your throat to feel your voice box vibrate.

## Reading rules

When the vowel carries the stress, pronounce the sound /a/, as in the word (брат) /brat/. In the syllable right before the stress, pronounce the sound /ɐ/, that is a clearer short uh sound, as in (вода) /vɐˈda/. In all other unstressed positions, pronounce the sound /ə/, that is a weak muffled uh sound, as in (карандаш) /kərɐnˈdaʂ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not make the stressed vowel glide like the vowel sound in father. Keep the sound steady from start to finish. When the vowel has no stress, do not say a wide open vowel sound. Let your mouth relax completely instead.

articles.title: Б
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is (бэ) /bɛ/. Its main sound is heard in (брат) /brat/, which means brother. This letter makes four different sounds in speech.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, press your lips tight and voice the burst. For the second sound, arch your tongue high toward the roof while releasing voiced lips. For the third sound, close your lips and blow out air with no voice. For the fourth sound, arch your tongue forward while popping air out silently. Touch your throat to feel when your vocal cords buzz.

## Reading this letter

This letter sounds like the sound /b/, that is a hard b, in (бык) /bɨk/. Before softening vowels or a soft sign, it sounds like the sound /bʲ/, that is a soft b, in (белый) /ˈbʲe.ɫɨj/. At the end of a word, it sounds like the sound /p/, that is a hard p, in (лоб) /lop/. Before a soft sign at word end, it gives the sound /pʲ/, that is a soft p, in (дробь) /dropʲ/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not puff out a heavy breath when you speak the voiceless sounds. Keep your lips tighter than in the English word bat. For the softened sounds, raise the middle of your tongue at the same moment.

articles.title: В
articles.body:
## The letter ve

The letter (вэ) /vɛ/ mainly makes the sound /v/, that is a hard v sound. You hear this sound in the word (вода) /vɐˈda/, which means water. Overall, this letter makes four different sounds in Russian.

## How to say it

Touch your upper front teeth lightly with your lower lip and vibrate your vocal cords. For the softer version, raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. For the next sound, keep the same mouth shape but turn your voice off completely. For the final sound, keep your voice off while raising your tongue toward the roof. Put your hand on your throat to feel when your voice turns on and off.

## Spelling rules

Before hard vowels and voiced consonants, it makes the sound /v/, that is a hard v sound, as in (волк) /volk/. Before soft vowels or a soft sign, it makes the sound /vʲ/, that is a soft v sound, as in (ветер) /ˈvʲetʲɪr/. At the end of a word or before voiceless consonants, it makes the sound /f/, that is a hard f sound, as in (вход) /fxot/. At the end of a word before a soft sign, it makes the sound /fʲ/, that is a soft f sound, as in (кровь) /krofʲ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the sound into a w sound, like the first sound in water. Always touch your lower lip against your upper teeth. For the soft sounds, do not add a separate y sound like in view. Keep the lip contact and tongue lift together in one smooth sound.

articles.title: Г
articles.body:
## The letter гэ

The letter (гэ) /ɡɛ/ usually sounds like the sound /ɡ/, that is a hard g. You hear it in the word (город) /ˈɡorət/, which means city or town. This letter can make four different sounds.

## How to say it

Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly with voice. For the soft sound, arch the middle of your tongue upward as you release the burst. For the third sound, keep the same mouth shape, but do not use your voice. For the last sound, press your top teeth against your lower lip and blow voice through.

## Reading this letter

Before hard vowels and voiced consonants, it makes the sound /ɡ/, that is a hard g, as in (глаз) /ɡlas/. Before soft vowels or a soft sign, it makes the sound /ɡʲ/, that is a soft g, as in (где) /ɡʲdʲe/ and (гитара) /ɡʲɪˈtarə/. At the end of a word or before voiceless consonants, it sounds like the sound /k/, as in (друг) /druk/ and (когти) /ˈkoktʲɪ/. In adjective and pronoun endings, it makes the sound /v/, as in (его) /jɪˈvo/ and (белого) /ˈbʲɛləvə/.

## Tips for English speakers

Do not puff a breath of air when making the sound /k/ at the word end. English words like back have a puff. Stop the breath firmly. Do not replace the soft sound with a separate sound like the y in yet. Raise your tongue while releasing the burst.

articles.title: Д
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The Russian letter (дэ) /dɛ/ sounds like the sound /d/, that is a hard d. You hear it in the word (дом) /dom/, which means house. The letter makes four different sounds in Russian.

## Pronunciation

Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your upper teeth. Drop your tongue quickly as air breaks out, vibrating your vocal cords. For the second sound, press the flat top of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. The third sound moves like the first, but without your voice. The fourth sound moves like the second, but without your voice. Feel your throat vibrate for the first two sounds.

## Spelling rules

The letter sounds like the sound /d/, that is a hard d, before hard vowels. It makes this sound in the word (два) /dva/. Before soft vowels or a soft sign, it makes the sound /dʲ/, that is a soft d. You hear this sound in the word (день) /dʲenʲ/. At the end of a word, it sounds like the sound /t/, that is a hard t. This happens in the word (сад) /sat/. When softened at the end, it makes the sound /tʲ/, that is a soft t. You hear this in the word (медь) /mʲetʲ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not place your tongue behind your teeth as you do in the English word door. Touch your upper teeth directly. Do not puff out air like you do in the English word time. Keep the air release sharp and clean.

articles.title: Е
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (е) /je/ makes the main sound in (ель) /jelʲ/, which means spruce. This letter has four sounds in total.

## How to say it

For the first sound, glide your tongue from the roof down and unround your lips. For the second sound, spread your lips and keep your tongue high. For the third sound, start with a quick glide and relax your tongue. For the fourth sound, lift your tongue close to the roof. Feel your vocal cords vibrate on your throat for all four sounds.

## Reading rules

Stressed after a vowel, it sounds like the sound /je/ in (поезд) /ˈpo.jist/. Stressed after a consonant, it makes the sound /e/ in (лес) /lʲes/. Unstressed at the beginning of a word, it gives the sound /jɪ/ in (еда) /jɪˈda/. Unstressed after a consonant, it makes the sound /ɪ/ in (весна) /vʲɪsˈna/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the sound into the long sound in English day. Keep your tongue steady and do not slide into another vowel. When it follows a consonant, do not insert a separate y sound like in yes. Instead, soften the consonant itself before the vowel.

articles.title: Ё
articles.body:
## Sound of yo

The letter (ё) /jo/ is named (ё) /jo/. Its main sound appears in the word (ёлка) /ˈjɵlkə/, which means fir tree, Christmas tree. This letter can make three sounds depending on where it appears. It is always stressed in standard Russian words.

## How to say yo

To make the first sound, lift your tongue high like a y sound. Then move your tongue forward and round your lips tightly. For the second sound, keep your tongue forward and round your lips into a tight circle. For the third sound, pull your tongue back and make your lips round. Place a hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz throughout all three sounds.

## Spelling of yo

At the start of a word or after another vowel, you say the sound /jɵ/, as in (ёж) /jɵʂ/. After most consonants, the letter softens that consonant and sounds like the sound /ɵ/, as in (мёд) /mʲɵt/. After hard hissing consonants, it sounds like the sound /o/, as in (жёлтый) /ˈʐoltɨj/.

## Comparing yo to English

Do not turn this vowel into the glide in the English word boat. Keep your lips held in one fixed circle without sliding toward a w sound. Do not drop the soft sound of the consonant before it. Press the flat middle of your tongue against the roof of your mouth before you shape the vowel.

articles.title: Ж
articles.body:
## Sound of zhe

Russian speakers call this letter (жэ) /ʒɛ/. It usually sounds like the sound /ʐ/, as in the word (жук) /ʐuk/, which means beetle. This letter makes two different sounds.

## How to say it

Curl your tongue tip slightly back behind your top teeth. Push air through the narrow gap with your voice turned on. For the unvoiced sound, make the exact same mouth shape, but whisper without using your voice. Place your hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration stop.

## Reading rules

This letter usually sounds like the voiced sound /ʐ/. You hear it before vowels and voiced consonants, like in (жар) /ʐar/. It changes into the unvoiced sound /ʂ/ at the end of a word, as in (муж) /muʂ/. It also makes the unvoiced sound /ʂ/ before voiceless consonants, as in (ложка) /ˈloʂkə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not make the soft sound in the English word measure. That sound keeps your tongue flat. Pull your tongue tip further back and curl it slightly up. Do not soften the unvoiced sound like the start of ship. Keep your tongue firm and drawn back.

articles.title: З
articles.body:
## Sound of letter ze

The name of this letter is (зэ) /zɛ/. Its main sound appears in the word (зима) /zʲɪˈma/, which means winter. This letter can make four different sounds in Russian speech.

## How to say ze

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth and hum. For the soft partner, raise the middle of your tongue while you hum. For the third sound, whisper that same air without humming. For the soft whisper, raise your tongue middle without your voice. Put your hand on your throat to feel the humming stop.

## Spelling rules for ze

Before hard vowels and voiced consonants, it makes the sound /z/, that is a hard z, as in (зуб) /zup/. Before soft vowels and the soft sign, you hear the sound /zʲ/, that is a soft z, as in (зелень) /ˈzʲe.lʲɪnʲ/. At the end of a word, it becomes the sound /s/, that is a hard s, as in (глаз) /ɡlas/. When softened at the end of a word, it makes the sound /sʲ/, that is a soft s, as in (мазь) /masʲ/.

## Common mistakes with ze

Do not voice the final sound like the buzzing in buzz. Russian changes the end sound into a crisp hiss, like the finish of bus. Do not forget to raise your tongue for the soft sounds. Keep the middle of your tongue high to avoid sounding too plain.

articles.title: И
articles.body:
## The letter ee

The name of this letter is (и) /i/. Its main sound is heard in the word (игра) /ɪˈɡra/, which means game or play. This letter produces three different sounds in Russian.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, push your tongue high and forward toward the roof of your mouth. Spread your lips wide and vibrate your vocal cords. For the second sound, relax your tongue slightly lower. For the third sound, pull your tongue further back into the middle of your mouth. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration.

## Reading the variants

Under stress, it makes the sound /i/, as in (мир) /mʲir/. Without stress, it makes the sound /ɪ/, that is a softer short ih sound, as in (зима) /zʲɪˈma/. After certain hard consonants, it makes the sound /ɨ/, that is a deeper ih sound from the back of the mouth, as in (жить) /ʐɨtʲ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace the third sound with the vowel in the English word sit. The English sound is made near the front of your mouth. To fix this, pull your tongue back toward your throat and keep your lips flat.

articles.title: Й
articles.body:
## The letter ee kratkoye

The letter (и краткое) /i ˈkratkəjə/ sounds like the sound /j/. You hear it in the Russian word (йогурт) /ˈjoɡʊrt/, which means yogurt. This letter makes only one sound.

## How to say it

Raise the middle of your tongue high toward the roof of your mouth. Keep the tip down behind your lower front teeth. Spread your lips slightly. Push air through and vibrate your vocal cords. Touch your neck to feel the buzzing vibration.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /j/. It appears after vowels and before consonants or at word ends, as in (май) /maj/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not turn this letter into a long vowel like the sound in see. Keep it very quick and glide immediately away, just like the first sound in yes.

articles.title: К
articles.body:
## Letter ka sound

The letter (ка) /ka/ makes its main sound in the word (кот) /kot/, which means cat. This letter produces three sounds in speech.

## How to say ka

Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly without any voice. For the softer version, raise the middle of your tongue at the same time. For the voiced sound, keep the same mouth position but vibrate your vocal cords. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Reading the letter ka

Before consonants or hard vowels, pronounce the sound /k/, that is a hard k, as in (как) /kak/. This sound also appears at the end of words. Before soft vowels or a soft sign, pronounce the sound /kʲ/, that is a soft k, as in (кит) /kʲit/. Before certain voiced consonants, say the sound /ɡ/ as in (вокзал) /vaɡˈzal/.

## Mistakes to avoid with ka

You might release a puff of breath as in the English word kite. Keep the air burst much tighter. Do not add a separate y sound when saying the softer sound as in the English word cue. Raise the middle of your tongue smoothly instead.

articles.title: Л
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter is called (эль) /ɛlʲ/. Its main sound is the sound /ɫ/, that is a hard l, as in the word (лампа) /ˈɫam.pə/, which means lamp. This letter makes two sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, touch your upper teeth with the tip of your tongue. Pull the back of your tongue upward and let your voice vibrate. For the second sound, press the flat blade of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Keep the tip low behind your bottom teeth. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration of your vocal cords.

## When to use each

This letter makes the sound /ɫ/, that is a hard l, before hard vowels, before consonants, or at the end of a word. You can hear it in (стол) /stoɫ/. It makes the sound /lʲ/, that is a soft l, before soft vowels or the soft sign. You can hear it in (лето) /ˈlʲe.tə/ and in (соль) /solʲ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace the hard sound with the light l in light. Keep the back of your tongue raised to make it dark and heavy, like the ending of ball. Do not pronounce the soft sound like the l in leaf. Flatten your tongue against the roof of your mouth, as if you are saying million.

articles.title: М
articles.body:
## The letter эм

The letter (эм) /ɛm/ makes the sound /m/, that is hard m, in (мама) /ˈma.mə/, which means mom. This letter has two sounds in Russian.

## How to say эм

Close both lips firmly and let your voice hum through your nose. Keep your tongue flat for the hard sound. To make the soft sound, arch the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Place a finger on your throat to feel the buzzing voice.

## Reading the letter эм

You make the sound /m/, that is hard m, before hard vowels, consonants, or at the end of a word. A clear example is (дом) /dom/. You make the sound /mʲ/, that is soft m, before soft vowels or the soft sign. An example is (мир) /mʲir/, and another is (семь) /sʲemʲ/.

## Mistakes to avoid
