Do not forget to soften the sound before soft vowels. English has the hard sound in mom, but lacks the soft sound. Prepare to smile and raise your tongue before your lips part.

articles.title: Н
articles.body:
## Letter sound en

The name of this letter is (эн) /ɛn/. Its main sound is heard in the word (нос) /nos/, meaning nose. This letter makes two sounds.

## How to say en

For the first sound, press your tongue tip firmly against your upper teeth. Let air flow out through your nose with voice. For the second sound, press the middle of your tongue flat against the roof. Keep the tip low behind your bottom teeth. Touch your neck to feel your vocal cords buzz.

## Spelling rules en

You make the hard sound /n/, that is a plain n, before hard vowels and consonants. It also sounds this way at the end of a word, as in (сон) /son/. You make the soft sound /nʲ/, that is a softened n, before soft vowels and the soft sign. You can hear this soft sound in the word (нет) /nʲet/ and the word (день) /dʲenʲ/.

## Common mistakes en

Do not pull your tongue back to the ridge behind your teeth like in no. Instead, touch your upper teeth directly. Do not insert a separate y sound when softening the consonant like in canyon. Instead, keep the sound smooth by pressing the tongue flat as you speak.

articles.title: О
articles.body:
## Sound of letter o

The name of this letter is (о) /o/. Its main sound appears in (окно) /ɐkˈno/, which means window. The letter makes three distinct sounds in Russian.

## How to say it

For the first sound, pull your tongue back and round your lips into an open circle. For the second sound, relax your lips and open your mouth slightly wider. For the third sound, keep your mouth almost closed and leave your tongue relaxed in the middle. Place a hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz continuously.

## Spelling rules

When the accent falls on this letter, pronounce the sound /o/, as in (дом) /dom/. In the syllable right before the accent, it becomes the sound /ɐ/, that is a clearer short ah, heard in (вода) /vɐˈda/. In other unaccented positions, it weakens to the sound /ə/, that is a muffled neutral sound, heard in (молоко) /məlɐˈko/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not turn the accented vowel into a double vowel like the one in boat. Keep your lips firmly in one place until the vowel ends. Also, do not pronounce every unaccented position as a clear vowel from law. Let your mouth relax completely when the accent falls elsewhere.

articles.title: П
articles.body:
## The letter pe

The name of this letter sounds like (пэ) /pɛ/. Its main sound appears in (папа) /ˈpa.pə/, which means dad. The letter makes three different sounds.

## How to say pe

To say the plain sound, press your lips firmly together. Release them without letting out a puff of air. Keep your vocal cords still. To make the soft sound, arch your tongue high toward the roof of your mouth while closing your lips. Release the lips cleanly. To make the voiced sound, close your lips and vibrate your vocal cords. Touch your throat to feel that vibration.

## Spelling rules for pe

Before consonants, at word ends, and before hard vowels, the letter makes the sound /p/, that is a plain voiceless sound, as in (суп) /sup/. Before soft vowels and the soft sign, it makes the sound /pʲ/, that is a softened voiceless sound, as in (песня) /ˈpʲe.sʲnʲə/. Before voiced consonants, it changes to the sound /b/, as in (сбербанк) /zbʲɪrˈbank/.

## Common mistakes with pe

Do not puff out air like in the English word pet. Stop the breath burst completely. When making the soft sound, do not add an extra consonant sound like the first sound in yes. Simply keep the middle of your tongue high against the roof of your mouth as your lips part.

articles.title: Р
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (эр) /ɛr/ makes the rolled sound /r/, that is a hard rolled r. You hear it in (рука) /rʊˈka/, which means hand or arm. This letter has two different sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, let the tip of your tongue vibrate against the roof of your mouth. Send out strong air and let your vocal cords buzz. For the second sound, raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth while rolling the tip. Touch your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Reading the letter

You say the hard sound /r/, that is a hard rolled r, before hard vowels or at the end of a word. You hear it in (рыба) /ˈrɨbə/ and (брат) /brat/. You say the soft sound /rʲ/, that is a soft rolled r, before softening letters. You hear it in (река) /rʲɪˈka/ and (дверь) /dvʲerʲ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not make the smooth sound of the English word red. Keep your tongue tip forward and roll it sharply. Do not drop the roll at the end of a word like door. Keep the vibration clear every time.

articles.title: С
articles.body:
## Sound of es

The letter (эс) /ɛs/ makes four different sounds in Russian words. Its primary sound is heard in the word (солнце) /ˈsont͡sə/, which means sun.

## How to say es

Put your tongue tip behind your lower teeth. Blow air through the narrow gap without voice for the hard hiss. For the soft hiss, raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof. Keep your vocal cords vibrating for the two voiced versions. Place a hand on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Reading the letter es

Before hard vowels or at the end of a word, it sounds as /s/, that is a plain s, like in (сом) /som/. Before soft vowels or a soft sign, it sounds as /sʲ/, that is a softened s, in (семь) /sʲemʲ/. Before voiced consonants, it turns into /z/, that is a plain z, in (сделать) /ˈzdʲeɫətʲ/. Before voiced soft consonants, it becomes /zʲ/, that is a softened z, in (сбить) /zʲbʲitʲ/.

## Common mistakes with es

You might forget to soften the hissing sound before soft vowels. Do not say the start of simple words like sit. Lift the middle of your tongue high to make a crisp, light hiss. You might also forget to voice the letter before voiced consonants. Let your throat buzz strongly so it does not sound like sea.

articles.title: Т
articles.body:
## The letter te

The name of this letter is (тэ) /tɛ/. Its main sound is the sound /t/, that is a hard t, heard in the word (стол) /stol/, which means table. This letter can make three different sounds.

## How to make the sounds

Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your upper teeth. Release the breath sharply without voicing. For the soft sound, arch the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. For the voiced sound, keep the tongue in the first position and vibrate your vocal cords. Place a hand on your throat to feel the vibration.

## Reading this letter

This letter makes the sound /t/, that is a hard t, at the end of words or before most consonants, as in (там) /tam/. It makes the sound /tʲ/, that is a soft t, before soft vowels or a soft sign, as in (тётя) /ˈtʲɵ.tʲə/ and (мать) /matʲ/. Before voiced consonants, it makes the sound /d/, as in (отдых) /ˈod.dɨx/ and (футбол) /fudˈbol/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not puff air when you say this letter. English words like top release a puff of breath. Keep the release clean and tight. Also place your tongue against your teeth, not further back on the gum ridge.

articles.title: У
articles.body:
## Sound of letter oo

The letter (у) /u/ is named by its sound. It mainly makes the sound /u/, heard in (ухо) /ˈu.xə/, which means ear. This Russian letter makes two different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, pull your tongue back. Round your lips tightly into a small circle. Push your lips forward and let your voice vibrate. For the second sound, keep your mouth slightly wider. Relax your tongue slightly. Put your hand on your neck to feel your voice buzz steadily.

## Spelling rules

You say the sound /u/ when the letter has the stress, as in (утро) /ˈu.trə/. It also sounds like the sound /u/ before the stressed beat, as in (рука) /ruˈka/. In other unstressed positions, it makes the sound /ʊ/, like in (улица) /ˈu.lʲɪ.tsə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not add a w sound at the end, like in English boot. Keep your lips still throughout the entire sound. Also, do not pronounce it like the vowel in book when stressed. Push your lips forward firmly to keep the sound pure.

articles.title: Ф
articles.body:
## Letter ef

The name of this letter sounds like (эф) /ɛf/. Its main sound appears in the word (фонарь) /fɐˈnarʲ/, which means lantern, streetlight. In Russian, this letter represents two distinct sounds.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, place your upper teeth lightly against your lower lip. Blow air steadily through the gap without using your vocal cords. For the second sound, make the same contact and raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Place a hand on your throat to feel that it does not buzz.

## Reading the variants

The letter makes the sound /f/, that is a hard f, before hard vowels, consonants, and word-finally, as in (факт) /fakt/. It makes the sound /fʲ/, that is a soft f, before softening vowels and the soft sign, as in (фильм) /fʲilʲm/ or (кофе) /ˈkofʲe/.

## Common mistakes

You may pronounce the soft sound like the ordinary f in fast. Prepare the y sound with your tongue at the same time to soften it. Do not let your vocal cords vibrate, or you will produce the sound of vine instead of fine.

articles.title: Х
articles.body:
## The Russian letter kha

The letter (ха) /xa/ makes the sound /x/, that is a hard rasping breath, heard in the word (хлеб) /xlʲep/, which means bread. This letter has two different sounds.

## Pronouncing the letter kha

Lift the back of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Blow air steadily through the narrow gap without stopping the airflow. Keep your vocal cords completely still. For the soft version, raise the middle of your tongue closer to the roof as you breathe out. Put a hand on your throat to make sure it does not buzz.

## Reading the letter kha

Before consonants or non front vowels, you say the sound /x/, that is a hard rasping breath, as in (хорошо) /xərəˈʂo/. Before front vowels and the soft sign, you say the sound /xʲ/, that is a soft rasping breath, as in (химия) /ˈxʲimʲɪjə/.

## Avoiding common English errors

Do not replace this sound with the sound in the English word cat. Keep the airflow continuous and never let your tongue touch the roof of your mouth. Do not use the sound in the English word hat. Always make the breath scrape firmly at the back of your mouth.

articles.title: Ц
articles.body:
## Sound of tse

The letter (цэ) /tsɛ/ makes the sound /ts/. You hear this main sound in (цвет) /tsvʲet/, which means colour. This letter can make two sounds.

## How to say tse

Press the tip of your tongue against your upper gum. Release the air through a tiny gap while hissing. Keep your vocal cords completely still. For the voiced sound, keep the same mouth shape, but vibrate your vocal cords. Touch your throat to feel that vibration.

## Reading tse

This letter usually makes the sound /ts/, as in (центр) /tsɛntr/ or (конец) /kɐˈnʲets/. It sounds like /dz/ when it stands directly before a voiced consonant. You hear this voiced sound in the word (плацдарм) /plɐdzˈdarm/.

## Common mistakes

Do not split this into two separate sounds. Say it together as one blend, like the end of the word cats. Keep the sound crisp and hard. Do not soften it by lifting your tongue middle to the roof of your mouth.

articles.title: Ч
articles.body:
## The letter che

The letter (че) /tɕe/ makes the main sound /tɕ/. You hear it in the word (час) /tɕas/, which means hour. This letter has two different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, press your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth. Push air through as you release it softly. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. To make the second sound, keep the air hissing smoothly without the stop. Touch your throat to feel that your voice stays quiet.

## Reading this letter

This letter usually makes the soft sound /tɕ/, as in (чай) /tɕaj/. In a few frequent words before the letter en, it sounds like /ɕː/ instead. You hear this long soft hissing sound in the word (скучно) /ˈskuɕːnə/, and also in (конечно) /kɐˈnʲeɕːnə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce this like the hard sound in the English word chair. Keep the tongue much flatter and softer against the roof of your mouth. Also, avoid using a hard hissing sound in the special words with en. Soften your mouth completely.

articles.title: Ш
articles.body:
## The letter sha

The name of this letter sounds like (ша) /ʃa/. It mainly makes the sound /ʂ/, as heard in the word (школа) /ˈʂko.ɫə/, meaning school. Overall, this single letter makes two distinct sounds in speech.

## How to say it

Curl the tip of your tongue slightly back behind your top teeth. Push air through the small gap without your vocal cords vibrating. For the second sound, keep the same tongue position and vibrate your vocal cords. Touch your throat to feel that vibration.

## Reading rules

In most words, this letter makes the voiceless sound /ʂ/. You hear this sound in (шар) /ʂar/. Before voiced consonants, it changes to the voiced sound /ʐ/. You hear this voiced sound in the phrase (наш дом) /naʐ dom/.

## Common mistakes

Do not make the soft sound heard in ship. Pull your tongue tip further back and keep the sound hard and dry.

articles.title: Щ
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (ща) /ɕːa/ makes the sound /ɕː/. You hear it in the word (щи) /ɕːi/, which means cabbage soup. This letter makes only one sound.

## How to say it

Put the middle of your tongue high against your roof. Place the tip of your tongue behind your lower front teeth. Push a continuous stream of air through this narrow gap. Do not use your voice. Keep your lips slightly spread. Hold the hiss longer than a normal shushing noise. Touch your throat to feel no vibration.

## Reading this letter

The letter always makes the sound /ɕː/ in every position. You can hear this sound clearly at the end of the word (борщ) /borɕː/.

## Common mistakes

Do not say the sound like the start of ship. The sound in ship is deeper and your lips stick out. For this Russian sound, spread your lips and raise your tongue higher. Do not add a hard stop like the start of chip. Keep the airflow smooth, soft and long from start to finish.

articles.title: Ъ
articles.body:
## The hard sign

The letter (твёрдый знак) /ˈtvʲɵrdɨj ˈznak/ has no sound of its own. It acts as a hard separator. You hear this separation in (объект) /ɐbˈjekt/, which means object. Because it makes no sound, this letter has zero sounds to learn. It only changes how you say nearby letters.

## Mouth movements

You make no sound for this silent mark. Your mouth pauses briefly after the consonant before it. Keep the consonant hard by leaving your tongue flat and low. Do not raise your tongue body toward the roof of your mouth. Then quickly start the next vowel with a strong y sound. Place a hand on your throat to feel the brief pause.

## Spelling rules

This letter appears after prefixes ending in a consonant and before certain vowels. It keeps the previous consonant hard and inserts a y sound. In this position, the letter is not pronounced, as in (подъезд) /pɐdˈjest/. Another clear case where it stays completely silent is (съел) /sjel/.

## Common pitfalls

A common mistake is blending the consonant directly into the vowel. In English words like subdue, consonants often soften smoothly. With this letter, keep the consonant plain and insert a clean break before the y sound. Do not drop the separating y sound either.

articles.title: Ы
articles.body:
## The letter sound

The letter name is (ы) /ɨ/, that is a close central vowel. This letter makes the vowel sound in (сын) /sɨn/, which means son. It has two sounds in spoken Russian.

## Making the sound

Pull your tongue back into the middle of your mouth. Keep your lips flat and spread slightly. Vibrate your vocal cords with a tense throat. For the unstressed sound, relax your tongue slightly downwards. Touch your throat to feel the strong steady vibration.

## Reading the variants

In stressed syllables after hard consonants, say the sound /ɨ/, that is a close central vowel, as in (дым) /dɨm/. In unstressed syllables, make the shorter sound /ɨ̞/, that is a lower central vowel, as in (рыбак) /rɨ̞ˈbak/.

## Common mistakes

Do not say the sound in the English word sit. Do not make the sound in the English word see. Pull your tongue farther back in your mouth instead.

articles.title: Ь
articles.body:
## The soft sign

The letter is called (мягкий знак) /ˈmʲaxkʲɪj ˈznak/. It makes no sound by itself. Instead, it changes the consonant before it, as in (день) /dʲenʲ/, which means day. This sign has two jobs in speech.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first effect, raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Keep the tip touching your lower teeth. For the second effect, lift your tongue quickly toward the roof of your mouth, like the first sound in yes. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz.

## Reading the sign

At the end of a word or before another consonant, it softens the consonant before it. You hear this change in (мальчик) /ˈmalʲt͡ɕɪk/. When it stands before a vowel letter, it adds a quick glide right before that vowel. You hear this glide in (семья) /sʲɪmʲˈja/.

## Common pitfalls

Do not add an extra vowel sound like the ending of city. Do not insert a separate vowel between consonants. Keep the consonant soft without dragging it out. To check this, keep your tongue high against the roof of your mouth as you finish the consonant.

articles.title: Э
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter e

The letter (э) /ɛ/ is named (э) /ɛ/. Its main sound is the vowel sound /ɛ/, heard in the word (это) /ˈɛtə/, which means this, that. This letter produces two different sounds in speech.

## How to say it

For the first sound, open your mouth slightly and keep your lips relaxed. Rest the tip of your tongue behind your lower front teeth and raise the middle part of your tongue. Your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, lift your tongue higher toward the roof of your mouth. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration of your vocal cords.

## When to use each sound

This letter makes the sound /ɛ/ when it carries the word stress, as in (поэт) /pɐˈɛt/. In syllables without stress, it makes the sound /ɪ/, as in the word (этаж) /ɪˈtaʂ/.

## Common mistakes to avoid

Do not start this letter with a y sound. It never sounds like the first sound in yes. Keep your tongue steady from the start, like the vowel in the English word bet.

articles.title: Ю
articles.body:
## The letter yu

The letter (ю) /ju/ is called (ю) /ju/. Its main sound is heard in the word (юг) /juk/, which means south. This letter has four sounds in total.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first sound, push your tongue forward and then round your lips tightly. For the second sound, pull your tongue back and push your lips forward into a circle. For the third sound, start with a quick glide and relax your tongue and lips. For the fourth sound, loosen your lips into an open ring. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration of your voice.

## Reading this letter

At the start of a stressed syllable, say the sound /ju/ as in (каюта) /kɐˈjutə/. After a consonant under stress, make the consonant soft and say the sound /u/ as in (люди) /ˈlʲʉdʲɪ/. At the beginning of an unstressed syllable, say the sound /jʊ/ as in (юрист) /jʊˈrʲist/. After a consonant without stress, soften the consonant and say the sound /ʊ/ as in (люблю) /lʲʊˈblʲu/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not drop the quick glide when this letter starts a word. Connect it cleanly, exactly like the start of the English word you. After consonants, do not say a separate sound like the start of yes. Soften the consonant itself and glide directly into the vowel, avoiding the extra step you hear in beauty.

articles.title: Я
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (я) /ja/ is called (я) /ja/. Its main sound is the sound /ja/, as in the word (яблоко) /ˈja.blə.kə/, which means apple. This letter can make four different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, lift the middle of your tongue high. Then open wide and let your voice ring out. For the next sound, drop your jaw and keep your tongue low and flat. For the third sound, raise your tongue high, then drop it just slightly. For the last sound, keep your tongue relaxed near the roof of your mouth. Place your hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz.

## Reading rules

At the start of a word or after another vowel, this stressed letter makes the sound /ja/, as in (маяк) /mɐˈjak/. After a soft consonant under stress, it makes the open sound /a/, as in (мясо) /ˈmʲa.sə/. Without stress at the start of a word or after a vowel, it makes the sound /jɪ/, as in (яйцо) /jɪjˈt͡so/. After a soft consonant without stress before the accent, it makes the sound /ɪ/, as in (мясной) /mʲɪsˈnoj/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the sound /jɪ/ into a long English sound like the vowel in eel. Keep the sound short and weak, like the vowel in the English word bit. When you say the sound after a consonant, do not insert a strong English consonant sound like the first sound in yes. Soften the consonant itself, then glide straight into the vowel.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## Sound of a

The letter (a) /a/ is named (a) /a/. It makes the sound /a/, like in the word (amore) /aˈmo.re/, which means love. This letter always makes only one sound.

## How to say a

Open your mouth wide and let your jaw drop comfortably. Keep your tongue low and flat on the floor of your mouth. Let your lips stay neutral and relaxed. Vibrate your voice freely as air passes through your mouth. Place a hand on your throat to feel the strong buzzing.

## Spelling of a

This letter always makes the sound /a/ in every position, as in the word (casa) /ˈka.za/.

## Mistakes with a

Do not pronounce this sound like the weak murmur at the end of comma. Do not say it like the vowel in cat. Keep your mouth opened wide and clear, just like the open vowel in father.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter bi

The letter (bi) /bi/ makes the sound /b/, as in the word (bene) /ˈbɛ.ne/, which means well. This letter always has one single sound in Italian.

## How to say bi

Press your lips firmly together to stop the air. Release your lips suddenly so the air bursts out. Vibrate your vocal cords at the same time. Place your hand on your throat to feel the gentle buzz.

## Spelling of bi

The letter (bi) /bi/ always makes the sound /b/ everywhere it appears. You hear it at the start of (bello) /ˈbɛl.lo/. You also hear it inside (albero) /ˈal.be.ro/.

## Compare bi with English

This letter sounds just like the English sound in the word boat. Make sure your lips close fully. Do not puff out too much air when you open them.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## Sound of ci

The letter (ci) /tʃi/ usually makes the sound /k/. You hear this in the word (casa) /ˈka.za/, which means house. This letter has two different sounds in Italian.

## How to say ci

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof. Block the air, then release it sharply without voice. For the second sound, touch the ridge behind your front teeth with your tongue tip. Release the air through the small gap with a soft rush. Put your hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords do not vibrate.

## Reading ci

This letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, u, or before consonants. You hear this sound in the word (corpo) /ˈkɔr.po/. The letter makes the sound /tʃ/ when it comes before e or i. You hear this softer sound in the word (cena) /ˈtʃe.na/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not puff out a burst of breath when you make the sound /k/. English words like cat have a strong puff of air. Hold your hand before your mouth and keep the release clean. For the other sound, do not say the sound /s/ as in center. Keep the crisp start like the beginning of cheese.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## The letter di

The letter (di) /di/ makes the sound /d/, heard in (dove) /ˈdo.ve/, which means where. This letter has only one sound in Italian. It stays clear in all positions.

## Making the sound

Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your upper front teeth. Build up gentle air pressure behind it. Drop your tongue tip to release the air. Vibrate your vocal cords at the same moment. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Reading the letter

This letter always makes the sound /d/ in all positions. You hear it at the start of a word, as in (dente) /ˈdɛn.te/. You also hear it between vowels, as in (cadere) /kaˈde.re/.

## Common mistakes

In English words like door, your tongue touches the gum ridge above your teeth. For the Italian sound, move your tongue forward. Touch the flat back of your upper teeth instead. Keep the sound light, with no extra puff of air.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## Letter sound e

This letter is called (e) /e/. Its main sound is the sound /ɛ/, heard in (essere) /ˈɛs.se.re/, which means to be. In Italian, this letter makes two different sounds.

## Pronouncing the letter e

For the first sound, keep your lips spread wide. Raise your tongue high in your mouth, near the roof. For the second sound, drop your jaw slightly lower. Keep your tongue a bit lower in your mouth, with relaxed lips. Touch your throat to feel your voice box vibrate for both vowels.

## Spelling rules for e

This letter sounds closed in all unstressed positions, as in (vedere) /veˈde.re/. It also has this closed sound /e/ in some stressed syllables, like in (mela) /ˈme.la/. In other stressed syllables, it has the open sound /ɛ/, that is an open sound, as in (bello) /ˈbɛl.lo/. The single stressed word (è) /ɛ/ also takes this open sound.

## Common mistakes with e

Do not turn the sound into a glide like the vowel in day. Keep your tongue still until the vowel ends. Do not weaken the unstressed vowel to the weak sound in sofa. Always pronounce the vowel clearly and brightly.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## The letter effe

The letter (effe) /ˈɛffe/ makes the sound /f/. You hear it in the word (fare) /ˈfa.re/, which means to do or to make. This letter has only one sound in Italian.

## Saying the letter

Rest your upper teeth lightly on your lower lip. Push air out gently through the small gap between them. Keep your vocal cords completely still. You can place your hand on your throat to feel that it does not buzz.

## Reading the letter

This letter always makes the sound /f/ in every position. You hear it as a double letter in (caffè) /kafˈfɛ/. Hold the sound longer when you see two of them together.

## Comparing with English

This sound is identical to the sound in the English word find. You do not need to change anything about how you say it. Just hold the sound longer when the letter is doubled.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## The letter gi

The letter (gi) /dʒi/ makes its main sound in the word (gatto) /ˈɡat.to/, which means cat. This letter has two different sounds in Italian.

## How to say gi

Press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly while you buzz your voice. For the other sound, press the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Push air through while your voice buzzes. Place your fingers on your throat to feel that vibration.

## Spelling of gi

This letter sounds like /ɡ/ before the vowels a, o, u, or before a consonant, as in (grande) /ˈɡran.de/. It sounds like /dʒ/ before the letters e or i, as in (gelato) /dʒeˈla.to/ and (giorno) /ˈdʒor.no/.

## Mistakes with gi

Do not soften this letter before the vowel sound in get. The first sound must match the hard sound in goat, not the soft start of gentle.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## The letter acca

The letter (acca) /ˈakka/ has no sound of its own in Italian. You see it at the start of (hotel) /oˈtɛl/, which means hotel. This letter has only one silent form.

## Making the sound

Your mouth makes no sound at all for this letter. Keep your throat quiet and let no extra air push out. Place your hand on your throat. You feel nothing move until you speak the vowel right after it.

## Where it appears

This letter is always silent in every Italian word. You see it at the beginning of words like (hanno) /ˈan.no/.

## Common mistakes

Never blow air like the first sound in hat or house. Start straight on the vowel as in the English word hour or honest.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## Sound of letter i

The name of this letter is (i) /i/. Its main sound is heard in (isola) /ˈiːzola/, which means island. This Italian letter produces two spoken sounds, and sometimes it stays silent.

## How to say it

For the vowel sound, raise your tongue high near the roof of your mouth. Spread your lips wide and keep your voice steady. For the second sound, make this shape very quickly as you glide into the next vowel. Touch your throat to feel your vocal cords buzz continuously.

## Spelling rules

This letter makes the pure vowel sound /i/ on its own, as in (amici) /aˈmiːtʃi/. Next to another vowel in the same syllable, it sounds like /j/, as in (piatto) /ˈpjatto/ and (ieri) /ˈjɛːri/. It is silent when it softens a preceding c or g before a, o, or u, as in (ciao) /ˈtʃaːo/ and (giorno) /ˈdʒorno/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the vowel sound like the short vowel in English bit. Keep your tongue high and tense, like in machine. When it sits between a c or g and another vowel, do not add an extra sound. Keep it completely silent in those words.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## The Letter Elle

The letter (elle) /ˈɛlle/ makes the sound /l/, like in the word (luna) /ˈlu.na/, which means moon. This letter always represents one single sound in Italian words.

## Pronouncing Elle

Press the tip of your tongue against your upper gum ridge, right behind your front teeth. Let the air flow smoothly past both sides of your tongue while you voice the sound. Touch your throat to feel your vocal cords vibrate.

## Reading Rules

This letter always makes the sound /l/ in all positions. You can hear it clearly in the word (sole) /ˈso.le/.

## Common Pitfalls

Do not pull the back of your tongue down as in the English word ball. Keep your tongue tip light and flat behind your teeth, like in the English word leaf.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## Sound of emme

The letter (emme) /ˈɛmme/ makes the sound /m/. You hear this in the word (mare) /ˈma.re/, which means sea. This letter has only one sound in standard Italian.

## How to say it

Close both lips gently together. Send the air out through your nose. Turn on your voice. You can feel your throat vibrate, and your lips buzz softly.

## Spelling rules

The letter makes the sound /m/ in all positions. For instance, you hear it clearly in (mamma) /ˈmam.ma/.

## Common mistakes

This sound is identical to the sound in the English word moon. Italian speakers never drop or alter this sound. You do not need to fix anything.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## The letter enne

The letter (enne) /ˈɛnne/ has three sounds. Its main sound is heard in (notte) /ˈnɔt.te/, which means night.

## How to say enne

Press the tip of your tongue against your upper teeth. Let the air flow through your nose and vibrate your vocal cords. For the second sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. For the third sound, touch your upper front teeth with your lower lip while humming. Feel the vibration in your nose with your finger.

## Reading the letter enne

Before vowels, most consonants, or at the end of a word, it makes the sound /n/ as in (ponte) /ˈpon.te/. When it comes before the letters c or g, it makes the sound /ŋ/ as in (banca) /ˈbaŋ.ka/ and (fango) /ˈfaŋ.ɡo/. When it comes before the letters f or v, it makes the sound /ɱ/ as in (anfibio) /amˈfi.bjo/ and (invito) /imˈvi.to/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not press your tongue behind your top teeth like in the English word net. Keep your tongue directly against your upper teeth. Do not drop the nasal sound before other consonants.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## The letter o

The letter (o) /o/ makes the main sound /ɔ/. You hear it in (occhio) /ˈɔk.kjo/, which means eye. This letter produces two different sounds in Italian.

## Pronouncing the letter o

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue toward the roof. Form a small circle with your lips. For the second sound, lower your jaw slightly more and make a wider circle with your lips. Feel your voice box buzz gently with your fingers.

## Reading the letter o

In unstressed syllables, this letter makes the sound /o/, that is, a closed sound, as in (sole) /ˈso.le/. In stressed syllables before certain consonants, it makes the sound /ɔ/, that is, an open sound, as in (notte) /ˈnɔt.te/.

## Tips for the letter o

Do not turn this letter into two vowels like the sound in boat. Keep your tongue completely still and hold one clear pure tone. Do not relax it into an unclear murmur when unstressed.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## The letter pi

The letter (pi) /pi/ makes the sound of the letter itself. Its main sound is heard in (pane) /ˈpa.ne/, which means bread. This letter makes two sounds, short and long.

## How to say it

Close both lips firmly to stop the airflow completely. Release the air suddenly without breathing out extra air. For the longer sound, hold your lips closed twice as long before opening them. Keep your vocal cords silent while your lips are closed. Put your hand on your throat to feel no vibration.

## Spelling rules

In most places, this letter makes the sound /p/, that is a short p, as in (aperto) /aˈpɛr.to/. When written double or between two connected words, it makes the sound /pː/, that is a long double p, as in (cappa) /ˈkap.pa/.

## Tips for English speakers

You might release a small puff of breath, like in the English word pet. Hold your breath back completely, like after the s in spin. Hold a paper before your mouth to see it stay still.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter cu

The letter (cu) /ku/ has only one sound. You pronounce it as the sound /k/. A good example is (quando) /ˈkwan.do/, which means when.

## How to say it

Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Stop the airflow for a brief moment. Then drop your tongue quickly to release a small burst of air. Do not vibrate your vocal cords. You can touch your throat with your hand to make sure it does not buzz.

## Reading the letter cu

This letter always appears before the vowel u and another vowel. In every single word, it makes the sound /k/. You can see this regular pattern in the word (questo) /ˈkwes.to/. Another clear example is the word (quadro) /ˈkwa.dro/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not release a puff of breath with this sound. In English words like quick, you breathe out sharply. Keep this Italian sound dry, crisp and clean.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## Sound of letter erre

The name of this letter is (erre) /ˈɛrre/. It marks the sound /s/ in the word (sole) /ˈsɔ.le/, which means sun. This letter makes one sound in standard Italian.

## How to say erre

Place the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Let the air pass over your tongue so the tip vibrates rapidly. Vibrate your vocal cords at the same time. You can feel a buzz if you place your fingers on your throat.

## Spelling of erre

This letter always represents the sound /r/. You hear it at the start of a word in (roma) /ˈro.ma/. You also hear a stronger rolled sound when it is written double, as in (carro) /ˈkar.ro/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not make the sound of red by curling your tongue backwards. Instead, tap or roll the tip of your tongue quickly against the roof of your mouth. Keep the rest of your tongue low and relaxed.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## Sound of esse

The name of this Italian letter is spoken as (esse) /ˈɛsse/. Its main sound is the sound /s/, heard in (sera) /ˈse.ra/, which means evening. This letter can make two different sounds in Italian.

## How to say esse

For the first sound, place your tongue tip close behind your upper teeth. Blow air out without using your voice. For the second sound, keep your mouth in the exact same shape. Blow air out while using your voice. You can feel your throat buzz with a hand on your neck.

## Spelling rules for esse

At the start of a word before a vowel, it makes the sound /s/, as in (sole) /ˈso.le/. Next to a voiceless consonant, it also makes the sound /s/, like in (testa) /ˈtɛ.sta/. Before a voiced consonant, it becomes the sound /z/, heard in (sbaglio) /ˈzbaʎ.ʎo/. Between two vowels, it usually makes the sound /z/, as in (rosa) /ˈrɔ.za/.

## Common mistakes with esse

Do not turn the sound /s/ into a sound /z/ when a word begins with a vowel. In English, words like please end with a buzzing sound. Keep your voice quiet when you say the sound /s/ in Italian.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Letter sound ti

The letter (ti) /ti/ makes the sound /t/. You hear this sound in the word (tempo) /ˈtɛm.po/, which means time or weather. This letter always makes this one sound in Italian.

## Saying the sound

Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your upper front teeth. Stop the air completely for a brief moment. Release the air cleanly with no puff of breath. Keep your vocal cords silent. Hold a hand before your lips to check that no warm breath escapes.

## Reading the sound

The letter always sounds as the clean sound /t/ in all positions. You find it at the start, inside or doubled in words. For example, listen to the sound /t/ inside the word (notte) /ˈnɔt.te/.

## Avoiding mistakes

In English words like top, you blow out a puff of air. In Italian, you must hold that breath back. Also place your tongue against your upper teeth, not further back on the gum ridge like in the English word table.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## Sound of u

You call this letter (u) /u/. Its main sound is heard in the word (uno) /ˈu.no/, which means one. It makes two different sounds in Italian.

## How to say u

For the vowel sound, pull your tongue back and high. Round your lips tightly into a small circle. Let your vocal cords vibrate steadily. For the gliding sound, keep the same mouth shape but move quickly into the next vowel. Touch your throat to feel continuous vibration.

## Spelling of u

This letter makes the vowel sound /u/ on its own or between consonants, as in (luna) /ˈlu.na/. It makes the quick gliding sound /w/ right before or after another vowel, as in (uomo) /ˈwɔ.mo/.

## Pitfalls with u

Do not let this sound slide into two vowels like in the English word boot. Keep your tongue steady and your lips firm. Do not add a y sound before it like in music. Make a pure, steady Italian sound from start to finish.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## The letter vu

The letter (vu) /vu/ makes the sound /v/. You hear it in the word (vita) /ˈvi.ta/, which means life. This letter has only one sound in Italian.

## Making the sound

Rest your upper teeth gently on your bottom lip. Push air through the small gap while you use your voice. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the strong buzz.

## When it appears

The letter (vu) /vu/ always makes the sound /v/. You hear it anywhere in a word, as in (avanti) /aˈvan.ti/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not confuse this sound with the sound /b/ or the sound /w/. Keep your top teeth lightly touching your lower lip, as in the English word vine. Never round both lips as you would for wine.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## Sound of zeta

The letter name is (zeta) /ˈdzɛta/. Its main sound is the sound /dz/, heard in the word (zaino) /ˈdzai̯.no/, which means backpack. This letter makes two sounds in Italian.

## How to say zeta

For the first sound, place your tongue behind your top front teeth. Block the air, then release it sharply with a hissing sound. Do not vibrate your vocal cords. For the second sound, make the exact same mouth shape and release the air. This time, vibrate your vocal cords. Put a hand on your throat to feel the buzzing.

## Spelling of zeta

This letter makes the voiceless sound /ts/ after consonants or in common endings, as in (stazione) /statˈtsjoːne/ and (marzo) /ˈmartso/. It makes the voiced sound /dz/ at the start of many words and between vowels, as in (zero) /ˈdzɛːro/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not pronounce this letter like an English z in the word zoo. That English sound is a simple buzz without a stop. Always start with your tongue pressed tight against your teeth. First make a quick t sound or d sound, then let the hiss follow.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## The letter i lunga

The letter (i lunga) /i ˈluŋɡo/ mainly makes the sound /dʒ/, heard in (jeans) /dʒins/, which means jeans. This letter has two different sounds in Italian.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, press the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Release the air with friction while your voice box vibrates. For the other sound, raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Let your voice hum smoothly as the air flows out without friction. Feel your throat vibrate for both sounds.

## Reading the letter

In words borrowed from English, this letter makes the sound /dʒ/, as in (jazz) /dʒɛz/. In old Italian spellings, proper names, and words taken from Latin or German, it makes the sound /j/, as in (juventino) /juvenˈtino/ and (junior) /ˈjunjor/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not confuse the two sounds of this letter. Say the first sound like the starting consonant in jam. Say the other sound like the starting consonant in yes. Never drop the sound or turn it into an open vowel.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## Letter cappa

The letter (cappa) /ˈkappa/ makes the clear sound /k/. Hear it in the word (kiwi) /ˈki.wi/, which means kiwi. This letter has only one sound in Italian. It appears almost only in words taken from other languages.

## Pronouncing the letter

Raise the back of your tongue against the soft back of your mouth roof. Stop the air for a moment. Then release the air suddenly without any breathy puff. Place a hand before your mouth. You should feel no burst of air when you make this crisp click.

## Spelling and use

You see (cappa) /ˈkappa/ in foreign borrowings and international loanwords. In these words, it always makes the sound /k/. You can hear it in (kamikaze) /kamiˈkad.dze/.

## Avoiding mistakes

In English words like kite, you release a small puff of breath. Italian never adds this breathy air. Make the stop sharp and clean, closer to the k in skin than the k in key. Hold back your breath completely.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## Sound of letter doppia vu

The letter (doppia vu) /ˈdoppja vu/ is a foreign letter in Italian. Its main sound is the sound /w/, heard in (web) /ˈwɛb/, meaning web, internet. This foreign letter makes two sounds in Italian.

## How to say doppia vu

To make the first sound, place your top teeth gently on your bottom lip. Blow air through while your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, make a tight small circle with your lips. Pull the back of your tongue up toward the roof of your mouth and voice the sound. Place your hand on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Reading doppia vu

This letter appears only in borrowed words. In words from German and in older loanwords, it makes the sound /v/, as in (wurstel) /ˈvurstel/. In words from English, it makes the sound /w/, as in (weekend) /wiˈkɛnd/.

## Common mistakes with doppia vu

Do not mix up the two sounds in borrowed words. If you see a word from German, do not use the English sound in win. Place your top teeth on your bottom lip, as in vine. If the word comes from English, make a small circle with your lips instead.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## The letter ics

The letter (ics) /iks/ makes the sound /ks/. You hear it in the word (xilofono) /ksiˈlɔfono/, which means xylophone. This letter is not native to Italian and appears in borrowed words. It has two sounds.

## How to say ics

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to block the airflow. Release it sharply without voice, then hiss through your closed teeth. For the second sound, make that same block while vibrating your vocal cords. Then let air buzz between your tongue and upper teeth. Place your fingers on your throat to feel that buzz.

## Spelling of ics

In borrowed words and scientific terms, this letter makes the sound /ks/, as in (extra) /ˈɛkstra/ and (taxi) /ˈtaksi/. Between vowels in certain words taken from French, it makes the sound /ɡz/, as in (ex) /ˈɛɡz/.

## Comparing ics

Do not pronounce this letter at the start of a word as a single buzzing sound, like the z in English zebra. Always start with a crisp stop, as in the middle of English box.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## The letter ipsilon

The letter (ipsilon) /ˈipsilon/ makes the sound /j/. You hear it in the loanword (yogurt) /ˈjɔ.ɡurt/, which means yoghurt. This foreign letter has two sounds in Italian.

## How to say ipsilon

Raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Push voice through the small gap and glide quickly into the next vowel. For the vowel sound, keep your tongue high and forward. Spread your lips wide and let your vocal cords buzz continuously. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration.

## Spelling and sounds

This letter appears in borrowed words. Before another vowel, it makes the sound /j/, as in (yacht) /jɔt/. At the end of a word or as a full vowel, it makes the sound /i/. You hear this vowel sound in (hobby) /ˈɔb.bi/ and in (baby) /ˈbɛi̯.bi/.

## Tips for pronunciation

You might want to make this letter into a vowel at the start of words. Do not say it like the vowel in the English word eat. Keep the start quick and tight, exactly like the beginning of yes.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## The letter a

The letter (a) /a/ is called (a) /a/. Its main sound is the vowel /a/, heard in (agua) /ˈa.ɣwa/, which means water. This letter makes only one sound in standard Spanish.

## Pronouncing the letter

Open your mouth wide and keep your lips relaxed. Rest your tongue flat in the bottom of your mouth. Let your voice flow freely with no friction. Put a hand on your throat to feel the steady vibration of your vocal cords.

## Reading rules

The letter (a) /a/ always represents the sound /a/ in all standard positions. You hear this vowel in (casa) /ˈka.sa/ and in (madre) /ˈma.dɾe/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn this vowel into the sound heard in English cat or father. Keep your mouth open wide and do not change the sound at the end. Never weaken this vowel to an unclear sound when it carries no stress.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## The letter be

The name of this letter is (be) /be/. Its main sound is heard in the word (bueno) /ˈbwe.no/, which means good. This letter makes two different sounds in Spanish.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first sound, close both lips firmly to stop the air. Then open them with voice. For the second sound, bring both lips close together without touching. Let the voice flow through the narrow gap. Put a hand on your throat to feel the voice buzz for both sounds.

## Reading the variants

After a pause or after the letters m or n, you say the sound /b/, as in (también) /tamˈbjen/. Between vowels and after most other consonants, you say the softer sound /β/. You hear this softer sound in (lobo) /ˈlo.βo/ and in (árbol) /ˈaɾ.βol/.

## Avoiding common mistakes

Do not press your lips together when the sound is between vowels. That sounds like the b in baby. Do not touch your upper teeth with your lower lip either, like the v in vine. Keep only your lips close together, and let the air pass gently.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## The letter ce

The name of this letter is (ce) /θe/. Its main sound is heard in the word (casa) /ˈka.sa/, which means house. This letter produces two different sounds in spoken Spanish.

## How to say it

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air sharply without voice. For the second sound, put the tip of your tongue between your teeth. Blow air through the narrow opening softly. Hold your hand on your throat to check that your vocal cords stay still for both sounds.

## Reading and spelling

This letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o and u, as in the word (clase) /ˈkla.se/. It also makes the sound /k/ when placed directly before another consonant. This letter makes the sound /θ/ before the vowels e and i, as in the word (cena) /ˈθe.na/ and the word (cielo) /ˈθje.lo/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not release a puff of breath when saying the sound /k/. The English word cat has a burst of air, so keep your breath back. Do not pronounce the sound /θ/ like an s sound, as in the word sun. Push your tongue gently between your front teeth instead.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## Letter de sound

The letter (de) /de/ makes the sound /d/ in the word (día) /ˈdi.a/, which means day. This Spanish letter has three sounds.

## How to say de

For the first sound, press your tongue tip against the back of your top front teeth. Block the air, voice the sound, and release it gently. For the second sound, place your tongue tip between your teeth without closing them, letting air flow smoothly. For the third sound, blow soft air between your teeth without voicing. Feel your throat vibrate for the first two sounds.

## Spelling rules for de

After a pause, or after the letters m, n, or l, you pronounce the sound /d/ as in (donde) /ˈdon.de/. Between vowels and in most other places, you pronounce the sound /ð/ as in (cada) /ˈka.ða/ or (madre) /ˈma.ðɾe/. At the end of a word in central and northern Spain, you pronounce the soft sound /θ/ as in (madrid) /maˈðɾið/ or (verdad) /beɾˈðað/.

## Mistakes with de

Do not press your tongue behind your teeth as you do in dog. Touch the back of your top front teeth instead. Do not say a hard stop between vowels like the d in ladder. Keep your tongue slightly open so the air flows softly, just like the th sound in either.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## The Sound of the Spanish E

The letter **E** in Spanish represents a clean mid front unrounded vowel, transcribed as `/e/` (phonetically `[e̞]`). Unlike English 'e' or 'ay', it is a pure, steady monophthong that never glides into an 'i' or 'w' sound. It sits comfortably between the vowel in English **bed** and the tense vowel in **say**, but without any diphthongal offglide.

## How to Pronounce E

Part your lips into a relaxed, slight smile and keep your mouth half-open. Place the tip of your tongue gently behind your lower front teeth while raising the middle of your tongue toward the hard palate. Keep your vocal cords vibrating and hold your jaw completely still so the sound remains crisp and pure from start to finish.

## Spelling and Accents

The letter **E** is one of the most frequent letters in Spanish, appearing in countless roots, endings, and verb conjugations. When it carries the word's primary stress contrary to regular accent rules, it receives an acute accent mark as **é** (such as in **café** or **esté**). The graphic accent changes only the stress placement and does not alter the actual quality of the vowel sound.

## Nuances and Common Mistakes

In all positions—whether in **escuela** or **solamente**—Spanish **E** remains crisp, never reducing to a weak schwa `[ə]` like unstressed English vowels. English speakers often make the mistake of turning it into the diphthong `[eɪ]` (as in **play**), especially at the end of words like **bebe** or **tomé**. Focus on cutting the sound off cleanly without letting your tongue slide upward at the end.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## Letter efe sound

The letter (efe) /ˈefe/ makes the sound /f/. You hear it in the word (fuego) /ˈfwe.ɣo/, which means fire. This letter has only one sound in Spanish.

## Pronouncing the letter

Rest your upper teeth lightly against your lower lip. Push air out gently between your teeth and lip. Keep your vocal cords still so you make no humming voice. Place a hand on your throat to feel that it does not buzz.

## Reading the letter

The letter always makes the sound /f/ in all positions. You hear this sound clearly in the word (café) /kaˈfe/.

## Tips for speakers

This sound matches the normal sound in the English word fish. There is no real pitfall with this Spanish letter.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## Sound of letter ge

The name of this letter is (ge) /xe/. Its main sound is the sound /ɡ/, heard in (gato) /ˈɡa.to/, which means cat. This letter makes three different sounds in Spanish.

## How to say ge

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof. Block the air briefly, then release it while your voice buzzes. For the second sound, lift the back of your tongue near the soft roof. Let the air squeeze through smoothly without stopping, keeping your vocal cords vibrating. For the third sound, raise your back tongue high and blow rough air without voice. Touch your throat to feel the buzz stop.

## Spelling of letter ge

After a pause or after a nasal letter before a, o, or u, you hear the hard sound /ɡ/, as in (tengo) /ˈteŋ.ɡo/. Between vowels or after any other letter before a, o, or u, it softens to the sound /ɣ/, like in (amigo) /aˈmi.ɣo/. Before the vowels e or i, it makes the raspy sound /x/, as heard in (gente) /ˈxen.te/.

## Mistakes with ge

Do not say the sound /x/ softly like the letter h in hat. Tighten the back of your throat so the air scrapes loudly. Avoid stopping the air completely when saying the sound /ɣ/ between vowels, as in the English word dagger. Keep the airflow open so it never clicks shut.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## Sound of hache

The letter (hache) /ˈatʃe/ is completely silent in standard Spanish. You hear this clearly in the greeting (hola) /ˈo.la/, which means hello. This letter has two different sounds across words. Most of the time it makes no sound at all. In a few borrowed words, it makes a rough breath sound instead.

## How to say hache

For the main sound, you make no sound and keep your vocal cords quiet. For the second sound, pull the back of your tongue close to the soft roof of your mouth. Push air through the narrow gap to make a raspy, dry hiss. Place a hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords do not buzz.

## Spelling rules for hache

In native and regular Spanish words, you do not pronounce this letter at all. You can hear this in the word (hijo) /ˈi.xo/. In recent foreign loanwords, the letter makes the rough sound /x/. You hear that rasping sound in the word (hámster) /ˈxams.teɾ/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not pronounce this letter like the soft English sound in house. Making a breathy English sound when greeting someone is a very common mistake. Simply skip the letter entirely and start with the next vowel. If the word is a foreign loanword, make the sound rougher than in the English word hot.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## The letter i

The letter (i) /i/ is called (i) /i/. Its main sound is the vowel /i/, that is a steady vowel, heard in the word (isla) /ˈiz.la/, which means island. This letter makes three sounds.

## Pronouncing the letter

For the first sound, spread your lips wide. Raise your tongue high and forward in your mouth. Let your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, push the tongue closer to the roof of your mouth. Glide quickly into the next vowel. For the third sound, glide smoothly from the main vowel toward a high tongue position. Place a hand on your throat to feel continuous vibration.

## Reading the letter

When it forms its own full vowel sound, you say the sound /i/, that is a steady vowel, as in the word (mío) /ˈmi.o/. Before another vowel, it sounds like the quick sound /j/, as in (bien) /bjen/. After another vowel, it becomes the gliding sound /i̯/, that is a closing glide, as in (aire) /ˈai̯.ɾe/.

## Common mistakes

Do not shorten this letter to the relaxed vowel of English sit. Make your lips tighter and keep the sound clean. Do not let the gliding sound become a heavy consonant like the English sound in jump. Keep the airflow smooth without friction.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## Letter sound jota

The name of this letter is (jota) /ˈxota/. It makes the sound /x/, as heard in (jugar) /xuˈɣaɾ/, which means to play. This letter always represents just one single sound in Spanish.

## How to say jota

Raise the back of your tongue toward the soft roof of your mouth. Leave a narrow gap so air rubs through with friction. Do not vibrate your vocal cords. You can feel a steady stream of warm air against your hand held before your lips.

## Spelling rules for jota

This letter always makes the sound /x/ in every position. You can hear it at the end of the word (reloj) /reˈlox/.

## Mistakes to avoid with jota

Do not pronounce this letter like the soft sound in the English word house. Also avoid using the sound in English jump. Push air strongly through the back of your mouth, just like the sound in Scottish loch.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter ka

The letter (ka) /ka/ makes the sound /k/. You hear it in the word (kilo) /ˈki.lo/, which means kilo. This letter has only one sound in Spanish. It is an uncommon letter mostly used in borrowed words.

## How to say it

Press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Stop the air completely for a moment. Then release the air suddenly without puffing out a breath. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. Put a hand on your throat to feel that it stays still.

## When it sounds like this

This letter always makes the sound /k/. You see it at the end of borrowed words like (anorak) /a.noˈrak/. It keeps this same clean sound in any position.

## Common mistakes

In English you often release this sound with a puff of air, as in kite. In Spanish you must not puff out any air. Hold a hand before your lips to make sure you feel no breeze. Keep the stop crisp and dry.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## The letter ele

This letter is called (ele) /ˈele/. Its main sound is heard in the word (luna) /ˈlu.na/, which means moon. The letter makes three slightly different sounds in Spanish.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, place your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Let the air flow past the sides of your tongue. For the second sound, press your tongue tip directly against the back of your top teeth. For the third sound, raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth while touching the ridge. Your voice vibrates, and you can feel this buzz on your throat.

## Reading this letter

Most of the time, the letter makes the sound /l/, that is an l on the ridge, as in (sol) /sol/. Before the consonants t and d, it becomes the sound /l̪/, that is an l against the upper teeth, as in (alto) /ˈal̪.to/. Before ch or y, it makes the sound /lʲ/, that is a softened l, as in (el chico) /elʲ ˈt͡ʃi.ko/.

## Sounds to avoid

Do not swallow this consonant at the end of a syllable. In English words like ball, the back of your tongue pulls down. Keep your tongue high and light in Spanish, like the first sound in leaf.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## Sound of eme

The letter (eme) /ˈeme/ makes the sound /m/. You can hear it in (mano) /ˈma.no/, which means hand. This letter always makes only one sound in Spanish.

## How to say eme

Close both lips firmly together. Let your voice hum through your throat. Send the stream of air out through your nose. Place your hand on your neck to feel the steady buzz.

## Reading eme

This letter always makes the sound /m/ in all positions. Say this sound at the beginning of a syllable or at the end of a syllable, as in (campo) /ˈkam.po/.

## Pitfalls with eme

This sound is identical to the English sound in mother. You do not need to change anything about your mouth or your tongue. There are no special traps or pitfalls.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (ene) /ˈene/ sounds like the start of (noche) /ˈno.t͡ʃe/, which means night. This Spanish letter makes four different sounds.

## How to say

Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Let voiced air flow through your nose. Close both lips completely to let voiced air pass through your nose. Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Press the flat middle of your tongue against your hard roof. Place a hand on your throat to feel continuous vibration.

## Spelling rules

Before vowels and at the start of a word, it sounds like /n/ as in (mano) /ˈma.no/. Before the letters p, b or v, it sounds like /m/ as in (un beso) /um ˈbe.so/. Before c, qu, g or j, it makes the sound /ŋ/ as in (cinco) /ˈθiŋ.ko/. Before ch, y or ll, it sounds like /ɲ/ as in (ancho) /ˈaɲ.t͡ʃo/.

## Common mistakes

You might keep the tip of your tongue raised before letters like p or b. Do not keep your lips open there. Close your lips fully as you would in the English word input. Before sounds made at the back of the mouth, do not keep the tongue fronted. Let your tongue shift to match the next sound smoothly.

articles.title: Ñ
articles.body:
## The letter eñe

The letter (eñe) /ˈeɲe/ represents the sound /ɲ/. You can hear it in the word (niño) /ˈni.ɲo/, which means boy, child. This letter has only one sound in Spanish.

## Mouth movements

Press the broad middle of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Keep the tip of your tongue down behind your bottom front teeth. Let the air pass out through your nose while your vocal cords vibrate. Place two fingers on the bridge of your nose to feel the vibration.

## Reading the letter

The letter (eñe) /ˈeɲe/ always makes the sound /ɲ/ in every position. You see this sound inside the word (año) /ˈa.ɲo/. You also hear this exact sound in the word (España) /esˈpa.ɲa/.

## Common mistakes

Do not separate this sound into two parts like the letters in onion or canyon. Press the flat part of your tongue flat in one single smooth movement. Do not touch your upper teeth with the tip of your tongue.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (o) /o/ is called (o) /o/. It makes the sound /o/, like in the word (ojo) /ˈo.xo/, which means eye. This letter makes only one sound in Spanish.

## How to say it

To make the sound /o/, open your mouth halfway. Pull your tongue back slightly. Round your lips into a circle. Keep your lips and tongue still so the sound stays steady. Your vocal cords vibrate.

## Reading and spelling

The letter (o) /o/ always makes the sound /o/. It makes this sound in every position, as in the word (sol) /sol/.

## Common mistakes

Do not let this vowel slide into a double sound like in the English word boat. Keep your mouth firmly in place from start to finish. Also, never relax it into a weak sound like the second vowel in carrot.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter pe

The letter (pe) /pe/ makes the sound /p/. You hear it in (pan) /ˈpan/, which means bread. This letter has only one sound in Spanish.

## How to say pe

Close both lips firmly to block the air. Then open your lips quickly to release the air. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. Hold your hand in front of your lips to feel almost no breath.

## Spelling of pe

The letter (pe) /pe/ always makes the sound /p/. It sounds the same in every position, as in the word (copa) /ˈko.pa/.

## Mistakes to avoid with pe

Do not blow out a puff of air. In English words like pin, a burst of breath follows the lips opening. Release your lips gently so no puff comes out.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (cu) /ku/ makes the sound /k/. You hear it in the word (queso) /ˈke.so/, which means cheese. This letter makes only one sound in Spanish. It is always followed by another letter to write this sound before vowels.

## Pronunciation guide

Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Stop the breath completely for a moment. Then release the air sharply without using your vocal cords. Hold a hand before your mouth to feel a light burst of air.

## Spelling rules

The letter (cu) /ku/ always appears before the letter u. Together with that letter, it makes the sound /k/ before the letters e or i. For example, you hear this sound in the word (química) /ˈki.mi.ka/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the following vowel letter as a separate sound like in the English word quick. The sound is just a clean consonant, exactly like the first sound in the English word keep. Release the sound cleanly without a strong puff of air.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## The letter erre

The letter (erre) /ˈere/ makes two sounds in Spanish. Its main sound is the sound /r/. You hear this sound in the word (rojo) /ˈro.xo/, which means red.

## How to say it

For the first sound, touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Push air forward to make your tongue tip flap rapidly several times. For the second sound, tap your tongue tip once against that same ridge behind your teeth. Your vocal cords vibrate for both sounds. Place two fingers on your throat to feel this steady buzz.

## When to use each

This letter makes the rolled sound /r/ when written as double r, as in (perro) /ˈpe.ro/. It also makes the sound /r/ at the start of a word, or after l, n, or s. The letter makes the single tap sound /ɾ/ between two vowels, as in (pero) /ˈpe.ɾo/. It also makes the sound /ɾ/ after another consonant, as in (tres) /tɾes/, or at the end of a syllable.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not pull your tongue back into your mouth, as in the English word red. Keep your tongue forward against the hard ridge behind your teeth. Do not blow air without tongue contact, as in the English word rose. Tap your tongue tip firmly against your upper gum instead.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## Letter ese

The letter (ese) /ˈese/ makes the sound /s̺/, as in (sol) /ˈsol/, which means sun. This letter has two sounds in European Spanish.

## How to say ese

For the first sound, lift the tip of your tongue toward the ridge behind your upper teeth. Blow air out without using your voice. For the second sound, make the exact same mouth shape, but turn your voice on. You can feel your throat vibrate with your fingers during the second sound.

## Spelling of ese

The letter (ese) /ˈese/ usually makes the sound /s̺/, like in the word (casa) /ˈkasa/. Before voiced consonants, it can sound like /z̺/, as in (mismo) /ˈmizmo/ or (desde) /ˈdezðe/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not flatten the front of your tongue like in the English word sea. Use the very tip of your tongue raised slightly higher instead. Also, never make a buzzing sound between two vowels like in the English word rise.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Letter te sound

The letter (te) /te/ makes the sound /t/. You hear this sound in the word (tiempo) /ˈtjem.po/, which means time, weather. This letter has only one sound in standard speech.

## How to say letter te

Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your top front teeth. Stop the air completely, then release it quickly without puffing out air. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. Hold your hand before your mouth. You should feel no burst of breath when you release the air.

## Reading letter te

This letter always makes the sound /t/ in all positions. You hear it at the start of the word (taza) /ˈta.θa/. You also hear it in the middle of the word (patio) /ˈpa.tjo/.

## Pitfalls with letter te

Do not puff out a burst of air as you do in top. Keep the release crisp and dry. Do not place your tongue behind your teeth on the gum ridge. Always touch the upper teeth directly.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## The letter u

The letter (u) /u/ is named (u) /u/. Its main sound is heard in the word (uno) /ˈu.no/, which means one. This letter makes two spoken sounds in Spanish, and it can also stay completely silent.

## How to say u

For the main vowel, pull your tongue back and raise it high. Push your lips forward into a tight circle and vibrate your voice. For the quick gliding sound, make the same mouth shape, but glide right into the next vowel without stopping. Check your throat with your fingers to feel the continuous vibration.

## Spelling rules for u

As an ordinary vowel, the letter sounds like /u/, as in (luna) /ˈlu.na/. Next to another vowel, it turns into a quick glide like the sound /w/, as in (agua) /ˈa.ɣwa/. After the letters q or g before e or i, the letter is not pronounced at all. You can hear this silence in (guitarra) /ɡiˈta.ra/.

## Common mistakes with u

Do not let this vowel glide into two parts like the vowel sound in boot. Keep your tongue steady until the sound ends. Also, do not relax your mouth into the weak vowel heard in the word put. Make a tight circle with your lips every time.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## Letter uve sound

This letter is called (uve) /ˈube/. Its main sound is the sound /b/, heard in the word (verde) /ˈbeɾ.de/, which means green. In Spanish, this letter makes two different sounds.

## How to say uve

For the first sound, close both lips firmly. Stop the air, then let it burst open while your voice sounds. For the other sound, bring both lips close together without touching. Let the air squeeze gently through the narrow gap with your voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Spelling rules for uve

At the start of a sentence or after an m or n, it makes the sound /b/, as in (enviar) /emˈbjaɾ/. Between vowels or after any other letter, it makes the sound /β/, as in (uva) /ˈu.βa/. You also hear that softer sound in (curva) /ˈkuɾ.βa/.

## Mistakes to avoid with uve

Do not touch your bottom lip to your top teeth like in the English word vine. Spanish never uses that English sound. Keep your top teeth entirely out of the way. Bring only your two lips together, as if blowing gently on hot soup.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## Letter uve doble

The name of this letter is (uve doble) /ˈdoble be/. Its main sound is heard in the word (web) /ˈweb/, which means web. This letter makes three different sounds in borrowed words.

## Mouth movements

For the first sound, round your lips tightly and lift the back of your tongue. For the second sound, press your lips firmly together, stop the airflow, and release it with your voice. For the third sound, bring your lips close together without touching, and let the air flow smoothly between them. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz for all three sounds.

## Spelling rules

In borrowed words from English, this letter makes the sound /w/, like in (whisky) /ˈwis.ki/. In words from German, at the start of a word, it makes the sound /b/, like in (wolframio) /bolˈfɾa.mjo/ and (wagneriano) /baɡ.neˈɾja.no/. Between vowels in German borrowings, it makes the softer sound /β/, like in (kuwaití) /ku.βajˈti/.

## Common mistakes

You might want to touch your top teeth with your bottom lip, like in the English word vine. Spanish never uses teeth for these sounds. Keep your teeth completely away from your lips. When you say the soft sound, let air squeeze between your lips without closing them fully.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## The letter equis

In Spanish, this letter is called (equis) /ˈekis/. Its main sound is the sound /s/, heard in (xilófono) /siˈlofono/, which means xylophone. This letter can make three different sounds.

## How to say equis

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the roof. Release the air sharply, then blow air through your front teeth without voice. For the second sound, hiss air through your front teeth. For the third sound, blow rough air from deep in your throat. Put your hand on your throat to check that your voice stays off.

## Spelling rules for equis

Between vowels, it makes the sound /ks/, as in (éxito) /ˈeksito/. At the end of a word, it also makes the sound /ks/, as in (tórax) /ˈtoɾaks/. Before a consonant, it makes the sound /s/, as in (texto) /ˈtesto/. In traditional place names, it sounds like the sound /x/, as in (México) /ˈmexiko/ or (Don Quixote) /doŋ kiˈxote/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not voice the sound between vowels as in English exact. Keep it crisp without vocal cord vibration, like the end of box. When it sits before a consonant, do not insert a full k sound. Pronounce it simply as a smooth hiss, just like the s in English best.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## The letter ye

The letter (ye) /ˈje/ sounds like (yo) /ˈɟʝo/, which means I. This letter has three different sounds in spoken Spanish.

## Pronouncing the letter

Raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Push voiced air through the gap to make friction. For the stronger sound, press your tongue firmly against the roof first. Release the air with a slight burst and friction. For the vowel sound, spread your lips wide and keep your tongue high. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration of your vocal cords.

## Reading the letter

Between vowels or after most consonants, the letter sounds like /ʝ/, as in (mayo) /ˈma.ʝo/. At the start of a word or after n or l, it sounds like /ɟʝ/, as in (cónyuge) /ˈkon.ɟʝu.xe/. At the end of a word, it sounds like /i/, as in (rey) /rei̯/. The single word (y) /i/ also uses this vowel sound.

## Common pronunciation errors

Do not turn the strong sound into the English j in judge. Keep the tip of your tongue down behind your bottom teeth. Do not replace the friction sound with a weak English y in yes. Make sure you squeeze the air through a narrow space. Do not make the vowel too long like the ee in see. Keep the sound short and tense.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## Letter zeta sound

The letter (zeta) /ˈθeta/ makes the sound /θ/. You hear it in (zapato) /θaˈpa.to/, which means shoe. This letter has only one sound in standard Spanish from Spain.

## How to say zeta

Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your upper and lower front teeth. Blow air gently through the small gap without vibrating your vocal cords. You can feel cool air flowing across your tongue tip.

## Reading zeta in words

This letter always makes the sound /θ/ in standard European Spanish. You can find it at the end of a word like (luz) /luθ/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not buzz this sound like the English letter z in zoo. Also, do not use the hissing s sound from sun. Keep your tongue between your teeth and blow soft air.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## The letter a

You call this letter (a) /a/. Its main sound is the sound /a/, as in (ami) /a.mi/, which means friend. This letter makes two sounds in French.

## Making the sound

For the front sound, drop your jaw wide. Lay your tongue flat and forward in your mouth. For the back sound, pull your tongue slightly back into your throat and widen your mouth. Your vocal cords vibrate for both sounds. You can touch your throat to feel that vibration.

## Reading the letter

You pronounce the regular letter or the accented letter with a grave accent as the front sound /a/, as in (là) /la/. You pronounce the letter with a circumflex accent as the deeper back sound /ɑ/, that is a back vowel, as in (pâte) /pɑt/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not turn this vowel into the sound in cat. Keep your mouth open and relaxed, like the vowel in father. Do not glide to another sound at the end, as in day. Hold one steady vowel until the sound stops.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (bé) /be/ makes the sound /b/ in the word (balle) /bal/, which means ball. Across French words, this letter can make two different sounds, or stay completely silent.

## Mouth shape and sound

Press your lips tightly together, build up gentle air behind them, and release your lips. Let your voice box buzz at the exact moment your lips open. To make the other sound, bring your lips together in the same way, but do not use your voice box. Place a hand flat against your throat. You should feel a clear buzz for the first sound, but no vibration for the second.

## Reading rules and spelling

In most positions, the letter gives the sound /b/, as in the word (robe) /ʁɔb/. It changes to the sound /p/ right before an unvoiced consonant, as in the word (obtenir) /ɔp.tə.niʁ/. At the end of a few words, this letter is silent and makes no sound, as in the word (plomb) /plɔ̃/.

## Tips for English learners

In English words like bat, the sound starts with a tiny puff of air. In French, you must buzz your vocal cords earlier, before the lips part. Do not push out a strong puff of breath. Keep the sound light and clean.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## The letter cé

The letter (cé) /se/ usually sounds like the sound /k/. You hear it in the word (café) /ka.fe/, which means coffee. This letter makes two different sounds across French words, and it can also stay silent.

## Mouth movements

For the first sound, raise the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Release a burst of air without using your voice. For the second sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap. You can place a hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords do not vibrate for either sound.

## Spelling and sounds

This letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, or u, or before consonants, as in (carte) /kaʁt/. It makes the sound /s/ before e, i, or y, as in (cerise) /sə.ʁiz/. With a cedilla mark underneath, it makes the sound /s/ before a, o, or u, as in (garçon) /gaʁ.sɔ̃/. At the end of some words, it is not pronounced, as in (tabac) /ta.ba/ and (porc) /pɔʁ/.

## Common mistakes

In English, the sound of k in words like cat often comes with a puff of air. In French, release the air gently with no puff. Keep the sound clear and crisp.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter dé

The letter (dé) /de/ is called (dé) /de/. Its main sound is the sound /d/, heard in the word (date) /dat/, which means date. This letter has one spoken sound, and can also be silent.

## How to say it

Touch the back of your upper front teeth with your tongue tip. Build up air behind the tip, then release it sharply. Vibrate your vocal cords at the exact same moment. Put a hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Reading and spelling

In most positions, this letter gives the sound /d/, like in the word (mode) /mɔd/. At the end of many words, this letter is not pronounced at all. You can hear this silence in the word (nord) /nɔʁ/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not place your tongue on the gum ridge behind your teeth, as in door. Touch the back of your upper teeth instead. Keep the burst crisp without puffing out extra breath. When this letter stands at the end of a word, do not pronounce it.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## The letter e

The letter name is (e) /ə/. Its main sound is heard in (menu) /mə.ny/, which means menu. This letter makes three spoken sounds, and it can also stay completely silent.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first sound, relax your tongue in the middle of your mouth. Round your lips gently and push them forward a little. For the second sound, spread your lips wide and keep your tongue high. For the third sound, drop your jaw slightly lower and keep your lips relaxed. Check that your vocal cords vibrate for all three vowels.

## Reading the spellings

In short one-syllable words like (le) /lə/, this letter makes the sound /ə/. When written with an acute accent, as in (été) /e.te/, it makes the sound /e/.
