With a grave accent, as in (père) /pɛʁ/, it makes the sound /ɛ/, that is an open e sound. Finally, this letter is completely silent at the end of many words, such as (table) /tabl/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not let your lips glide or change shape while speaking. In English words like day, the vowel glides into another sound. Keep your jaw completely still until the sound finishes. Do not pronounce the silent ending as an extra syllable, unlike the end of the English word menu.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (effe) /ɛf/ makes the sound /f/ in the word (film) /film/, which means film, movie. This letter can produce two spoken sounds, and sometimes it stays silent.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, place your top teeth on your bottom lip. Blow air gently between them without using your voice. To make the second sound, keep the same mouth shape. Add your voice so you feel a strong buzz on your throat.

## Spelling rules

In most positions, the letter sounds like the sound /f/, as in the word (café) /ka.fe/. When the number nine links to a word starting with a vowel, the letter sounds like the sound /v/, as in (neuf ans) /nœ.vɑ̃/. In a few special words, the letter is not pronounced, as in (clef) /kle/.

## Comparing with English

The main sound is identical to the English sound in fox. No special adjustment is needed. When you voice the letter before a vowel, make sure it matches the English sound in vine. Simply let your vocal cords buzz.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## The letter gé

The letter (gé) /ʒe/ mostly makes the sound /ɡ/, like in the word (gare) /ɡaʁ/, which means train station. This letter has two different spoken sounds in French. Sometimes it stays completely silent.

## How to say it

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly while using your voice. For the second sound, push your lips forward slightly into a soft circle. Blow air gently through your teeth while vibrating your vocal cords. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz.

## Reading this letter

You say the sound /ɡ/ when the letter sits before a, o, u or a consonant, as in (gros) /ɡʁo/. You say the sound /ʒ/ before e, i or y, as heard in (gel) /ʒɛl/ and (girafe) /ʒi.ʁaf/. At the end of some words, the letter is not pronounced, like in (doigt) /dwa/ and (sang) /sɑ̃/.

## Common mistakes

Do not add a puff of air when you say the hard sound. Keep the sound /ɡ/ crisp and smooth. Do not add a d sound before the soft variant. You must say the sound like the middle of the English word measure, not like the start of jump.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (ache) /aʃ/ has no sound of its own. It is completely silent in the word (habiter) /a.bi.te/, which means to live. This letter never makes any sound in French words.

## How to say it

You make no movement with your mouth. Your tongue and lips stay ready for the next letter. No air puffs out from your throat. Hold a hand before your lips to feel no puff of breath.

## Spelling rules

This letter is always silent. It makes no sound in (homme) /ɔm/. It also makes no sound in (héros) /e.ʁo/.

## Common mistakes

Do not breathe out like the first sound in hat. Keep your throat quiet. Go straight to the next vowel with no breath.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## The letter i

The letter (i) /i/ is called /i/. Its main sound is the sound /i/, heard in the word (ici) /i.si/, which means here. In French, this letter has two distinct sounds across various words.

## How to say it

For the vowel sound, spread your lips wide into a smile. Push your tongue high and forward against your lower teeth. For the glide sound, quickly narrow your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Glide swiftly into the next vowel without stopping the airflow. Touch your throat to feel continuous voice vibration.

## Spelling rules

This letter usually makes the sound /i/ on its own or with diacritics, like in (île) /il/. It makes the gliding sound /j/ when it stands directly before another vowel. You hear this glide in the word (ciel) /sjɛl/. The sound flows quickly into the following vowel.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce this letter like the relaxed vowel in the English word sit. Keep your tongue high and your lips tense. Do not lengthen the vowel into a glide like the sound in see. Keep the sound pure, short, and steady.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## The sound

The letter (ji) /ʒi/ makes the sound /ʒ/. You hear this sound in the word (jupe) /ʒyp/, which means skirt. This letter makes only one sound in standard French words.

## How to say it

Push your lips forward into a loose ring. Raise the front of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Do not touch the roof. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap. Make your vocal cords vibrate at the same time. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the steady buzz.

## Spelling rules

In almost all regular French words, this letter makes the sound /ʒ/. You hear it at the start of (joli) /ʒɔ.li/. You also hear it in (jeu) /ʒø/. It keeps this same sound before every vowel.

## Common mistakes

Do not start this sound with a hard tap. English words like jam or jump begin with a firm press against the roof. The French sound must start smoothly with no tap. Keep the air flowing smoothly like the sound in the middle of treasure or measure.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter ka

The letter (ka) /ka/ makes the sound /k/. You hear it in the word (kilo) /ki.lo/, which means kilo. This letter always makes just one sound in French.

## How to say it

Press the back of your tongue firmly against the roof of your mouth. Stop the air completely for a moment. Then lower your tongue quickly to release a sharp burst of air. Do not vibrate your vocal cords. Hold a hand before your lips to feel a sudden puff of air.

## Spelling rules

This letter always produces the same sound in all positions. At the end of a word, it sounds like /k/ in (anorak) /a.nɔ.ʁak/.

## Common mistakes

In English, this sound comes with a strong puff of breath at the start of words like keep. In French, you must release much less air. Keep the burst very crisp and short. Hold a hand before your mouth and make sure you feel only a tiny breath.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## Letter sound elle

The name of this letter is (elle) /ɛl/. Its main sound is the sound /l/, like in the word (lune) /lyn/, which means moon. This letter has one spoken sound in standard speech, but it can also stay completely silent.

## How to say elle

Press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper front teeth. Keep the sides of your tongue down so air passes freely around them. Turn on your voice. You can feel your throat vibrate with your fingers. Keep the back of your tongue flat and relaxed throughout the whole sound.

## Spelling rules elle

In most positions, you pronounce this letter as the sound /l/, like in (bal) /bal/. At the end of a few specific words, the letter is not pronounced. For example, it stays silent in the word (fusil) /fy.zi/ and in the word (outil) /u.ti/.

## Mistakes to avoid elle

Do not raise the back of your tongue at the end of a word. Many learners make a dark sound, like the end of bell. Keep your tongue flat and clear instead. Never drop the sound when it sits at the end of most normal words.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## Letter emme sound

The French letter (emme) /ɛm/ makes the sound /m/. You hear this sound in the word (mer) /mɛʁ/, which means sea. This letter has two spoken variants.

## Saying the sound

Close both lips firmly together. Let your vocal cords vibrate with your voice. Let the air flow out freely through your nose. Keep your hand on your throat to feel the strong hum.

## Spelling rules

This letter makes the sound /m/ before any vowel or another identical letter, as in (pomme) /pɔm/. It is not pronounced in a few special words, such as (damner) /dɑ.ne/.

## Common mistakes

This sound matches the English sound in mother. You already pronounce this sound naturally, so there is no real pitfall to avoid.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## The letter enne

The letter (enne) /ɛn/ makes the sound /n/. You hear it in the word (nez) /ne/, which means nose. This letter has one main spoken sound. In certain combinations, it can also stay completely silent.

## Pronouncing the letter

Press the tip of your tongue against the gum ridge behind your top teeth. Keep your lips relaxed and parted. Send the air out smoothly through your nose while your vocal cords vibrate. Place two fingers on your throat to feel the steady buzzing.

## Reading the letter

This letter makes the sound /n/ before a vowel, as in (minute) /mi.nyt/. It stays completely silent at the end of words or after the letter m, as in (condamner) /kɔ̃.da.ne/ and (monsieur) /mə.sjø/.

## Avoiding common mistakes

The French sound is lighter and crisper than in English. Do not pull your tongue tip back or press too heavily like in net. Keep your tongue relaxed against the front gum ridge, and let the air flow smoothly.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (o) /o/ is called (o) /o/. It usually makes the sound /ɔ/, that is an open o, like in (olive) /ɔ.liv/, which means olive. This letter has two different sounds in French. Both sounds are clear vowels.

## How to say it

For the first sound, drop your jaw slightly. Round your lips gently and pull your tongue back. For the second sound, push your lips forward into a small tight circle. Keep your tongue pulled back and raise the back of your tongue higher. Touch your throat to feel your vocal cords vibrate for both.

## When to use each

This letter makes the sound /ɔ/, that is an open o, in most closed syllables. You can hear it in (porte) /pɔʁt/. It makes the sound /o/, that is a closed o, at the end of a word, as in (vélo) /ve.lo/. It also makes this sound before an s that sounds like a z, as in (rose) /ʁoz/.

## Common mistakes

Do not let your lips glide into a w sound at the end, like in the English word boat. English vowels often move, but French vowels stay completely still. Keep your lips frozen in a circle until the sound finishes.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## The letter pé

The name of this letter sounds like (pé) /pe/. It usually makes the sound /p/, as in the word (porte) /pɔʁt/, which means door. This letter has one spoken sound, but it can also stay completely silent.

## How to say it

Close both lips firmly together to stop the air. Then open your lips quickly to let the air pop out. Keep your vocal cords still so they do not buzz. Hold your hand before your mouth. You should feel only a very gentle breath.

## Spelling rules

This letter makes the sound /p/ at the beginning or inside a word, as in (pomme) /pɔm/. It is usually silent at the very end of a word, as in (drap) /dʁa/ and (trop) /tʁo/.

## Common mistakes

In English words like pat, a strong puff of air escapes. In French, you must release your lips with very little air. Hold a light paper strip before your face. The paper must hardly move when you speak.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is (qu) /ky/. Its main sound is the sound /k/, heard in the word (cinq) /sɛ̃k/, which means five. This letter produces one single sound on its own.

## How to say it

Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Stop the air for a moment. Then release the air suddenly without using your voice. Touch your throat to feel that your vocal cords do not vibrate.

## Spelling rules

This letter appears at the end of words or very rarely on its own. It always makes the sound /k/, as in the word (coq) /kɔk/.

## Common mistakes

In English words like quick, this letter has an added w sound. Do not add any extra sound in French. You should produce only the crisp k sound, just like the sound in the English word cook.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter erre

The letter (erre) /ɛʁ/ is called by its name. It makes the sound /ʁ/ as in (rue) /ʁy/, which means street. This letter makes one spoken sound, and can also be silent.

## How to say erre

Keep the tip of your tongue down behind your lower front teeth. Raise the back of your tongue toward the soft part of your throat. Push air through the small gap to make a soft friction. Your vocal cords can vibrate gently. Place your hand on your throat to feel this light vibration.

## Spelling rules for erre

This letter usually makes the sound /ʁ/ in almost any position, as in (rare) /ʁaʁ/. At the end of many words, especially verbs ending in e r, the letter is not pronounced at all. You can hear this silence in the word (parler) /paʁ.le/.

## Mistakes to avoid with erre

Do not roll the sound with the tip of your tongue like in Spanish. Do not curl your tongue backward like in the English word red. Keep your tongue tip strictly down behind your bottom front teeth. Let the air pass only at the very back of your mouth.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## The letter esse

The letter (esse) /ɛs/ makes the sound /s/ in the word (sac) /sak/, which means bag. This letter has three different sounds across French words.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth. Push air through the small gap without your voice. For the second sound, keep the same mouth shape, but turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel the strong buzz. For the third variant, keep your mouth still and make no sound at all.

## Reading this letter

At the start of a word or next to a consonant, it makes the sound /s/ as in (poste) /pɔst/. When it stands between two vowels, it makes the sound /z/ as in (rose) /ʁoz/. At the end of many words, you do not pronounce this letter, as in (bras) /bʁa/.

## Common mistakes

Do not buzz the letter between vowels if you want the sound in sun. When this letter appears between vowels, always pronounce it like the buzzing sound in zero. At the ends of most words, remember to stay silent, unlike English plurals such as cats or dogs.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Letter sound té

The letter (té) /te/ makes the sound /t/. You hear it in the word (table) /tabl/, which means table. This letter has three possible pronunciations.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, press the tip of your tongue against your upper front teeth. Release the air suddenly without breathing out a puff of air. For the second sound, place your tongue tip near your lower front teeth and blow air through. Hold your fingers against your neck to feel that your voice stays completely silent.

## Reading rules

In most positions, before vowels and consonants, you pronounce the sound /t/, as in (tapis) /ta.pi/ or (porte) /pɔʁt/. Before the letter i followed by another vowel, you say the sound /s/, as in (patient) /pa.sjɑ̃/ or (démocratie) /de.mɔ.kʁa.si/. At the end of many common words, this letter is silent, as in (salut) /sa.ly/ or (petit) /pə.ti/.

## Common mistakes

In English words like top, you puff air out after the consonant. Keep your tongue directly against your teeth and stop any puff of air. Also, do not pronounce the silent letter at the end of a word like you would in English net.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## Sound of letter u

The letter (u) /y/ is named (u) /y/. Its main sound is heard in (usine) /y.zin/, which means factory. This letter makes two distinct sounds in spoken French.

## How to say u

For the first sound, place your tongue forward against your bottom teeth. Push your lips forward into a tight small circle and vibrate your voice. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration. For the second sound, make this same shape and quickly glide into the next vowel.

## Spelling of u

In most words, this vowel gives the full sound /y/, as in (sûr) /syʁ/. When it stands directly before another spoken vowel, it becomes a brief glide /ɥ/. You hear this gliding sound in (huit) /ɥit/ and (nuit) /nɥi/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not replace this sound with the vowel of boot. Keep your tongue pushed forward, like saying beet, but push your lips into a tight circle. Do not add a glide sound like you hear in music.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## Letter sound

French spells this letter as (vé) /ve/. It makes the sound /v/. You hear it clearly in the word (vélo) /ve.lo/, which means bicycle. Across French words, this letter has only one sound.

## How to say it

Press your top front teeth gently against your lower lip. Blow air smoothly through that small gap. Turn your voice on at the same time. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Spelling rules

This letter always makes the sound /v/ in French words. You hear it at the start of a word, as in (vent) /vɑ̃/. You also hear it in the middle of words.

## Common mistakes

This sound matches the first sound in the English word vine. Do not round your lips as you would for the letter w in water. Keep your upper teeth firmly on your lower lip so the sound never slips.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## The letter double vé

The letter is called (double vé) /dublə ve/. Its main sound is heard in the word (wagon) /va.ɡɔ̃/, which means railway carriage. This letter can make two different sounds.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, place your upper front teeth against your lower lip. Push air out while your vocal cords vibrate. For the next sound, make a tight small circle with your lips. Pull the back of your tongue upward. Let your vocal cords vibrate as air flows outward. Touch your neck to feel the steady buzz.

## Reading the letter

In older borrowings mostly from Germanic languages, this letter sounds like /v/, as in (warrant) /va.ʁɑ̃/. In modern loanwords mainly taken from English, it sounds like /w/, as in (web) /wɛb/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not use the sound in vine for every loanword. Some modern words require the beginning sound of water instead. Never pause awkwardly before this letter. Simply pronounce it as one smooth glide.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter ixe

The letter (ixe) /iks/ sounds mainly like the sound /ks/. You hear it in (texte) /tɛkst/, which means text. This letter has four different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, lift the back of your tongue. Stop the air, release it, and blow through your teeth. For the second sound, make that same movement and vibrate your vocal cords. For the last sound, blow air past your tongue tip behind your teeth without voice. Place a hand on your neck to check the vibration.

## Spelling rules

Before a consonant or after a starting vowel, you say the sound /ks/, as in (taxi) /tak.si/. After a starting e and before a vowel, you say the sound /ɡz/, as in (examen) /ɛɡ.za.mɛ̃/ or (exil) /ɛɡ.zil/. In special counting words, it sounds like the sound /s/, as in (dix) /dis/ or (six) /sis/. At the end of most words, it is silent, as in (paix) /pɛ/ or (deux) /dø/.

## Common mistakes

Do not voice every double sound. In the English word exit, many people say the sound /ɡz/. Keep the French combination unvoiced when a consonant follows. Also, remember that word ends stay silent. Do not pronounce the final letter as in the English word box.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (i grec) /i ɡʁɛk/ makes the sound /j/. You hear it in (yeux) /jø/, which means eyes. This letter has two different sounds.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, lift your tongue high toward the roof of your mouth. Keep your lips relaxed and let the voiced air glide quickly into the next vowel. For the other sound, spread your lips wide and smile. Keep your tongue very high and forward. Place a hand on your throat to feel continuous vibration.

## Reading rules

Before a vowel, it sounds like the sound /j/, as in (yoga) /jo.ɡa/. Between two consonants, it makes the sound /i/, as in (cycle) /sikl/. At the end of a word, it also makes the sound /i/, as in (jury) /ʒy.ʁi/.

## Common mistakes

Do not let this letter glide into a double sound like in the English word my. French vowels stay pure and steady. Keep your jaw still and avoid shifting your lips at the end of the sound.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## Letter zède sound

The letter (zède) /zɛd/ makes the main sound /z/, as in the word (zèbre) /zɛbʁ/, which means zebra. This letter has one spoken sound in standard French, but it can also be silent.

## How to say zède

Bring your teeth close together and place your tongue tip near your upper ridge. Push air through the narrow gap while you buzz your vocal cords. Place your hand on your throat to feel the buzzing vibration clearly.

## Reading the letter zède

At the start of a word or between vowels, this letter sounds like /z/, as in (zone) /zon/. At the end of many everyday words, the letter is silent, as in (nez) /ne/ and (riz) /ʁi/.

## Sounds to watch for

This sound is just like the buzzing sound in the English word zip. Do not whisper the sound like the hiss in sip, because your throat must vibrate throughout. At the end of words, remember to leave the letter completely quiet.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (a) /ɒ/ is called (a) /ɒ/. Its main sound is heard in (alma) /ˈɒlmɒ/, which means apple. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian. It never changes its sound.

## Mouth shape

Open your mouth fairly wide and drop your jaw. Pull your tongue back and keep it low. Shape your lips into an open ring. Let your vocal cords vibrate freely. You can feel your throat vibrate when you make this voiced vowel.

## Reading rules

This letter always makes the sound /ɒ/. In every position, it keeps the same quality. For instance, see the word (ablak) /ˈɒblɒk/.

## Common pitfalls

Do not say the flat vowel in cat. That sound keeps the lips wide and flat. Instead, pull your tongue back and make an open ring with your lips. It is very close to the vowel in the British word lot.

articles.title: Á
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter á

The letter (á) /aː/ is called (á) /aː/. It makes the sound /aː/, as in the word (ár) /ˈaːr/, which means price or flood. This letter always makes only one sound in Hungarian.

## How to say it

Open your mouth wide and keep your tongue low and flat. Do not round your lips. Let your voice flow out steadily to make a long clear vowel. Place your hand on your throat to feel the strong steady vibration.

## Spelling rules

This letter always makes the long sound /aː/ in every position. You hear this sound in the word (ház) /haːz/.

## Common mistakes

You might make this vowel too short. It sounds very close to the vowel in the English word father. Keep your mouth wide open and hold the sound twice as long as a short vowel.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## Sound of bé

The letter name is (bé) /beː/. Its main sound is heard in the word (baba) /ˈbɒbɒ/, which means baby or doll. This letter makes two sounds.

## How to say bé

Close both lips firmly to block the air. Open your lips quickly and let your voice vibrate. For the other sound, keep the same mouth shape and release the air without your voice. Touch your throat to feel the vibration turn on or off.

## Reading bé

Normally, you pronounce the sound /b/, as in the word (jobb) /jobː/. Before voiceless consonants, you pronounce the sound /p/ instead, as in the word (rabkocsi) /ˈrɒpkot͡ʃi/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not release a puff of breath with the sound /p/. Keep it tight, like the letter in spin rather than pin.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## The letter cé

The letter (cé) /tseː/ is the fifth letter of the Hungarian alphabet. Its primary sound is the sound /ts/, heard in (cica) /ˈtsi.tsɒ/, which means kitten. This letter produces two sounds in total.

## Pronouncing cé

For the first sound, place the tip of your tongue behind your upper front teeth. Build air pressure, then release it quickly with a sharp hiss. Keep your vocal cords quiet. For the second sound, make the exact same movement, but add your voice so your throat vibrates. Put two fingers on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Spelling rules for cé

In most positions, this letter makes the sound /ts/. You hear this at the end of (arc) /ɒrts/. Before a voiced consonant, the letter changes its sound to /dz/. You hear this in the word (lécből) /ˈleːdzbøːl/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce this letter as a hard sound like the c in cat. Never pronounce it as a soft sound like the c in city. Instead, think of the sound at the end of cats. Unlike in English, this crisp sound easily starts a word.

articles.title: Cs
articles.body:
## Sound of csé

The letter (csé) /tʃeː/ makes the sound /t͡ʃ/ in (csillag) /ˈtʃil.lɒɡ/, which means star. This letter makes two sounds in Hungarian.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, touch the roof of your mouth behind your upper teeth. Release the air with a soft burst. Keep your voice quiet. To make the second sound, shape your mouth the same way. Turn on your voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Reading the letter

Most of the time, this letter sounds like the sound /t͡ʃ/, as in (kocsi) /ˈkot͡ʃi/. Before certain voiced consonants, it changes to the sound /d͡ʒ/, as in (tanácsba) /ˈtɒnaːd͡ʒbɒ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not soften this letter into the sound in sheet. Make a clean, crisp stop like the sound in cheese. When it turns voiced, match the sound in jump.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (dé) /deː/ makes the sound /d/. You hear it in the word (dob) /ˈdob/, which means drum. This letter has three different sounds.

## How to say it

Press the tip of your tongue against your upper gum line. Release the air with your voice on. Next, make the same movement without your voice. For the last sound, press the flat body of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Hold the closure longer, and let your voice hum. Put your hand on your throat to feel the voice buzz.

## Reading rules

Before vowels and at the start of words, it sounds as /d/, like in (madár) /ˈmɒdaːr/. When it sits before voiceless consonants, it sounds as the unvoiced sound /t/, as in (adta) /ˈɒttɒ/ and (hadtest) /ˈhɒttɛʃt/. Before the letter j, it joins with it to make the long sound /ɟː/, as in (adja) /ˈɒɟːɒ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not place your tongue tip too far back like in the English word door. Keep the tongue tip forward against your upper teeth ridge. Also, do not puff out a breath of air at the end. Make the sound sharp and clean.

articles.title: Dz
articles.body:
## Sound of dzé

The name of this letter is (dzé) /dzeː/. Its primary sound is the sound /ˈd͡ʒuŋɡɛl/, heard in the word (dzsungel) /ˈd͡ʒuŋɡɛl/, which means jungle. This letter makes two distinct sounds in Hungarian.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, place your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Release the air slowly with vibration from your vocal cords. For the second sound, pull your tongue slightly further back against the roof of your mouth. Push the air through firmly while your vocal cords vibrate. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the strong buzzing.

## Spelling patterns

In native roots and everyday loanwords, this letter makes the sound /ˈbod͡zɒ/, as in the word (bodza) /ˈbod͡zɒ/. When followed by the letter s, it combines to produce the sound /ˈd͡ʒɛki/, as in the word (dzseki) /ˈd͡ʒɛki/.

## Common traps

Do not split the first sound into two separate letters. It is a single smooth blend, like the middle of the English word kids. For the second sound, avoid an unvoiced puff of air. Keep your vocal cords buzzing steadily, exactly like the first consonant in the English word jam.

articles.title: Dzs
articles.body:
## Letter name dzsé

The letter is called (dzsé) /dʒeː/. It makes the sound /d͡ʒ/, as in the word (dzsem) /ˈd͡ʒɛm/, which means jam. This letter has only one sound.

## Pronouncing the letter

Press the tip of your tongue against the roof of your mouth, just behind your upper teeth. Push air gently against this seal, then release it while your vocal cords vibrate. Put a hand on your throat. You will feel a strong buzz when you make the sound.

## Letter spelling rules

This letter always produces the same sound wherever it appears in a word. You pronounce it as the sound /d͡ʒ/ in every position, for instance in the word (tiniédzser) /ˈtini.eːd͡ʒɛr/.

## Comparing similar sounds

This sound is identical to the first sound in the English word judge. Make sure your vocal cords vibrate, so you do not say the softer sound in church.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## Sound of letter e

The letter name is (e) /ɛ/. It makes the sound /ɛ/, like in the word (este) /ˈɛʃtɛ/, which means evening. This letter always makes only one sound in Hungarian. It sounds very open and clear.

## How to say letter e

Open your mouth fairly wide. Keep your tongue low and forward, touching your bottom teeth. Spread your lips slightly. Let the air flow freely while you vibrate your vocal cords. Place your fingers on your throat to feel that strong buzz.

## Spelling of letter e

This letter always produces the same open sound /ɛ/ everywhere. You can hear it in the word (ember) /ˈɛmbɛr/. No accents or neighbouring consonants change this vowel.

## Mistakes to avoid with e

Do not make this vowel too long. Do not glide into an extra sound at the end, as in the English word say. Keep it short and steady, very similar to the vowel in bet.

articles.title: É
articles.body:
## Sound of letter é

The name of this letter is (é) /eː/. It represents the sound /eː/, like in the word (ég) /eːɡ/, which means sky or burn. This letter has only one sound.

## How to say é

Spread your lips wide into a smile. Raise the front of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Hold your mouth steady and do not move your lips or tongue. Let your vocal cords vibrate steadily. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the strong and steady buzzing.

## Spelling of letter é

This letter always keeps its one sound in all regular positions. It represents the sound /eː/ in the word (kép) /keːp/.

## Comparing letter é

Learners often turn this sound into a gliding vowel, like the sound in cake. Do not move your tongue up at the end. Keep your tongue completely still and hold one pure sound.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (eff) /ɛf/ makes the sound /f/. You hear it in the word (fa) /ˈfɒ/, which means tree or wood. This letter makes only one sound in Hungarian.

## How to say it

Rest your upper teeth gently on your lower lip. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap. Keep your vocal cords completely still. Touch your throat to feel that it does not buzz.

## Reading guide

This letter always makes the sound /f/ in all regular positions. You can hear it clearly in the word (fül) /ˈfyl/.

## Common mistakes

This sound is identical to the first sound in the English word fish. There are no tricky pitfalls with this letter in Hungarian.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter gé

The letter (gé) /ɡeː/ has two sounds. Its main sound is the sound /ɡ/, like in the word (gomb) /ˈɡomb/, which means button.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly and turn on your voice. For the second sound, make the exact same tongue movement, but do not use your voice. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the vibration stop.

## Spelling rules

In most places, this letter makes the sound /ɡ/, like in the word (ág) /ˈaːɡ/. It changes to the sound /k/ when it stands directly before a voiceless consonant. You hear this sound change in the word (megfog) /ˈmɛkfoɡ/.

## Common mistakes

You might soften this letter before front vowels into the sound in English gem. Always keep it hard, like the first sound in garden. Also, do not forget to turn off your voice before voiceless sounds. Say it like the sound in bake, not bag.

articles.title: Gy
articles.body:
## Letter gyé

The letter (gyé) /ɟeː/ makes the sound /ɟ/, as in the word (gyerek) /ˈɟɛrɛk/, which means child. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian. Always pronounce it with voice from your throat.

## Pronunciation of gyé

Press the flat top of your tongue against the hard roof of your mouth. Keep the tip of your tongue down behind your bottom front teeth. Release the air smoothly while using your voice. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration of your vocal cords.

## Spelling of gyé

The letter (gyé) /ɟeː/ always represents the sound /ɟ/ wherever it appears. You hear it at the end of a word in (ágy) /aːɟ/. You also hear it when it stands in other standard positions.

## Common English mistakes

Do not replace this letter with the sound in jam. The English sound starts behind the teeth and releases with friction. Press the middle of your tongue firmly against the roof of your mouth instead. Do not add a separate y sound either.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## Sound of há

The letter (há) /haː/ sounds like the start of (ház) /ˈhaːz/, which means house. This letter makes three distinct sounds in Hungarian words, and in some positions it remains completely silent.

## How to say há

Breathe out gently through an open throat without any voice. Next, make that same breathy sound while your vocal cords vibrate. For the third sound, raise the back of your tongue near the roof of your mouth to create rough friction. Put your hand on your throat to feel the voice turn on and off.

## Spelling of há

At the start of words, say the sound /h/, that is a voiceless h, as in (tehén) /ˈtɛheːn/. Between two vowels, use the sound /ɦ/, that is a voiced h, as in (lehelet) /ˈlɛɦɛlɛt/. At the end of words like (düh) /ˈdyx/, use the rough sound /x/. Finally, the letter is not pronounced at the end of certain words, such as (cseh) /ˈt͡ʃɛ/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not drop this letter at the start of words like hat. Always breathe out firmly. Do not pronounce the silent letter at the end of certain words like tea. In words that keep the ending sound, do not use the clean sound of lock. Instead, push air through a tight gap at the back of your throat.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## Sound of letter i

The name of this letter is (i) /i/. Its main sound is the sound /i/, heard in the word (itt) /ˈitː/, which means here. This letter always represents one single sound.

## How to say it

Spread your lips wide into a smile. Raise the front of your tongue high towards the roof of your mouth. Keep your jaw almost closed. Let your vocal cords vibrate freely. You can touch your throat to feel the strong buzzing.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /i/ in all positions. You can hear it at the start of the word (ing) /ˈiŋɡ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce this letter like the sound in the English word sit. Make your tongue higher and spread your lips wider, closer to the vowel in machine, but keep it very short.

articles.title: Í
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter name is (í) /iː/. It makes the long sound /iː/, as heard in the word (íz) /ˈiːz/, which means taste. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian. You hear the same pure vowel sound in every position.

## Mouth shape

Spread your lips wide into a smile. Raise the front of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Keep the air flowing steadily and let your vocal cords vibrate. Hold the vowel steady for twice as long as a short vowel. Place two fingers on your throat to feel the steady vibration throughout the sound.

## Reading the vowel

The letter with an acute accent always makes the long sound /iː/ in all positions. You read it in the word (híd) /hiːd/. You also read it the same way in the word (tíz) /tiːz/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not let this vowel glide into a y-like ending as in the English word see. Hungarian long vowels remain completely steady from start to finish. Keep your tongue high and firmly fixed in place until the sound ends. Do not shorten it, because length changes the meaning of words.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (jé) /jɛ/ has only one sound. Its main sound is /j/, as heard in the word (jó) /ˈjoː/, which means good.

## Pronunciation guide

Raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Keep your tongue close without touching the roof. Let your vocal cords vibrate as air flows smoothly out. Place a hand on your throat to feel the steady buzz.

## Reading rules

The letter always makes the sound /j/. You hear it clearly in the word (hajas) /ˈhɒjɒʃ/.

## Common pitfalls

Do not pronounce this letter like the sound in joy or the sound in jar. It sounds exactly like the first sound in yellow or yes. Keep the airflow smooth without stopping it.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## The letter ká

The letter (ká) /kaː/ has two sounds. Its basic sound is the sound /k/. You hear this in the word (kék) /ˈkeːk/, which means blue.

## How to say it

Press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly without any voice. Put your hand on your throat to feel that it does not vibrate. For the voiced sound, keep the same mouth shape. Add your voice so your throat vibrates.

## Reading this letter

This letter usually sounds like the sound /k/ before vowels and quiet consonants. You hear it in the word (kutya) /ˈkucɒ/. It becomes the sound /ɡ/ before voiced consonants like b, d or g. You hear this sound change in the word (lökdös) /ˈløɡdøʃ/.

## Common mistakes

In English, this sound comes out with a puff of air. Hold your hand before your mouth. Say key, and you feel air. In Hungarian, drop that puff completely. Make the sound crisp and dry, like the sound in skip. Never add a puff of air.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## The letter ell

The letter (ell) /ɛl/ makes the sound /l/. You hear it in the word (ló) /ˈloː/, which means horse. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian.

## Pronouncing ell

Touch the ridge behind your upper front teeth with the tip of your tongue. Let the air flow smoothly around both sides of your tongue. Vibrate your vocal cords as the air leaves your mouth. Put a hand on your throat to feel the gentle vibration.

## Spelling and variants

This letter always produces the sound /l/ in all positions. You can hear it clearly in the word (toll) /ˈtolː/.

## Avoiding mistakes

At the end of words, do not swallow this sound or lift the back of your tongue. Keep your tongue flat and forward, exactly like the first sound in the English word leaf. Never make the hollow sound heard at the end of the English word ball.

articles.title: Ly
articles.body:
## The letter elly

The letter (elly) /ɛj/ stands for the sound /j/. You hear it in the word (lyuk) /ˈjuk/, which means hole. This letter always represents one single sound.

## Pronouncing the letter

Raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Keep the tip down behind your lower front teeth. Let the air flow smoothly over your tongue with your voice on. You can feel your throat vibrate.

## Reading the letter

In modern Hungarian, this letter always makes the sound /j/. You see it in words like (gólya) /ˈɡoːjɒ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce an l sound when you see this letter. Say it exactly like the first sound in the English word yellow. Never make a rolling or sliding sound.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## Sound of emm

The name of this letter is (emm) /ɛm/. It mainly sounds like the sound /m/, as heard in (ma) /ˈmɒ/, which means today. This letter makes only one sound.

## How to say it

Close both lips firmly together. Let your vocal cords vibrate to make voice. Direct the air out through your nose. Rest a finger on your nose to feel the buzz.

## Spelling rules

This letter always produces the sound /m/ in all positions. An example is the word (alma) /ˈɒlmɒ/.

## Common mistakes

This sound matches the sound in the ordinary English word mother. There are no pitfalls for you with this consonant.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## Sound of letter enn

The name of this letter sounds like (enn) /ɛn/. Its standard pronunciation is the sound /n/, heard in the word (nap) /ˈnɒp/, which means sun or day. This letter produces two different sounds in spoken words.

## How to say enn

Press your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper front teeth. Let air flow out through your nose while your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Send the air through your nose with vibrating vocal cords. Touch your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Spelling rules for enn

In most positions, you pronounce this letter as the sound /n/, as in (anya) /ˈɒɲɒ/. It changes to the sound /ŋ/ directly before the letters k or g. You can hear this sound before a letter g in the word (hang) /ˈhɒŋɡ/. You can also hear it before a letter k in the word (bank) /ˈbɒŋk/.

## Mistakes to avoid

You might drop the following consonant after the nasal sound, as in the English word sing. Always pronounce the following consonant clearly. Do not swallow the sound at the end of a syllable. Keep your tongue pressed firmly against your teeth ridge until the sound finishes cleanly.

articles.title: Ny
articles.body:
## The letter enny

The letter (enny) /ɛɲ/ makes the sound /ɲ/. You hear it in the word (nyár) /ˈɲaːr/, which means summer. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian.

## How to say it

Press the broad middle part of your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth. Keep the tip of your tongue down behind your lower front teeth. Send air through your nose while your vocal cords vibrate. Touch your throat to feel the gentle buzz of your voice.

## Spelling rules

This letter always produces the same sound in every position. You pronounce it as the sound /ɲ/ at the start, middle, or end of a word. For example, listen to the word (anya) /ˈɒɲɒ/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not pronounce two separate sounds like the letters in the English word canyon. It is a single unified nasal sound. Make sure the middle of your tongue seals the roof of your mouth completely.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## The letter o

The letter (o) /o/ is called (o) /o/. It makes the sound /o/, like in the word (okos) /ˈokoʃ/, which means smart. This letter has only one sound.

## How to say it

Pull your tongue back and keep it mid height. Round your lips into a circle. Push your lips slightly forward. Let your voice vibrate freely without moving your jaw. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration of your vocal cords.

## When it appears

The letter (o) /o/ makes the sound /o/ in all standard positions. You hear it at the start of the word (orvos) /ˈorvoʃ/. Keep the vowel short and steady.

## Common mistakes

You might glide this vowel like in the English word go. Do not add a w sound at the end. Keep your lips still from start to finish. Make it a clean, short sound.

articles.title: Ó
articles.body:
## Sound of ó

The letter (ó) /oː/ is named (ó) /oː/. Its main sound is the sound /oː/, heard in the word (óra) /ˈoː.rɒ/, which means clock or hour. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian.

## How to say ó

Pull your tongue back and raise it halfway. Form a firm circle with your lips, pushing them forward. Let your voice vibrate steadily. Hold your mouth still so the sound stays steady. You can feel your lips stay firm and tense as you make the sound.

## Spelling of ó

This letter always makes the sound /oː/ in all positions. An example is the word (só) /ʃoː/.

## Comparing ó with English

In English words like boat or go, your lips move toward a w sound. Do not move your lips while you say this vowel. Keep your lips in a steady circle until you finish speaking.

articles.title: Ö
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The name of this letter is (ö) /ø/. It makes the sound /ø/, as in the word (öt) /øt/, which means five. This letter has only one sound in Hungarian.

## How to say it

Shape your lips into a tight circle. Keep your tongue pushed forward, near your lower teeth. Let your voice buzz smoothly. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /ø/ wherever it appears. For example, you hear it in the word (kör) /kør/.

## Common mistakes

Do not say the sound in the English word bird. Round your lips firmly, and push your tongue forward.

articles.title: Ő
articles.body:
## Letter ő sound

The letter (ő) /øː/ is called (ő) /øː/. Its main sound is the sound /øː/, heard in the word (ősz) /øːs/, which means autumn. This letter makes only one sound.

## Saying the letter ő

To make this vowel, place your tongue forward as if saying the vowel in see. Purse your lips forward into a small circle, as if saying the vowel in too. Keep your tongue steady and vibrate your vocal cords to make a long sound. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the steady buzz.

## Spelling of letter ő

This letter always produces the same long vowel sound everywhere. You will hear the sound /øː/ at the start, middle, or end of words. For example, it appears at the end of the word (erdő) /ˈɛrdøː/.

## Mistakes with letter ő

Do not replace this vowel with the sound in bird. Do not glide into another sound like the vowel in go. Shape your lips first, and hold the vowel steady without moving your mouth.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## Sound of pé

The letter name is (pé) /peː/. It usually makes the sound /p/, as in (piros) /ˈpiroʃ/, which means red. This letter can make two sounds.

## How to say pé

To make the first sound, press both lips firmly together. Stop the air completely, then release it quickly without voicing. To make the second sound, press both lips together in the same way, but vibrate your vocal cords as the air breaks through. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Spelling rules for pé

In most words, this letter makes the sound /p/, as in (apa) /ˈɒpɒ/. Before a voiced consonant, it changes into the sound /b/, as in (népdal) /ˈneːbdɒl/.

## Comparing pé

In English, the sound of p often has a strong puff of air, as in pen. In Hungarian, do not puff out extra air. Release the sound cleanly, like the p in spin.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## Letter sound kú

The name of this letter is (kú) /kuː/. Its main sound is heard in (quasi) /ˈkvɒzi/, which means quasi, as if. This letter has only one sound.

## How to say kú

Raise the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Block the air briefly, then release it sharply with no voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel no vibration.

## Reading the letter kú

This letter appears only in foreign loanwords and names, followed by the letter u. It always makes the sound /k/, as in (Aquincum) /ˈɒkviŋkum/.

## Common mistakes with kú

You might want to pronounce this letter like the sound in the English word quick. In Hungarian, the following letter u sounds like the v in vine, not like w.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## Sound of letter err

The letter is named (err) /ɛr/. Its main sound is the sound /r/, heard in the word (róka) /ˈroːkɒ/, which means fox. This letter makes only one sound in Hungarian.

## How to say it

Put the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Blow air quickly so the tip vibrates and taps against the gum. Turn on your voice to make a rolled sound. Touch your neck to feel your throat buzz.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /r/ in every position. You hear it at the start, in the middle, and at the end of words. For example, listen to the word (piros) /ˈpiroʃ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not curl your tongue back as in the English word red. Keep your tongue forward. Tap the tip against the roof behind your teeth. Make sure you do not swallow the sound at the end of a word.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## The letter ess

The letter (ess) /ɛʃ/ makes the sound /ʃ/. You hear it in the word (sárga) /ˈʃaːrɡɒ/, which means yellow. This letter always makes only one sound in Hungarian.

## Pronouncing ess

Push your lips forward a little. Raise the front of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Blow air gently through the narrow gap. Do not use your voice. Touch your throat with your hand to make sure it does not buzz.

## Spelling rules for ess

The letter (ess) /ɛʃ/ always makes the sound /ʃ/ in all standard positions. You can hear this sound clearly in the word (most) /moʃt/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce this letter like the soft sound in the English word sun. It always sounds like the quiet rushing sound in the English word ship. Round your lips slightly and push the air through.

articles.title: Sz
articles.body:
## Sound of letter essz

The letter (essz) /ɛs/ makes the sound /s/. You hear this sound in the word (szem) /ˈsɛm/, which means eye. This letter has two sounds in Hungarian speech.

## How to say essz

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth. Blow air through the narrow gap without using your voice. For the second sound, make the exact same mouth shape, but turn your voice on. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Spelling rules for essz

In regular positions, this letter makes the sound /s/, as in (tavasz) /ˈtɒvɒs/. When it stands before a voiced sound, it changes to the sound /z/. You can hear this change in the word (szembogár) /ˈzɛmboɡaːr/ and in the word (részben) /ˈreːzbɛn/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not read this letter as the sound in the English word shoe. Instead, always make the clean hiss heard in the English word sun. When it voices, do not keep the hissing sound, but let it buzz like the consonant in the English word zoo.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (té) /teː/ makes the sound /t/. You hear this sound in the word (tél) /ˈteːl/, which means winter. This letter can make two sounds.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, press your tongue tip firmly against your upper gum. Build up breath behind your tongue, then release the air suddenly without vibrating your vocal cords. For the second sound, make the exact same mouth movement, but vibrate your vocal cords. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the buzz.

## Spelling rules

In most words, this letter makes the voiceless sound /t/, as in (torta) /ˈtortɒ/. It changes to the voiced sound /d/ when it stands directly before voiced consonants, as in (hatvan) /ˈhɒdvɒn/.

## Common mistakes

In English words like table, you release a small puff of air. In Hungarian, do not puff out extra breath when you release your tongue. Keep the release sharp, dry, and tight.

articles.title: Ty
articles.body:
## Letter sound

You call this letter (tyé) /ceː/. Its main sound is the sound /c/, heard in the word (tyúk) /ˈcuːk/, which means hen. This letter has only one sound.

## How to say it

Press the middle of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Keep the tip down behind your bottom front teeth. Build air behind the tongue, then drop it cleanly away. Do not vibrate your vocal cords. Hold a finger before your lips to feel a sharp burst of breath.

## Reading rules

This letter always makes the sound /c/ everywhere in a word. You hear it inside the word (kutya) /ˈkucɒ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not say this like the first sound in cheese. That sound rubs air through teeth, while this sound is a clean stop. Do not say two separate sounds like the start of tune. Keep your tongue wide and still against the roof until you release it.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## Sound of letter u

The letter (u) /u/ is named (u) /u/. It represents the sound /u/. You hear this sound in the word (utca) /ˈut.tsɒ/, which means street. This letter makes only one sound.

## How to say u

Pull the back of your tongue high towards the roof of your mouth. Push your lips forward and make a small tight circle. Let your vocal cords vibrate as air flows out freely. Touch your throat to feel the steady buzz.

## Spelling of letter u

This letter always produces the same sound in every position. It sounds as the sound /u/ everywhere, like in the word (falu) /ˈfɒ.lu/.

## Comparing letter u

Do not pronounce this like the vowel in the English word cut. It is closer to the vowel in the English word boot. Keep your lips pushed forward into a small circle, and keep the vowel pure without gliding.

articles.title: Ú
articles.body:
## Sound of ú

The letter (ú) /uː/ is called (ú) /uː/. It makes the sound /uː/, as heard in (út) /ˈuːt/, which means road, path. This letter makes only one sound in all words.

## How to say ú

Push your tongue back toward the roof of your mouth. Round your lips tightly into a small circle. Push your lips slightly forward. Make a steady voice sound without moving your tongue or your lips. Keep your hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Spelling of ú

The accent mark over the letter shows that the sound is always held long. It sounds as /uː/ in every position, as in (húsz) /ˈhuːs/.

## Common mistakes with ú

Do not let your lips glide toward a w sound as in the English word boot. Keep your lips firmly fixed in place from start to finish. Do not shorten this sound to the quick vowel of book. Hold the vowel long and steady without changing your mouth shape.

articles.title: Ü
articles.body:
## Sound of letter ü

The name of this letter is (ü) /y/. Its main sound is the sound /y/, heard in the word (üveg) /ˈyvɛɡ/, which means glass. This letter always has one single sound.

## Saying letter ü

Push your tongue high and forward, as if making an ee sound. Now round your lips tightly into a small circle, as if whistling. Keep your tongue forward while your lips stay round. Let your voice hum steadily. You can feel your lips pushing forward firmly with your finger.

## Spelling of letter ü

This letter always makes the sound /y/ in all positions. You hear this sound clearly in the word (tűz) /tyːz/.

## Comparing letter ü

You may be tempted to use the sound in English boot. Do not pull your tongue back into your throat. Keep your tongue forward, exactly like the vowel in see, while rounding your lips.

articles.title: Ű
articles.body:
## Sound of letter ű

The letter (ű) /yː/ is called (ű) /yː/. Its main sound is the sound /yː/, heard in the word (űr) /ˈyːr/, which means space, cosmos. This letter makes only one sound.

## How to say it

Push your tongue high and forward in your mouth. Shape your lips into a tight small circle. Hold this position steady while your vocal cords vibrate. Keep the sound long and even. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the steady buzz.

## Spelling rules

This letter always keeps its one sound in every standard position. You hear the long sound /yː/ in words like (tűz) /ˈtyːz/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not replace this vowel with the sound in the English word spoon. Keep your tongue pushed forward instead of pulling it back. Do not glide into a second sound at the end. Hold the vowel pure and long.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## Letter vé

The letter name is (vé) /veː/. This letter makes the sound /v/, as in (víz) /ˈviːz/, which means water. It has only one sound in standard Hungarian.

## How to say it

Rest your upper teeth lightly on your lower lip. Push air through the small gap while using your voice. Touch your throat to feel a strong buzz. Keep the airflow smooth and continuous.

## Reading it

This letter always makes the sound /v/ in every position. For example, you hear it in the word (tavasz) /ˈtɒvɒs/.

## Common mistakes

This sound matches the English sound in voice or vine. Do not swap it with the sound in wine. Keep your top teeth touching your bottom lip so your lips do not form a circle.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## The letter name

The letter is named (dupla vé) /dupləveː/. Its main sound is the sound /v/, as in (WC) /ˈveːtseː/, which means toilet. This letter makes two sounds.

## Pronouncing the sounds

To make the first sound, place your top teeth gently against your bottom lip. Push air through while your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, round your lips tightly and pull your tongue back. Let your vocal cords vibrate as air flows smoothly out. Place your fingers on your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Reading the variants

In almost all borrowed words and common terms, this letter makes the sound /v/. You hear it in (whisky) /ˈviski/. In some newer borrowed terms or names, some people pronounce it as the sound /w/. You hear this variation in (western) /ˈvɛstɛrn/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not read this letter as the sound in water when you see foreign words. Most speakers use the sound from very instead. Press your upper teeth against your lower lip to make the right buzz.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## The letter iksz

The letter (iksz) /iks/ is pronounced with two sounds in Hungarian. Its main sound is the cluster /ks/. You hear this in the word (xilofon) /ˈksilofon/, which means xylophone.

## Pronouncing the sounds

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air without your voice, then push air through slightly open teeth. For the second sound, make that exact same combination, but vibrate your vocal cords throughout. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the strong buzz on the second sound.

## When sounds change

This letter usually sounds like the cluster /ks/. This happens at the start of words and inside borrowed words, like (taxi) /ˈtɒksi/. Between two vowels in certain borrowed words, it sounds like the cluster /ɡz/. You hear this pattern in the word (egzotikus) /ˈɛɡzotikuʃ/.

## Avoiding common errors

At the start of words, do not say a single buzzing sound like the first sound in zebra. Always begin clearly with the sound /k/ followed by the sound /s/. Also, do not drop the first sound. Say both parts crisply.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## The letter ipszilon

The letter (ipszilon) /ipsilon/ sounds like the sound /j/. You hear it in the word (yacht) /ˈjɒht/, which means yacht. This letter has two different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, lift the middle of your tongue high. Keep the tip down behind your bottom front teeth. Let air flow smoothly while your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, spread your lips wide and keep your tongue high near the roof of your mouth. Place a hand on your throat to feel the vibration.

## Where each sound occurs

In foreign loanwords, this letter represents the sound /j/ as in (yoga) /ˈjoːɡɒ/. In historical family names with traditional spelling, it represents the sound /i/ as in (Báthory) /ˈbaːtori/.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not turn the vowel sound into the glide heard in boy. Keep it steady, pure and short, like the vowel in city. When it acts as a consonant, do not add an extra vowel before it. Start directly with the tongue high, like in yes.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## Sound of letter zé

The letter (zé) /zsɛ/ makes the main sound /z/. You hear it in the word (zöld) /ˈzøld/, which means green. This letter has two sounds in total.

## How to say it

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near the bump behind your top teeth. Push air through the narrow gap. Keep your vocal cords buzzing. Put a hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration. For the second sound, make the exact same mouth shape. Turn off your voice entirely. Your throat stops buzzing.

## Spelling rules

In most positions, the letter makes its voiced sound /z/. You hear this in (zene) /ˈzɛnɛ/. The letter becomes voiceless as the sound /s/ before a silent consonant. It also sounds like /s/ at the end of a word. You can hear this sound in the word (kéz) /ˈkeːz/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the voiced sound into an unvoiced hiss between vowels. In English, this letter can sound like the soft sound in measure. Hungarian never makes that sound here. Always keep it sharp like the buzzing sound in zebra.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## The letter á

The letter (á) /a/ makes the sound /a/, heard in (água) /ˈa.ɡwɐ/, which means water. This letter can make three different sounds.

## Mouth movements

For the first sound, relax your mouth and raise the middle of your tongue slightly. For the second sound, drop your jaw wide and keep your tongue low and flat. For the third sound, keep the same mouth shape, but send the air through your nose. Place your finger beneath your nostrils to feel the warm airflow.

## Spelling positions

In unstressed syllables or before nasal consonants, you pronounce the sound /ɐ/, as in (cama) /ˈkɐ.mɐ/. In stressed open syllables, you say the sound /a/, as in (pá) /pa/. When marked by a tilde or followed by a syllable-final nasal consonant, you produce the sound /ɐ̃/, as in (canto) /ˈkɐ̃.tu/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the sound /ɐ/ like the vowel in cat. Keep your mouth less open, closer to the vowel in cup. Do not pronounce the nasal variant like an English vowel followed by an audible n sound. Keep your tongue from touching your upper gums, and send the air through your nose.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## Letter sound

This letter is called (bê) /be/. Its main sound is the sound /b/, heard in (bom) /bõ/, which means good. The letter makes two sounds in European Portuguese.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, close both lips tightly to stop the air. Release your lips with voice. For the second sound, bring both lips close together without touching. Blow air gently through the narrow gap with voice. Put your hand on your throat to feel the buzzing voice.

## Reading rules

You make the sound /b/ at the start of a word or after another consonant. You hear this sound in (ombro) /ˈõ.bɾu/. You make the softer sound /β/ between vowels in normal speech. You hear this softer sound in (cabo) /ˈka.βu/ and (saber) /sɐˈβeɾ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse the soft variant with the English sound in vine. For the English sound, your top teeth touch your lower lip. For this Portuguese sound, your teeth never touch your lip. Keep both lips close together instead.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## The letter cê

The letter (cê) /se/ has two sounds. Its main sound is the sound /k/, as in the word (casa) /ˈka.zɐ/, which means house.

## How to say cê

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Block the air, then release it sharply without voice. For the second sound, place the tip of your tongue near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Push air smoothly through the narrow gap. Put two fingers on your throat to feel that your voice stays quiet.

## Spelling rules for cê

The letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, u, or before consonants, as in (corpo) /ˈkoɾ.pu/. The letter makes the sound /s/ before the vowels e or i, as in (cedo) /ˈse.du/ and (cidade) /si.ˈda.dɨ/.

## Mistakes to avoid with cê

Do not release a puff of air when you make the sound /k/ before vowels, like in the English word cat. Keep the burst very crisp and dry. Do not turn the sound /s/ before the vowel i into the soft sound in shoe. Keep it crisp, like the sound in sun.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## Letter dê

The letter (dê) /de/ makes the sound /d/. You can hear it in (dia) /ˈdi.ɐ/, which means day. This letter has only one sound in European Portuguese.

## Making the sound

Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your top teeth. Build up a little air behind your tongue. Release the air suddenly while you make a sound with your voice. You can feel your vocal cords vibrate if you touch your throat.

## Reading this letter

This letter always makes the sound /d/. It keeps this sound at the beginning of a word and after vowels or consonants. For example, it sounds like this in (onde) /ˈõ.dɨ/.

## Avoiding mistakes

In English, you often touch the gum ridge behind your teeth to say door. In Portuguese, touch the back of your upper teeth instead. Keep your tongue further forward to avoid a heavy English sound.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter é

The letter (é) /e/ is called (é) /e/. Its most common spoken sound appears in the word (escola) /iʃˈkɔ.lɐ/, which means school. This letter can make four different vowel sounds in Portuguese.

## How to say it

For the first sound, keep your mouth almost closed and pull your tongue back. For the second sound, spread your lips wide and raise your tongue high. For the third sound, raise the middle of your tongue slightly and relax your lips. For the fourth sound, drop your jaw lower and open your mouth wide. Place your hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz throughout all four sounds.

## Spelling rules

In an unstressed syllable or at the end of a word, it sounds like /ɨ/, as in (de) /dɨ/. At the beginning of a word before the letters s or x and a consonant, it makes the sound /i/, as in (estar) /iʃˈtaɾ/. In a stressed closed syllable, it makes the sound /e/, as in (mesa) /ˈme.zɐ/. In a stressed open syllable or with an acute accent, it sounds like /ɛ/, as in (café) /kɐˈfɛ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the sound /ɨ/ like the vowel in the English word roses. Keep your mouth nearly shut and swallow the sound slightly instead. Do not say the sound /e/ like the vowel glide in day. Keep your tongue completely still so the vowel does not slide at the end.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## The letter efe

The name of this letter is (efe) /ˈɛfi/. Its main sound is heard in the word (fogo) /ˈfo.ɣu/, which means fire. This letter makes only one sound in European Portuguese.

## How to say it

Rest your upper teeth gently on your lower lip. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap. Do not use your voice. You can feel cool air on your hand, but no buzzing in your throat.

## When it sounds like this

The letter always has the same sound in all positions. You can hear it in the word (café) /kɐˈfɛ/.

## Common mistakes

This sound is identical to the English sound in fish. You will not face any real pitfall with this letter.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## Sound of letter gê

The name of this letter is (gê) /ʒe/. Its primary sound is the sound /ɡ/, heard in the word (gato) /ˈɡa.tu/, which means cat. Across Portuguese words, this letter represents two distinct sounds.

## How to say gê

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly while your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, raise the blade of your tongue near the roof of your mouth. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap with voice. Place a hand on your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Spelling rules for gê

Before the vowels a, o, u, or before another consonant, say the sound /ɡ/, as in (grande) /ˈɡɾɐ̃.dɨ/. When the letter sits right before e or i, make the sound /ʒ/, as in (gente) /ˈʒẽ.tɨ/. You also use the sound /ʒ/ before i, as in the word (girafa) /ʒiˈɾa.fɐ/.

## Comparing gê with English

Do not make the sound in bridge or gem when reading this letter before e or i. Avoid that extra pop at the beginning. Keep the airflow continuous and buzzing, exactly like the middle sound in the English word measure.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## Letter agá

The letter (agá) /aˈɡa/ has no sound of its own in European Portuguese. It is completely silent in the word (hotel) /ɔˈtɛl/, which means hotel. This letter never makes a sound when it stands alone. You always hear only the neighbouring vowel.

## How to say it

You make no sound at all. Keep your throat quiet and do not breathe out extra air. Put your hand on your throat. You feel no sound before the next vowel starts.

## Spelling rules

This letter is always silent when it stands alone. It never makes a sound at the start of a word, as in (hora) /ˈɔ.ɾɐ/. It also stays completely silent in words like (hoje) /ˈo.ʒɨ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not breathe out a puff of air as in house or hotel. You must never make that English sound in European Portuguese. Treat the word as if it begins straight with the first vowel, like honest or hour.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## The letter i

This letter is called (i) /i/. It sounds like the sound /i/ in the word (ilha) /ˈi.ʎɐ/, which means island. In European Portuguese, this letter has two sounds.

## Mouth movements

To make the first sound, spread your lips wide into a smile. Raise the front of your tongue high toward the roof of your mouth. Your vocal cords vibrate continuously. To make the second sound, push the tongue up even faster and glide instantly away. Place two fingers on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Reading rules

You hear the vowel sound /i/ when the letter forms a full syllable, as in (amigo) /ɐ.ˈmi.ɡu/. You make the quick gliding sound /j/ next to another vowel, as in (pai) /ˈpaj/ and in (viagem) /ˈvja.ʒɐ̃j̃/.

## Common mistakes

Do not shorten this vowel to the relaxed sound in the English word sit. Keep your tongue high and tense, like the sound in the English word see. When gliding, make a quick flick of the tongue.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## Sound of jota

The name of this letter sounds like (jota) /ˈʒɔtɐ/. It makes the sound /ʒ/, as heard in the word (jogo) /ˈʒo.ɣu/, meaning game. This letter has only one sound in European Portuguese. It is always reliable and never silent. Listen to the smooth buzzing air.

## How to say it

Put your tongue tip near the roof of your mouth, just behind your teeth. Push your lips slightly forward into a round shape. Blow continuous air over your tongue while turning on your vocal cords. You can feel a clear buzz when you place a hand on your throat.

## Where it appears

This letter always produces the same sound in all positions. You hear the sound /ʒ/ at the start of words like (janela) /ʒɐˈnɛ.lɐ/. It keeps the exact same voice and smooth airflow in every single position. No special accent or nearby vowel changes this rule.

## Mistakes to avoid

Do not start this letter with a hard tap like the sound in jam. It never has a stopping sound at the beginning. Do not blow breath from your throat like the Spanish sound either. Say it softly like the middle sound of measure or vision.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## The sound capa

The name of this letter is (capa) /ˈkapɐ/. It has only one sound, heard in the word (kilo) /ˈki.lu/, which means kilo or kilogram.

## Making the sound

Raise the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Block the air briefly, then release it sharply without using your voice. Place your fingers on your throat to feel that your vocal cords do not vibrate.

## Reading the letter

This letter appears only in foreign loanwords and international units of measurement. In these borrowed words, it always makes the sound /k/, as in (kit) /ˈkit/ and (karting) /ˈkaɾ.tĩŋ/.

## Sound pitfalls

This sound is just like the sound in the English word kite, but you must release less breath. Do not breathe out strongly after releasing the air from the back of your mouth.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter ele

The letter (ele) /ˈɛli/ sounds mainly like the sound /l/, that is a light l. You hear this sound in (lua) /ˈlu.ɐ/, which means moon. This letter makes two different sounds.

## How to say the letter ele

For the first sound, place the tip of your tongue against your upper gum. Let the air pass freely around the sides of your tongue. For the second sound, keep the tip there and raise the back of your tongue toward the soft roof of your mouth. Touch your throat to feel your voice box vibrate continuously.

## Spelling of the letter ele

Before a vowel, the letter makes the sound /l/, that is a light l. You can hear it in (falar) /fɐˈlaɾ/. At the end of a syllable or word, it makes the sound /ɫ/, that is a dark l. You can hear it in (alto) /ˈaɫ.tu/, and in (sol) /sɔɫ/.

## Mistakes with the letter ele

Do not drop the dark sound into a w sound like in law. Keep your tongue tip firmly on your upper gum until the sound ends. Do not use a dark sound before vowels like in full. Keep the tongue flat and light, like in the English word leaf.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## Sound of eme

The letter (eme) /ˈɛmi/ makes its main sound in the word (mão) /ˈmɐ̃w̃/, which means hand. This letter has two different sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, close both lips together. Send voiced air out through your nose. For the other sound, do not close your lips. Instead, lower the soft back of your mouth. Voiced air flows out through your nose and mouth together. Put two fingers against your nose to feel it buzz.

## Reading rules

Before a vowel or at syllable starts, it makes the sound /m/, as in (mar) /ˈmaɾ/. At the end of a syllable, it does not close your lips. It only makes the vowel nasal, like the sound /̃/ in (fim) /ˈfĩ/.

## Common mistakes

At the end of a syllable, do not close your lips. In English, you press your lips shut for the last sound in him. In Portuguese, keep your lips open and let the vowel ring through your nose.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## The letter ene

The letter (ene) /ˈɛni/ makes the sound /n/ as in (noite) /ˈnoj.tɨ/, which means night. This letter has two different sounds in European Portuguese.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, press the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Let the air flow through your nose and vibrate your vocal cords. For the other sound, do not block the air with your tongue. Drop the soft back of your mouth so air flows out through your nose. Place two fingers on your nose to feel it buzz.

## Reading the letter

Before a vowel, the letter sounds like the sound /n/ in (ano) /ˈɐ.nu/. At the end of a syllable, the letter is not pronounced on its own. Instead, it turns the vowel before it into a nasal sound, as in (canto) /ˈkɐ̃.tu/ and (ponte) /ˈpõ.tɨ/.

## Avoiding mistakes

At the end of a syllable, do not tap your tongue tip like in the English word tent. Keep your tongue low and let the air escape freely through your nose.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## Letter ó

The letter (ó) /ɔ/ takes its name from its open sound. Its main sound is heard in the word (olho) /ˈɔ.ʎu/, which means eye. This letter makes four different sounds in European Portuguese.

## Pronouncing the letter

For the first sound, round your lips tightly and pull your tongue back. For the second sound, open your mouth wider and round your lips loosely. For the third sound, close your mouth slightly more and push your lips forward. For the fourth sound, keep that close shape and let the air escape through your nose. Place a hand on your throat to feel continuous vibration.

## Spelling rules

In unstressed syllables, this letter makes the sound /u/, as in (amigo) /ɐˈmi.ɡu/. In stressed syllables with an open vowel, it makes the sound /ɔ/, as in (avó) /ɐˈvɔ/. In stressed syllables with a closed vowel, it gives the sound /o/, that is, a close vowel, as in (boca) /ˈbo.kɐ/. Before the letters m, n, or with a tilde, it produces the sound /õ/, as in (bom) /bõ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the stressed close vowel into a gliding sound like the vowel in boat. Keep your tongue completely still until the sound ends. In unstressed endings, avoid saying an open vowel like the sound in lot. Always round your lips tightly for that unstressed vowel.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter pê

The letter (pê) /pe/ makes the sound /p/. You hear it in the word (pão) /ˈpɐ̃w̃/, which means bread. This letter makes two sounds.

## How to say pê

Press your lips tightly together and block the air. Release your lips cleanly without adding a breath. Keep your vocal cords still for this first sound. For the second sound, press your lips together in the same spot. Make your vocal cords vibrate as you let the air escape. Put your hand on your throat to feel that vibration.

## Spelling of pê

In regular positions, this letter gives the sound /p/. You hear it in (pai) /ˈpaj/ and in (copo) /ˈkɔ.pu/. In quick speech before a voiced consonant, it shifts to the sound /b/. That happens in the word (subepático) /su.bɛ.ˈpa.ti.ku/.

## Comparing pê with English

In English words like pen, you release a small puff of air. In Portuguese, you must avoid that puff completely. Hold a finger before your lips. The air must not move your finger when you release the sound.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## Sound of quê

The letter (quê) /ke/ mainly makes the sound /kw/, like in the word (quatro) /ˈkwa.tɾu/, which means four. This letter has two different sounds in European Portuguese.

## How to say it

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air sharply while you round your lips into a tight circle. For the second sound, release the air without rounding your lips. Place a hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords stay still.

## Reading and writing

This letter always appears with the vowel u. Before the letters a or o, it sounds like /kw/, as in (quase) /ˈkwa.zɨ/. Before the letters e or i, the following vowel u stays silent, so the letter makes the sound /k/, as in (que) /kɨ/ and (aqui) /ɐˈki/.

## Common mistakes

Do not add a w sound when the letter stands before e or i. English words like quick always keep that sound. In Portuguese, keep the second letter silent so it sounds like the k in keep.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## Letter sound erre

The letter (erre) /ˈɛʁi/ mainly makes the sound /ʁ/, as in the word (rua) /ˈʁu.ɐ/, which means street. In European Portuguese, this letter can make two distinct sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue near the soft roof of your mouth. Let the air scrape gently past while your voice hums. For the second sound, tap the tip of your tongue once quickly against the ridge behind your upper front teeth. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz during both sounds.

## Spelling and sounds

At the start of a word, this letter makes the sound /ʁ/, as in (carro) /ˈka.ʁu/. Between two vowels, it makes the tapped sound /ɾ/, as in (caro) /ˈka.ɾu/. At the end of a syllable, it also makes the sound /ɾ/, as in (porta) /ˈpɔɾ.tɐ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not roll your tongue tip like the Spanish sound. Do not curl your tongue backward like the sound in the English word red. Keep your tongue flat for the back sound, or tap it once quickly against your upper gum for the light tap.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## Sound of esse

The letter (esse) /ˈɛsi/ makes the sound /s/ in the word (sol) /ˈsɔɫ/, which means sun. This letter has four different sounds in European Portuguese. Each sound depends on the position in the word and the letters around it.

## How to say esse

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth. Blow air through the narrow gap without voice. For the second sound, keep the same mouth shape, but turn your voice on. For the third sound, pull your tongue back and push air forward softly. For the fourth sound, use that back shape with your voice turned on. Touch your throat to feel the buzzing sounds.

## Spelling rules for esse

At the start of a word, it sounds like /s/, as in (sapo) /ˈsa.pu/. Doubled between vowels, it also makes the sound /s/, as in (passo) /ˈpa.su/. A single letter between vowels makes the sound /z/, as in (casa) /ˈka.zɐ/. At the end of a syllable before an unvoiced consonant, it sounds like /ʃ/, as in (festa) /ˈfɛʃ.tɐ/. At the very end of a word, it also makes /ʃ/, as in (português) /puɾ.tuˈɡeʃ/. Before a voiced consonant, it sounds like /ʒ/, as in (mesmo) /ˈmeʒ.mu/.

## Common mistakes with esse
