You might want to pronounce the final letter as the sound in bus. Do not do that. Make the sound of ship instead. Before a voiced consonant, you might make the sound in zoo. Instead, make the buzzing sound found in the middle of vision.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Sound of letter tê

The name of this letter is (tê) /te/. It makes one single sound, heard in (tempo) /ˈtẽ.pu/, meaning time or weather.

## How to say it

Touch the back of your upper front teeth with the tip of your tongue. Stop the air completely for a brief moment. Release the tongue cleanly without puffing out a breath of air. Keep your vocal cords silent. You can hold your hand before your mouth to feel no burst of air.

## Reading rules

This letter always makes the sound /t/ in every position. You hear it at the end of (noite) /ˈnoj.tɨ/.

## Common mistakes

In English words like tea, you puff out air. Keep your breath back completely. Never turn this sound into the ch sound in cheap when an e follows. Place the tongue tip strictly against your upper teeth.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## The letter u

You call this letter (u) /u/. Its main sound is the sound /ˈũ/, heard in (um) /ˈũ/, which means one, a. This letter has three different sounds.

## How to say u

For the first sound, pull your tongue back and push your lips forward into a small circle. For the second sound, make that same shape very quickly and glide into the next vowel. For the third sound, keep the same mouth shape, but let air escape through your nose. Feel your throat buzz with each sound.

## Spelling rules for u

This letter makes the sound /u/ when stressed or before vowels, as in (uva) /ˈu.vɐ/. It makes the gliding sound /w/ when joined with another vowel, as in (mau) /ˈmaw/. Before nasal consonants in the same syllable, it makes the nasal sound /ˈũ/, as in (junto) /ˈʒũ.tu/.

## Common mistakes with u

Do not add a y sound before the vowel, like in the English word music. Make a pure vowel instead, like in goose. Do not make the vowel too long, like in moon. Push your lips firmly into a small circle, and keep the vowel steady and short.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## Letter sound vê

The name of this letter is (vê) /ve/. It makes the sound /v/, as in (verde) /ˈveɾ.dɨ/, which means green. This letter has only one sound in European Portuguese.

## How to say it

Rest your upper teeth gently on your lower lip. Blow air through the gap while your voice box buzzes. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## Spelling rules

This letter always makes the sound /v/ in every position. You hear it at the start of a word in (vida) /ˈvi.dɐ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse this sound with the sound /b/. Never press your two lips together. Keep your upper teeth on your bottom lip, exactly like the sound in the English word vine.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## Letter sound dáblio

The letter (dáblio) /ˈdabliu/ sounds like the sound /w/ in (web) /ˈwɛb/, meaning web. This letter only appears in foreign loanwords. It has two sounds in European Portuguese.

## Mouth movements

To make the first sound, purse your lips into a tight circle. Raise the back of your tongue and let your voice hum. For the second sound, touch your upper teeth to your lower lip. Blow air gently through the gap while your voice hums. You can feel your throat vibrate for both sounds.

## Spelling rules

In borrowed words from English, the letter makes the sound /w/, as in (whisky) /ˈwiʃki/. In borrowed words from German or older traditional loanwords, the letter makes the sound /v/, as in (watt) /ˈvat/.

## Common mistakes

Do not swap the two sounds in borrowed words. In English words, shape your lips into a circle instead of touching your teeth, like in water. In German words, place your top front teeth against your lower lip, like in vine. Check the origin of the word to choose the right sound.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (xis) /ʃis/ is called (xis) /ʃis/. Its main sound is the sound /ʃ/, as in the word (xadrez) /ʃɐˈdɾeʃ/, which means chess. This letter can make four different sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, push your lips forward and blow gently without voice. For the second sound, rest your tongue tip behind your upper teeth and hum. For the third sound, blow air through your closed front teeth without your voice. For the fourth sound, stop the airflow briefly and release it into a hiss. Feel your vocal cords buzz only on the second sound.

## Reading rules

At the start of a word or after two vowels together, say the sound /ʃ/, as in (caixa) /ˈkaj.ʃɐ/. When the prefix ex comes before a vowel, make the sound /z/, as in (exame) /iˈzɐ.mɨ/. In words like (próximo) /ˈpɾɔ.si.mu/, pronounce the sound /s/. In learned words between vowels, say the sound /ks/, as in (táxi) /ˈta.ksi/.

## Common mistakes

Do not always pronounce this letter as the sound in box. At the start of words, use the soft hush of shoe instead. In common prefix words, avoid the sharp hiss of snake and use the buzzing hum of zero. Keep your tongue relaxed so you do not add extra vowel sounds.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## The letter ípsilon

The letter (ípsilon) /ˈipsilõ/ makes the sound /j/ as in the word (yoga) /ˈjɔ.ɡɐ/, which means yoga. This letter is rare and comes from foreign words. It can make two different sounds in European Portuguese.

## Pronouncing ípsilon

To make the first sound, lift your tongue high toward the roof of your mouth. Glide quickly into the next vowel while your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, smile slightly and hold your tongue high and forward without moving. Touch your throat to feel the steady vibration of your voice.

## Spelling rules for ípsilon

This letter sounds like /j/ next to another vowel, as heard in (playboy) /plɐjˈbɔj/. It sounds like the pure vowel /i/ when it stands on its own in borrowed names, as in (Sydney) /ˈsid.nej/.

## Common mistakes

Do not let this letter turn into an open English vowel sound like the first part of nylon. Keep the sound tight and clear like the start of yes or the vowel of machine.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## The letter zê

The letter is named (zê) /ze/. Its primary value is the sound /z/, heard in (zebra) /ˈze.βɾɐ/, which means zebra. This letter has three distinct sounds in European Portuguese.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, place your tongue close to your upper gum. Push air out while vibrating your vocal cords. For the second sound, pull your tongue slightly back and round your lips softly. Blow air gently without using your voice. For the third sound, keep the same mouth shape, but turn your voice on. You can feel your throat vibrate with your hand.

## Reading the letter

At the beginning of a word or between vowels, it makes the sound /z/, as in (fazer) /fɐˈzeɾ/. At the end of a word before a pause, it makes the sound /ʃ/, as in (paz) /paʃ/. Before an unvoiced consonant, it also makes the sound /ʃ/, as in (luz clara) /luʃ ˈkla.ɾɐ/. Finally, before a voiced consonant, it makes the sound /ʒ/, as in (luz divina) /luʒ diˈvi.nɐ/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not pronounce word endings with the buzzing sound in buzz. When a word ends before a pause, use the quiet sound in shoe instead. Before a voiced consonant, switch smoothly to the softer sound in vision.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## Sound of A

You call this letter (A) /eɪ/. Its main sound is the vowel in (apple) /æ.pəl/, which means an apple. This letter has four different sounds.

## Pronouncing A

For the first sound, drop your jaw low, widen your lips, and push your tongue forward. Next, glide from a middle vowel upward, moving your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Then, relax your entire mouth completely to make a quick, weak vowel. Finally, open your mouth wide and keep your tongue low and flat. Feel your throat vibrate with your fingers for all four sounds.

## Spelling of A

In a closed syllable with stress, you say the sound /æ/ as in (cat) /kæt/. In an open syllable or before a consonant with silent e, say the sound /eɪ/ as in (make) /meɪk/. In an unstressed syllable, use the weak sound /ə/ as in (sofa) /soʊ.fə/. Before certain consonants like r or lm, say the deep sound /ɑː/ as in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

## Common Mistakes

Do not replace the wide sound /æ/ with a simple vowel like the one in (calm) /kɑːm/. Drop your jaw lower and spread your lips wider. Do not stress the weak sound /ə/ at the end of a word. Keep that final sound very short and relaxed.
articles.summary: Letter name: A. Example: apple.

articles.title: B
articles.body:
## Sound of letter B

The letter (B) /biː/ makes the sound /b/. You hear it in the word (bed) /bɛd/, which means bed. This letter has one main spoken sound, but sometimes it makes no sound at all.

## How to say it

Close both lips firmly to stop the air. Release your lips quickly and use your voice. You can feel your throat vibrate when you touch your neck with two fingers.

## Reading and spelling rules

In most words, this letter makes the sound /b/. For example, you hear it at the end of (cab) /kæb/. The letter is silent when it sits right before the letter t, as in (doubt) /daʊt/. It is also silent after the letter m in the same syllable, as in (climb) /klaɪm/.

## Common mistakes to avoid

Do not confuse the voiced sound /b/ with the quiet sound /p/. For the sound /b/, always turn on your voice. If your throat does not buzz, you are making the wrong sound.
articles.summary: Letter name: B. Example: book.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## The letter C

The letter (C) /siː/ makes the sound /k/, as in (cat) /kæt/. A (cat) /kæt/ is a small furry pet. This letter has two different sounds.

## Making the sounds

Lift the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release a quick puff of quiet air. For the next sound, touch your upper side teeth with your tongue. Push air smoothly across the tongue tip without using your voice. Hold a finger before your lips to feel the steady breeze.

## Spelling rules

Before the letters a, o, u or consonants, this letter sounds like /k/, as in (cup) /kʌp/. Before the letters e, i, or y, it makes the sound /s/, as in (city) /sɪt.i/.

## Common mistakes

Do not add voice to the sound /k/. A hand on your throat should feel no vibration at all. Also, do not stop the airflow when you make the sound /s/. Let the air hiss continuously.
articles.summary: Letter name: C. Example: city.

articles.title: D
articles.body:
## Letter D sound

The letter (D) /diː/ makes the sound /d/. You hear it in the word (dog) /dɒɡ/, which means dog. The letter makes four different sounds in English words.

## How to say D

To make the first sound, place your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Stop the air briefly, release it quickly, and vibrate your vocal cords. For the second sound, make the same quick release with no voice. For the third sound, press your tongue flat behind your teeth, then pull it back as your voice buzzes. Touch your throat to feel the voice buzz.

## Spelling rules for D

Usually, this letter makes the sound /d/, as in (bed) /bɛd/. In regular past tense endings after a voiceless consonant, it sounds like /t/, as in (hoped) /həʊpt/. Before the letter u in certain words, it makes the sound /dʒ/, as in (educate) /ɛ.dʒʊ.keɪt/. In a few special words, the letter is silent and makes no sound at all, as in (handkerchief) /hæŋ.kə.tʃiːf/.

## Common mistakes with D

Do not turn the voiced sound into an unvoiced stop at the end of words. Keep your vocal cords vibrating so the ending does not sound like a sharp tap. In special words where the letter is silent, do not pronounce it at all.
articles.summary: Letter name: D. Example: dog.

articles.title: E
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter E

The letter (E) /iː/ sounds like /ɛ/ in the word (egg) /ɛɡ/. This word means egg. The letter has four different sounds across English words.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, open your mouth slightly and keep your tongue forward. For the second sound, smile widely and raise your tongue high near the roof. For the third sound, relax your tongue and lips completely in the middle. The fourth variant makes no sound at all. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz on all three spoken sounds.

## Spelling rules

In closed syllables with a consonant after, you make the sound /ɛ/ as in (bed) /bɛd/. In open stressed syllables, you make the long sound /iː/ as in (me) /miː/. In unstressed syllables, you use the weak sound /ə/ as in (problem) /prɒb.ləm/. Finally, the letter is not pronounced at the end of a word like (take) /teɪk/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse the short sound with the sound in cat. Keep your jaw closer to your teeth and do not drop it too low. Also, never say a sound at the end of words when the letter sits silent. Keep your lips still at the finish.
articles.summary: Letter name: E. Example: energy.

articles.title: F
articles.body:
## Sound of F

The letter (F) /ef/ makes the sound /f/, as in the word (fish) /fɪʃ/. This word means a creature that swims in water. This letter can make two different sounds in English words.

## How to Say F

Gently place your top teeth on your bottom lip. Blow air smoothly through the small gap between them. Do not use your voice for this sound. Place your hand on your neck to check for no vibrations. For the voiced sound, keep the same mouth shape, but make a steady humming sound with your voice.

## Reading F

In almost every English word, this letter sounds like /f/. You can hear this sound at the beginning of the word (fast) /fæst/. You also hear this sound at the end of the word (leaf) /liːf/. The main exception is one very common small word. In the word (of) /əv/, this letter sounds like the voiced sound /v/.

## Common Mistakes

Do not close both lips together when you make this sound. Keep your top teeth lightly touching your lower lip so air flows freely. Do not confuse this sound with the sound /p/ or the sound /b/. Remember to turn off your voice when you say the regular sound.
articles.summary: Letter name: F. Example: family.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## Sound of G

The letter (G) /dʒiː/ usually makes the sound /ɡ/, like in (gas) /ɡæs/, meaning gas. This letter has three spoken sounds in English, and it can also be silent.

## How to say G

To make the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly and make a sound with your throat. For the second sound, press your tongue behind your front teeth, push air through, and use your voice. For the third sound, push your lips out, keep the air flowing steadily, and vibrate your vocal cords. Touch your throat to feel the vibration.

## Spelling rules for G

You use the sound /ɡ/ before the vowels a, o, or u, before consonants, and at the end of words, as in (dog) /dɒɡ/. The sound /dʒ/ often appears before the vowels e, i, or y, as in (gem) /dʒɛm/ and (giant) /dʒaɪ.ənt/. Words borrowed from French use the sound /ʒ/ before e or i, such as (regime) /reɪ.ʒiːm/ and (genre) /ʒɒn.rə/. The letter is silent before n or m, as seen in (sign) /saɪn/ and (gnat) /næt/.

## Common mistakes with G

Do not drop the voice when you say the hard sound at the end of words. Keep your vocal cords buzzing so it does not sound like a k. When you say the soft sound, make sure your tongue touches the roof of your mouth first. Do not glide softly into it. Finally, remember to keep the letter completely silent when it stands directly before the letter n.
articles.summary: Letter name: G. Example: garden.

articles.title: H
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (H) /eɪtʃ/ makes the sound /h/. You hear it in the word (hat) /hæt/, which means a hat. This letter makes one spoken sound, but sometimes stays completely quiet.

## Mouth movements

Open your mouth slightly. Keep your tongue relaxed low in your mouth. Push air gently up from your throat. Do not vibrate your vocal cords. Hold a hand before your lips to feel a soft puff of warm air.

## Spelling rules

This letter makes the sound /h/ at the start of a syllable before a vowel, as in (help) /hɛlp/. In a few words, the letter is not pronounced at all at the start, as in (hour) /aʊ.ər/ and (honest) /ɒn.ɪst/.

## Common mistakes

Do not drop the breath at the start of words. Push a soft puff of air so you do not say words with an open vowel. Do not scrape your throat tightly. Keep the air flow gentle and smooth.
articles.summary: Letter name: H. Example: house.

articles.title: I
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (I) /aɪ/ makes several different vowel sounds. Its main sound is the short vowel /ɪ/, as in the word (ink) /ɪŋk/. In English, this letter has four common sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, open your mouth slightly and keep your tongue relaxed and high. For the second sound, open wide, then glide your tongue up toward your roof. For the third sound, smile widely and push your tongue forward and high. For the last sound, relax your whole mouth completely and make a quick, weak murmur. Put a hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz for all four.

## Reading rules

In a closed syllable with consonants after it, this letter makes the sound /ɪ/, as in (pin) /pɪn/. In an open syllable or before a silent e, you say the sound /aɪ/, as in (ice) /aɪs/ or (time) /taɪm/. In borrowed words or special endings, it makes the long sound /iː/, as in (ski) /skiː/ or (police) /pə.liːs/. In weak, unstressed syllables, it turns into the relaxed sound /ə/, as in (pencil) /pen.səl/ or (possible) /pɒs.ə.bəl/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse the short sound /ɪ/ with the long sound in beat. Keep your mouth relaxed and short, not smiling and tense. Also, do not turn the quick, weak sound /ə/ into a clear vowel. Keep unstressed syllables short and soft.
articles.summary: Letter name: I. Example: idea.

articles.title: J
articles.body:
## Sound of letter J

The letter (J) /dʒeɪ/ usually makes the sound /dʒ/. You hear it in the word (jam) /dʒæm/, which means sweet fruit spread. This letter has four sounds in English words. Most everyday words use only the first sound. Borrowed words can use the other three sounds.

## How to say letter J

For the main sound, press the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Push air through while your voice box vibrates. For the second sound, breathe air gently out through an open throat. For the third sound, raise the middle of your tongue near the roof of your mouth. For the fourth sound, push air smoothly across your tongue. Touch your throat to feel the voice buzzing.

## Spelling of letter J

In regular English words, this letter makes the sound /dʒ/, as in (job) /dʒɒb/. In words borrowed from Spanish, it makes the sound /h/, as in (jalapeño) /hæ.lə.peɪ.njoʊ/. In words from German or northern languages, it makes the sound /j/, as in (hallelujah) /hæ.lə.luː.jə/. In words taken from French, it makes the sound /ʒ/, as in (bijou) /biː.ʒuː/.

## Common mistakes with letter J

Many learners use the sound /j/ from yes instead of the main sound /dʒ/. Do not slide softly into the vowel. Block the air behind your top teeth first, then release it with a strong burst. Other learners make the soft sound /ʒ/ without stopping the air. Make sure your tongue presses firmly against the roof of your mouth before you let the air out.
articles.summary: Letter name: J. Example: job.

articles.title: K
articles.body:
## Letter sound

You call this letter (K) /keɪ/. It mainly sounds like the sound /k/, as heard in (kite) /kaɪt/. This word means a light toy that flies in the wind. This letter has one sound, and it can also stay silent.

## Pronunciation guide

Press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Stop the air for a moment. Then let the air burst out quickly without using your voice. Place your fingers on your throat. You will feel no buzz at all.

## Spelling patterns

This letter usually gives the sound /k/ at the start, middle, or end of a word, as in (milk) /mɪlk/. When it stands before the letter n at the start of a word, it stays silent, as in (knee) /niː/.

## Common mistakes

Learners often try to pronounce the silent letter before n. In words like (knot) /nɒt/, do not say any sound before the sound /n/. Let your tongue begin straight on the roof of your mouth.
articles.summary: Letter name: K. Example: key.

articles.title: L
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (L) /el/ makes the sound /l/ in the word (lamp) /læmp/, which means lamp. This letter makes one spoken sound, but sometimes stays completely quiet.

## How to say it

Press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your top teeth. Let the air flow smoothly around the sides of your tongue. Use your voice. Touch your throat to feel a strong buzz. When this sound comes after a vowel, raise the back of your tongue slightly toward the roof of your mouth.

## Spelling rules

This letter usually makes the sound /l/, like in the word (milk) /mɪlk/. It stays quiet before certain consonants in a few common words, like in the word (calm) /kɑːm/ and the word (salmon) /sæ.mən/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace the sound at the end of a word with a vowel sound like in tool. Keep the tip of your tongue firmly against the roof of your mouth until the sound ends completely.
articles.summary: Letter name: L. Example: language.

articles.title: M
articles.body:
## Letter sound

You call this letter (M) /em/. Its main sound is the sound /m/, as heard in (milk) /mɪlk/. This word means milk. The letter has two sounds across English words.

## How to say it

Close your lips completely and let air flow smoothly through your nose. Turn on your voice so your throat vibrates. You can place two fingers gently on your neck to feel the vibration.

## Spelling rules

In most positions, you pronounce the sound /m/, like in the word (map) /mæp/. When placed before the letter n at the start of a word, this letter is not pronounced, like in (mnemonic) /nə.mɒn.ɪk/.

## Common mistakes

Learners sometimes open their lips too soon at the end of a word. Keep your lips closed firmly until the humming sound stops completely. This letter causes very few problems.
articles.summary: Letter name: M. Example: music.

articles.title: N
articles.body:
## Sound of N

The letter (N) /en/ makes the sound /n/ in the word (net) /nɛt/. This word means a net. This letter can make two different sounds, or it can be silent.

## How to say it

Press the tip of your tongue against the roof of your mouth, just behind your top teeth. Let the air flow through your nose and use your voice. For the other sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz.

## Spelling patterns

In most words, this letter makes the sound /n/, as in (sun) /sʌn/. It makes the back nose sound /ŋ/ before the sounds k or g, as in (sink) /sɪŋk/. At the end of a word after the letter m, this letter is silent, as in (autumn) /ɔ.təm/.

## Common mistakes

Do not let air escape through your mouth when you make this sound. Keep your tongue firmly in place so all the air goes through your nose. Do not pronounce this letter at the end of a word after m, as in (hymn) /hɪm/. Say only the m sound at the end.
articles.summary: Letter name: N. Example: name.

articles.title: O
articles.body:
## Letter sound O

The name of the letter is (O) /oʊ/. Its main sound is the vowel /ɑ/, heard in the word (ox) /ɑks/, which means an ox. This letter has four sounds in total.

## How to say O

For the first sound, drop your jaw low, keep your tongue flat, and make a voiced sound. For the second sound, start with your lips open, then round them into a small circle. For the third sound, relax your tongue and lips completely and make a quick weak voice sound. For the fourth sound, push your lips forward tightly and pull your tongue back. Feel your vocal cords vibrate for each sound.

## Spelling rules for O

In a closed syllable with stress, this letter makes the sound /ɑ/, as in (hot) /hɑt/. At the end of an open syllable or before a silent e, it makes the sound /oʊ/, as in (go) /ɡoʊ/ or (home) /hoʊm/. In an unstressed syllable, it becomes the weak sound /ə/, as in (lemon) /lɛ.mən/ and (atom) /æ.təm/. In several common words, it sounds like /uː/, as in (do) /duː/ and (move) /muːv/.

## Common mistakes with O

Do not keep your lips completely still when you make the sound /oʊ/. Move your lips into a tight circle at the end. For the sound /ɑ/, open your mouth wider and drop your jaw lower than you might expect. For the weak sound /ə/, make the vowel very short and quiet.
articles.summary: Letter name: O. Example: open.

articles.title: P
articles.body:
## Sound of P

The letter name is (P) /piː/. It usually makes the sound /p/, as in the word (pen) /pɛn/, which means pen. This letter has two sounds across English words.

## Mouth movements

Close both lips together firmly to stop the breath completely. Let air build up behind them, then open your lips quickly with a small burst of air. Keep your vocal cords still so your throat does not vibrate. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel the quick puff of air.

## Reading rules

In most words, this letter makes the sound /p/ at the beginning, middle, or end, as in (cup) /kʌp/. In some words, this letter is silent and makes no sound at all, as in (cupboard) /kʌ.bəd/ and (corps) /kɔː/.

## Common mistakes

Do not voice this consonant like the sound in bad. Keep your throat quiet so it does not sound like a different letter. At the start of words, do not forget the small burst of air.
articles.summary: Letter name: P. Example: people.

articles.title: Q
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (Q) /kjuː/ usually represents a single basic sound. It makes the sound /k/ as in the word (qat) /kæt/, which means a khat plant. On its own, this letter has one main sound.

## Mouth movements

Raise the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Stop the air completely. Release the air suddenly without using your voice. Place a hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords do not vibrate.

## Spelling rules

On its own without the letter u in loanwords, it makes the sound /k/. An example is the word (qi) /tʃiː/.

## Common mistakes

Speakers sometimes add an extra sound when this letter stands alone. Do not add a w sound after the burst of air. Keep the sound /k/ crisp and short, just like the sound of the letter k in the common English word kite.
articles.summary: Letter name: Q. Example: question.

articles.title: R
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (R) /ɑːr/ makes the sound /r/ in the word (red) /rɛd/, which means red. This letter has one spoken consonant sound and one silent pattern.

## Pronouncing the letter

Curl the tip of your tongue slightly up and back. Do not touch the roof of your mouth. Keep the sides of your tongue against your upper back teeth. Turn on your voice and let the smooth air flow. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the strong buzz.

## Reading the letter

Before a vowel sound, read this letter as the sound /r/ in the word (run) /rʌn/. At the end of a word, or before another consonant, many speakers do not pronounce the letter at all. In that position, the letter is completely silent, as in the word (car) /kɑː/ or the word (hard) /hɑːd/.

## Avoiding mistakes

Do not roll or tap your tongue against your teeth. Keep your tongue back inside your mouth. Do not let your tongue touch anywhere near the front. If you make a tapping sound, pull your tongue tip down and back.
articles.summary: Letter name: R. Example: around.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## Sound of S

You call this letter (S) /es/. It mostly sounds like (sun) /sʌn/, which means the bright star in our day sky. This letter makes four different sounds in English words.

## How to say S

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near the bump behind your top teeth. Push air through the small gap without your voice. For the second sound, make that exact same air stream and turn your voice on. Feel your throat buzz. For the third sound, pull your tongue slightly back and round your lips while your voice hums. For the fourth sound, keep that same mouth shape and turn your voice off.

## Spelling of S

At the start of words or before quiet sounds, the letter makes the sound /s/, as in (stop) /stɒp/. Between vowels or after loud voiced sounds, it sounds like /z/, as in (rose) /roʊz/. When it sits before the endings ion or ual after a vowel, it makes the sound /ʒ/, like in (vision) /vɪ.ʒən/. Before ure or in special common words, it sounds like /ʃ/, as in (sugar) /ʃʊɡ.ər/.

## Mistakes with S

Learners often make a quiet hissing sound when the letter should buzz like a bee. Do not say the sound /s/ when the letter sits between two vowels. Make sure your vocal cords vibrate, just like the sound in the word zoo. Another common error is adding an extra vowel sound right before the letter at the start of a word. Start cleanly with pure air.
articles.summary: Letter name: S. Example: sun.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Sound of T

The letter (T) /tiː/ makes the sound /t/, that is a crisp burst of air. You hear this sound in the word (ten) /tɛn/, which means the number ten. This letter makes three sounds in English speech.

## How to say T

For the first sound, press your tongue tip behind your upper teeth. Release the air sharply without your vocal cords. For the second sound, tap your tongue tip very quickly against the roof of your mouth. Keep your voice on during this quick tap. You can feel a quick puff of air on your fingers during the first sound.

## Spelling of T

At the start of words and in stressed beats, you say the sound /t/, that is a crisp burst of air, as in (top) /tɒp/. Between two vowels before a light beat, you tap quickly with the sound /ɾ/, that is a quick tongue tap, as in (water) /wɔː.tər/. In words like (listen) /lɪs.ən/, the letter stays completely silent.

## Comparing T

Do not press your tongue flat against your front teeth. Touch the ridge just behind your top teeth instead. Do not hum with your throat on the first sound. Keep that sound sharp and voiceless. When you tap between vowels, do not stop the flow of sound entirely.
articles.summary: Letter name: T. Example: table.

articles.title: U
articles.body:
## The letter U

The letter (U) /juː/ usually makes the sound /ʌ/, as in the word (up) /ʌp/. This word means toward a higher place. This letter makes four sounds in English words.

## How to say it

For the first sound, keep your mouth open and let your tongue rest flat. For the next sound, lift your tongue and circle your lips tight. For the third sound, push your lips into a tight ring. For the last sound, keep your lips loose and slightly curved. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz for all four sounds.

## Spelling rules

In closed syllables, you say the sound /ʌ/, as in the word (cup) /kʌp/. In open syllables or before one consonant and silent e, you say /juː/, as in (music) /mjuː.zɪk/ or (cube) /kjuːb/. After r, l, or j, or before silent e, you say /uː/, as in (rule) /ruːl/ or (flute) /fluːt/. In special closed syllables, you say /ʊ/, as in (put) /pʊt/ or (full) /fʊl/.

## Common mistakes

Do not make the mouth too wide for the short vowel, or it sounds wrong. Keep your jaw relaxed. Do not forget to slide from a quick y sound into the long vowel when required. Do not push your tongue forward on the deeper sounds. Keep your tongue relaxed inside your mouth.
articles.summary: Letter name: U. Example: use.

articles.title: V
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter vee

The letter (V) /viː/ makes the sound /v/. You hear it in the word (van) /væn/, which means a van. This letter makes only one sound in English.

## How to say it

Rest your upper teeth gently on your lower lip. Push air out steadily while using your voice. You can feel your throat buzz with your fingers.

## Reading the letter

This letter always makes the sound /v/. It appears in words like (river) /rɪv.ər/.

## Common mistakes

Do not press your two lips together as in win. Make sure your top teeth touch your lower lip. Do not whisper the sound as in fan. Keep your voice buzzing continuously.
articles.summary: Letter name: V. Example: voice.

articles.title: W
articles.body:
## Letter sound double u

You call this letter (W) /dʌbəl.juː/. Its main sound is the sound /w/, like in the word (wet) /wɛt/. That word means wet. This letter has one sound, or it stays silent.

## Pronouncing double u

To make the sound /w/, round your lips tightly into a small circle. Pull the back of your tongue up toward the roof of your mouth. Let your vocal cords vibrate as air flows out. Place your hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration. Do not touch your teeth with your lips.

## Reading double u

You pronounce this letter as the sound /w/ before a vowel, like in (win) /wɪn/. This letter stays completely silent before the letter r, like in (write) /raɪt/. It also stays silent in some special words, like in (two) /tuː/.

## Avoiding common mistakes

Do not confuse the sound /w/ with the sound /v/. Never touch your lower lip to your upper teeth. Keep your lips apart and push them forward into a circle. If your teeth touch your lip, you make the wrong sound.
articles.summary: Letter name: W. Example: window.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## Sound of letter X

You call this letter (X) /eks/. It usually makes the sound /ks/, as in (box) /bɒks/, which means box. This letter can make three different sounds.

## How to say X

Lift the back of your tongue, release a burst of air, then blow air through your teeth. For the next sound, repeat this while buzzing your vocal cords. For the last sound, keep your tongue tip near your upper teeth and buzz your voice. Touch your throat to feel the buzz.

## Spelling rules for X

At the end of a syllable or word, it sounds like /ks/, as in (six) /sɪks/. It makes the sound /ɡz/ between vowels before a stressed syllable, as in (exam) /ɪɡ.zæm/. At the start of a word, it sounds like /z/, as in (xylophone) /zaɪ.lə.fəʊn/.

## Common mistakes with X

Do not drop the first stop sound at the end of a word. Make sure you do not say two sounds at the start of a word. Start words with a plain buzz, just like the sound in zoo.
articles.summary: Letter name: X. Example: example.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## Letter Y sound

The letter (Y) /waɪ/ mainly sounds like /j/, as in (yes) /jɛs/, which means yes. This letter makes four sounds in English words.

## How to say Y

For the first sound, lift your tongue high near the roof of your mouth. Push voiced air smoothly through the narrow gap. For the second sound, smile slightly and hold your tongue high and forward. For the third sound, open wide, then glide smoothly up to a high front smile. For the fourth sound, relax your tongue slightly lower. Touch your throat to feel each sound vibrate.

## Spelling rules for Y

At the start of a syllable before a vowel, this letter sounds like /j/, as in (yellow) /jɛl.oʊ/. Without stress at the end of a word, it sounds like /i/, as in (happy) /hæp.i/. With stress at the end of an open syllable, it sounds like /aɪ/, as in (fly) /flaɪ/. In a closed syllable between consonants, it sounds like /ɪ/, as in (gym) /dʒɪm/.

## Common mistakes with Y

Do not pronounce the consonant sound with a hard buzz like a soft j sound. Keep your tongue from touching the roof of your mouth so air glides freely. Do not confuse the short vowel with the long sound in words like (myth) /mɪθ/. Keep your mouth more relaxed than in the word (city) /sɪt.i/.
articles.summary: Letter name: Y. Example: yellow.

articles.title: Z
articles.body:
## Sound of Z

The letter (Z) /ziː/ sounds like the sound /z/. You hear this sound in the word (zebra) /zi.brə/, an animal with black and white stripes. This letter makes three sounds in English words.

## How to say Z

For the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper gum. Push air out smoothly and vibrate your vocal cords. For the second sound, pull your tongue back slightly, push the air, and keep your voice humming. For the third sound, block the air briefly behind your teeth, then release it sharply with no voice. Touch your throat to feel the buzz.

## Spelling patterns

In most places, this letter makes the sound /z/, as in (zone) /zoʊn/. Before an unstressed vowel or u, it makes the sound /ʒ/, as in (azure) /æ.ʒər/. In words borrowed from other languages, it makes the sound /ts/, as in (pizza) /pit.sə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the sound /z/ into an s. Always keep your vocal cords buzzing. Do not let the sound /ʒ/ become the sound /z/. Keep your tongue pulled back slightly and push the air smoothly.
articles.summary: Letter name: Z. Example: zoo.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## Sound of A

You call this letter (A) /æ/. Its main sound is the sound /æ/, as in the word (apple) /æ.pəl/, which means apple. This letter makes four different sounds in English words.

## How to say it

For the first sound, drop your jaw wide and spread your lips flat. For the next sound, move your mouth from an open position toward a smile. For the third sound, relax your mouth completely and let out a quick, weak breath. For the last sound, drop your jaw deeply and keep your tongue low and flat. Feel your throat vibrate for all four sounds.

## Spelling rules

In a closed syllable with stress, say the short sound /æ/, as in (cat) /kæt/. In an open syllable or before a consonant with silent e, say the sound /eɪ/, as in (bake) /beɪk/. In an unstressed syllable, make the quick weak sound /ə/, as in (ago) /ə.ɡoʊ/. Before consonants like lm or in broad words, say the long sound /ɑː/, as in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace the wide sound with a pure ah sound. Open your mouth wide and stretch your lips sideways, like in the word hat. Do not make the weak sound strong or clear. Keep that weak vowel very short, gentle, and quiet.
articles.summary: Letter name: A. Example: cat.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (A) /eɪ/ makes the sound /æ/ in the word (apple) /æ.pəl/, which means apple. This letter has four different sounds in English words.

## How to say it

Open your mouth wide and flatten your tongue low in your mouth. Next, glide from an open vowel to a soft smile sound. Then, relax your lips and tongue completely to make a weak, quick murmur. Finally, open your jaw wide and pull your tongue back without rounding your lips. Place a hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz on each sound.

## Spelling rules

In closed syllables with consonants after it, this letter makes the sound /æ/ as in (cat) /kæt/. In open syllables or before an ending silent e, it sounds like the sound /eɪ/ as in (make) /meɪk/. In weak, unstressed syllables, it softens to the murmur sound /ə/ as in (about) /ə.baʊt/. Before the letter r or in open foreign words, it makes the long back sound /ɑː/ as in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse the short flat sound with the sound in pet. Drop your jaw lower than you think. Do not replace the long vowel with a pure sound. Make sure your tongue moves from open to tight at the end. Keep the unstressed sound very weak and quick.
articles.summary: Letter name: A. Example: name.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (A) /ɑː/ sounds like the short vowel in (apple) /æp.əl/, meaning apple. This letter has four different sounds in English.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, open your mouth wide and flatten your tongue low. For the second sound, glide from an open mouth to spread lips. For the third sound, keep your mouth relaxed and make a short, weak sound. For the fourth sound, open your mouth fully and pull your tongue back. Feel your throat vibrate for all four sounds.

## Reading rules

In closed syllables, read the short sound /æ/ as in (cat) /kæt/. Before a silent e or in open syllables, make the long sound /eɪ/ as in (cake) /keɪk/. In weak syllables without stress, make the soft sound /ə/ as in (about) /ə.baʊt/. Before the letter r, make the deep sound /ɑː/ as in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

## Common mistakes

Do not mix up the short sound /æ/ with a simple open sound. Drop your jaw lower than you would for bed. Do not say the long sound /eɪ/ as one flat vowel. Make sure your tongue moves up at the end. In weak syllables, do not say a clear vowel. Keep the sound very short and quiet.
articles.summary: Letter name: A. Example: father.

articles.title: A
articles.body:
## Sound of A

You call this letter (A) /ə/. Its most common sound is the sound /æ/, as in the word (apple) /æ.pəl/, which means an apple. This letter makes four different sounds in English words.

## How to say it

For the first sound, drop your jaw wide and spread your lips. For the next sound, move your jaw up slightly while your tongue glides forward. For the third sound, keep your tongue completely relaxed in the middle of your mouth. For the final sound, open your mouth wide and keep your tongue flat at the bottom. Put your hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz for all four.

## Spelling rules

In a closed syllable, this letter sounds like the sound /æ/, as in the word (cat) /kæt/. In an open stressed syllable or before silent final e, it sounds like the sound /eɪ/, as in (lake) /leɪk/. In an unstressed syllable, it sounds like the quick sound /ə/, as in (about) /ə.baʊt/. Before certain consonants, it makes the long back sound /ɑː/, as in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

## Common mistakes

Do not mix up the short front sound with a simple flat ah. For the sound in (map) /mæp/, you must open your jaw wider and pull your lips sideways. Do not make the sound in (sofa) /soʊ.fə/ too long or clear, but keep it very short and relaxed. In (spa) /spɑː/, remember to drop your jaw and keep the sound deep.
articles.summary: Letter name: A. Example: about.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## Sound of letter C

The name of this letter is (C) /k/. Its main sound is heard in the word (cat) /kæt/, which means a small pet. This letter has three different sounds.

## How to say it

To make the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Stop the air for a moment, then push it out quickly with no voice. For the second sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth. Blow air through the narrow gap with no voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel no vibration.

## Spelling rules

This letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, u, or before consonants, as in (cup) /kʌp/. It makes the sound /s/ before the letters e, i, or y, as in (city) /sɪ.ti/. In some special words, this letter is not pronounced at all, as in (muscle) /mʌs.əl/.

## Common mistakes

Learners often use voice by mistake when they make the first sound. Keep your vocal cords quiet, so it does not sound like a heavy sound. You might also mix up the two main sounds before the vowels. Check the letter that follows, so you do not pronounce the wrong sound.
articles.summary: Letter name: C. Example: cat.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## Sound of C

The letter (C) /s/ has the name (C) /s/. Its primary sound is the sound /k/, heard in the word (cat) /kæt/, which means cat. This letter produces two different sounds in spoken English.

## How to say C

To make the first sound, lift the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly without using your voice. For the second sound, bring your tongue tip close to your upper gum. Push air smoothly through the narrow opening without using your voice. You can feel cool air on your hand.

## Spelling of C

This letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, u, or before consonants, as in (cup) /kʌp/. It makes the sound /s/ when it stands directly before the letters e, i, or y, as in (cent) /sɛnt/.

## Pitfalls with C

A common mistake is using the wrong sound before different vowels. Remember not to use the sound /k/ before the letters e, i, or y. Do not use your voice on either sound, because both are completely voiceless.
articles.summary: Letter name: C. Example: city.

articles.title: C
articles.body:
## Sound of C

The letter name is (C) /ʃ/. Its main sound is the sound /k/, as heard in (cat) /kæt/. This word means a small furry pet. The letter can make two different spoken sounds, or it can stay silent.

## How to say C

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release a quick puff of air without using your voice. For the second sound, place your tongue tip near your upper teeth. Blow air smoothly through the narrow gap. You can place a hand on your throat to check that your vocal cords stay still.

## Spelling of C

This letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, u or consonants, as in (cup) /kʌp/. It makes the sound /s/ before e, i, or y, like in (city) /sɪ.ti/ or (cent) /sɛnt/. In some special words, this letter is silent and you make no sound at all, as in (muscle) /mʌs.əl/.

## Common mistakes with C

Do not soften the hard sound into a hissing sound when you see the letter before a consonant. Keep the back of your tongue firm to stop the air completely. Before the letters e and i, do not use the hard tapping sound at the back of your mouth. Instead, let the air hiss gently between your teeth.
articles.summary: Letter name: C. Example: ocean.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## Sound of G

The letter (G) /g/ makes the sound /ɡ/ in the word (gas) /ɡæs/, which means gas. This letter has four different sounds in English.

## How to say G

Lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly with voice. For the next sound, touch the roof of your mouth with your tongue tip. Push air through and vibrate your vocal cords. For the third sound, push air smoothly between your tongue and the roof. For the last variant, keep quiet. Place your hand on your neck to feel the voice.

## Spelling of G

Before the letters a, o, u or consonants, this letter makes the sound /ɡ/, like in (gold) /ɡoʊld/. Often before e, i, or y, it makes the sound /dʒ/, as heard in (gem) /dʒɛm/. In French loanwords before e or i, it has the sound /ʒ/, such as in (genre) /ʒɑn.rə/. Before the letter n at the beginning or end of a root word, it is silent, as in (gnat) /næt/.

## Comparing G

Do not drop your voice on the hard sound. If you say it like the sound /k/, your throat will not vibrate. Put a hand on your throat to feel the buzz. Do not confuse the soft sound with the sound /tʃ/. Keep your voice on when you speak.
articles.summary: Letter name: G. Example: go.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## Sound of the letter

The letter (G) /dʒ/ takes its name. It makes the main sound /ɡ/ as in the word (gas) /ɡæs/, which means gas. This letter can make four sounds in total.

## How to say it

Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly with your voice on. For the next sound, touch your tongue tip behind your upper teeth. Push air through while your voice buzzes. Next, push air smoothly through flat lips with voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel the vibration.

## Reading rules

Before the letters a, o, u or consonants, this letter sounds like /ɡ/ in (gap) /ɡæp/. Often before the letters e, i or y, it gives the sound /dʒ/ in (gem) /dʒɛm/. In words borrowed from French, it makes the sound /ʒ/ in (genre) /ʒɑn.rə/. Before the letter n at the start or end of a root, the letter is not pronounced, like in (gnat) /næt/.

## Common mistakes

Do not drop your voice on the hard sound. If you switch off your vocal cords, you make the sound of the letter k. Keep your throat buzzing all the way through the release. Also do not pronounce this letter before n when it begins a word.
articles.summary: Letter name: G. Example: giant.

articles.title: G
articles.body:
## Letter G Sound

The letter (G) /dʒ/ usually makes the sound /ɡ/, as in the word (game) /ɡeɪm/, which means game. Across English words, this letter makes three different sounds, and it can also be silent.

## How to Say

For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air with your voice. For the second sound, touch your tongue tip behind your top front teeth. Push air through while your vocal cords vibrate. For the third sound, round your lips slightly and let voiced air flow smoothly over your tongue. Feel your throat vibrate for all three sounds.

## Reading and Spelling

Before the vowels a, o, or u, before consonants, or at the end of a word, it makes the sound /ɡ/, like in (gas) /ɡæs/. Often before e, i, or y, it makes the sound /dʒ/, like in (gem) /dʒɛm/. In some borrowed words before e or i, it makes the sound /ʒ/, like in (genre) /ʒɒn.rə/. It is not pronounced before the letter n, like in (sign) /saɪn/.

## Common Mistakes

Do not swallow the hard sound or make it rough in your throat. Keep the contact firm against the roof of your mouth, just like the sound in the word go. When it is soft, make sure you add your voice, so it does not sound like church. In words where the letter stands before n, remember to keep it completely silent.
articles.summary: Letter name: G. Example: gym.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## Sound of S

The letter (S) /s/ is named (S) /s/. Its main sound is the sound /s/, as in the word (sun) /sʌn/, which means sun. This letter has four sounds in English words.

## Pronouncing S

To make the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper gum. Push air out smoothly without using your voice. For the second sound, keep the same mouth position and add your voice. For the third sound, pull your tongue back slightly and voice the air. Put a hand on your throat to feel the buzzing vibration during voiced sounds.

## Spelling of S

The letter makes the sound /s/ at word starts, like in (sit) /sɪt/, or after quiet sounds. It makes the sound /z/ between vowels, as in (rose) /roʊz/. It makes the sound /ʒ/ before endings like ion or ure, as in (vision) /vɪ.ʒən/. Finally, the letter is not pronounced in some special words, like in (island) /aɪ.lənd/.

## Common Mistakes

Do not turn the sound /s/ into the sound /z/ too early. Many learners forget to add voice to plurals or between vowels. Touch your throat to check for vibration. When saying words like (dogs) /dɒɡz/, feel your vocal cords buzz at the end.
articles.summary: Letter name: S. Example: sun.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (S) /z/ sounds like the hiss in (sun) /sʌn/, which means the bright star in the sky. It has four sounds.

## How to say it

Put your tongue tip near the roof of your mouth. Blow air gently over your tongue without using your voice. Then make the same shape, but turn your voice on. Next, round your lips slightly, pull your tongue back, and blow quiet air. Finally, make no sound at all. Touch your throat to feel when your voice turns on.

## Spelling rules

At the start of a word, it makes the sound /s/ as in (cats) /kæts/. Between vowels, it makes the sound /z/ as in (busy) /bɪ.zi/. Before unstressed vowel letters, it makes the sound /ʃ/ as in (sugar) /ʃʊɡ.ə/. In some borrowed words, you do not pronounce it, as in (island) /aɪ.lənd/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse the unvoiced hiss with the buzzing sound. When a word ends with this letter after a voiced sound, remember to turn your voice on. Do not add an extra vowel sound before the word starts.
articles.summary: Letter name: S. Example: rose.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (S) /ʃ/ mainly makes the sound /s/. You hear this sound in the word (sun) /sʌn/, which means sun. This letter has three different sounds in English words.

## Mouth movements

For the first sound, place your tongue close to the tooth ridge behind your top teeth. Push air through the small gap without your voice. Your throat stays still. For the second sound, make the exact same mouth shape with your tongue. Now turn your voice on. You can feel your throat buzz with a finger on your neck.

## Spelling rules

This letter makes the sound /s/ at the beginning of words, as in (stop) /stɒp/. It also makes the sound /s/ before sounds that use no voice. Between vowels or after voiced sounds, it makes the sound /z/, as in (rose) /roʊz/ or (busy) /bɪ.zi/. The letter is silent in a few special words, such as (island) /aɪ.lənd/.

## Common mistakes

Do not confuse the quiet hissing sound with the buzzing sound. When you make the sound /z/, your vocal cords must vibrate. Check this by pressing two fingers gently to your throat while speaking.
articles.summary: Letter name: S. Example: sure.

articles.title: S
articles.body:
## The letter es

The letter (S) /ʒ/ is named es. It usually makes the sound /s/, like in the word (sun) /sʌn/, which means the star that lights our daytime sky. This letter has four different sounds across common English words.

## Making the sounds

Put the tip of your tongue close to the gum behind your top teeth. Push air through the small gap with no voice. For the second sound, keep the same position and add your voice. Next, pull your tongue slightly back and let voiced air rush through. Sometimes the letter is silent, so your mouth stays still. Put your hand on your neck to feel the vibration turn on and off.

## Reading the variants

At the start of words or before quiet consonants, it sounds like the sound /s/ in (sit) /sɪt/. Between vowels or at the end of many words, it makes the sound /z/ in (busy) /bɪ.zi/ and (rose) /roʊz/. Before endings like ion or ual after a vowel, it sounds like the sound /ʒ/ in (vision) /vɪ.ʒən/ and (usual) /ju.ʒu.əl/. In a few special words, the letter is not pronounced, such as in (island) /aɪ.lənd/ and (aisle) /aɪl/.

## Avoiding common traps

Do not add an extra vowel sound before this letter at the start of words. Keep your voice quiet when you say the first sound, so it does not turn into a buzz. When a word ends with a buzz, let your throat vibrate fully instead of whispering the finish. Make sure to keep the letter completely silent in the rare words where it makes no sound.
articles.summary: Letter name: S. Example: vision.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Letter T Sound

The letter (T) /t/ is called (T) /t/. Its main sound is the sound /t/, that is a crisp sound, as in (top) /tɑp/, which means top. This letter makes two spoken sounds. Sometimes it makes no sound at all.

## How To Say

Press the tip of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Hold the air back. Then release the breath with a sharp puff. Do not use your voice. For the quick tap, bounce the tongue tip lightly against the roof. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel the puff.

## Spelling Rules

This letter usually makes the sound /t/, that is a crisp sound, as in (ten) /tɛn/. Between vowels before an unstressed syllable, it makes the sound /ɾ/, that is a quick flap, as in (butter) /bʌ.tər/. In words with letters s, t, l or s, t, e, n, it makes no sound, as in (listen) /lɪs.ən/.

## Common Mistakes

Do not voice this crisp sound like the sound in dog. Keep your vocal cords still. Do not blow too much air when the sound sits at the end of a word. When you say the fast flap, do not stop the air fully. Tap your tongue quickly without stopping the flow.
articles.summary: Letter name: T. Example: top.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (T) /ʃ/ makes the sound /t/ in (table) /teɪ.bəl/, which means table. This letter has three sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, press your tongue tip behind your top teeth. Release a small puff of air with no voice. For the second sound, press your tongue tip higher. Then push air through gently, like the start of church. Put your hand on your throat. Your vocal cords do not vibrate.

## Spelling rules

This letter usually makes the sound /t/ at the start of a word, as in (ten) /tɛn/. Before an unstressed u, it makes the sound /tʃ/, as in (nature) /neɪ.tʃər/. In groups like sten or stle, it is silent, as in (castle) /kæ.səl/.

## Common mistakes

Do not voice the first sound into a d. Keep your vocal cords still and let a quick puff of air escape. Do not say the silent letter in words like (listen) /lɪ.sən/. Drop the sound completely.
articles.summary: Letter name: T. Example: station.

articles.title: T
articles.body:
## Sound of T

The letter (T) /tʃ/ has two spoken sounds. Its main sound is heard in the word (top) /tɑp/, which means top. Sometimes this letter makes a quick tap instead. In other words, you do not pronounce it at all.

## How to say T

Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Release the air suddenly without using your voice. For the quick tap, strike that same ridge very fast once with your tongue tip. Put your hand on your throat. You feel no buzzing for the first sound, but a quick vibration for the tap.

## Spelling of T

At the start of a word, it makes the sound /t/, that is a crisp unvoiced burst, as in (ten) /tɛn/. Between two vowels before a light beat, it makes the sound /ɾ/, that is a fast tap, as in (water) /wɑ.tɚ/. In some words after the letter s, it is not pronounced, as in (listen) /lɪ.sən/.

## Common mistakes

Do not press your tongue flat against your upper teeth. That mistake creates an unnatural, thick sound. Touch only the gum ridge behind your teeth, and let the air escape cleanly. Also, remember to stay quiet when this letter follows s in words like (castle) /kæ.səl/.
articles.summary: Letter name: T. Example: nature.

articles.title: -t- (silent)
articles.body:
## The silent letter

The letter inside words is sometimes silent and has no sound at all. In the word (listen) /lɪs.ən/, which means to pay attention with your ears, you hear no consonant there. This spelling pattern creates only this one silent variation in these words.

## Mouth and air

Your mouth makes no extra sound here. You move your tongue directly from the first sound to the next sound without stopping. Keep your breath flowing smoothly. Your throat stays relaxed during this transition.

## When it is silent

The letter stays quiet in the middle of words between other consonants. It often disappears before another consonant sound, as in the word (castle) /kɑːs.əl/. You simply drop the sound completely whenever you see this pattern.

## Common mistakes

Learners often try to pronounce every written consonant clearly. You must never tap your tongue against your teeth here. Simply move straight from the preceding sound to the following sound without adding any consonant touch.
articles.summary: Letter name: -t- (silent). Example: listen.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## Letter X sound

The letter (X) /ks/ is called /ks/. Its main sound is heard in the word (box) /bɒks/, which means box. This letter makes three different sounds in English words.

## How to say X

For the first sound, push the back of your tongue up, release air, and then hiss. For the second sound, make that same back sound with voice, and then buzz. For the third sound, put your tongue tip near your upper teeth and buzz with your voice. Touch your throat to feel the voice buzz.

## Spelling rules for X

Most often, especially in the middle or at the end of a word, it sounds like the sound /ks/, as in (fox) /fɒks/. Before a stressed vowel, it sounds like the sound /ɡz/, as in (exam) /ɪɡ.zæm/. At the beginning of a word, it sounds like the sound /z/, as in (xenon) /zɛn.ɒn/.

## Common mistakes with X

Do not pronounce the beginning of a word with the sound /ks/. Say only the buzzing sound /z/, with your voice on. At the end of a word, do not drop the hissing sound /s/. Make sure you pronounce both sounds clearly, without adding an extra vowel at the end.
articles.summary: Letter name: X. Example: box.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## Letter sound

You call this letter (X) /gz/. Its main sound is heard in the word (box) /bɒks/, which means a square container. This letter has three different sounds.

## Mouth movements

For the first sound, stop air with the back of your tongue, release it without voice, and push air through your teeth. For the second sound, make that same stop and hiss, but keep your voice buzzing. For the third sound, blow air smoothly over the tongue tip with voice. Feel your throat buzz on the voiced sounds.

## Reading rules

At the end of a word or before quiet consonants, pronounce the sound /ks/ as in (tax) /tæks/. Between vowels right before a stressed syllable, say the sound /ɡz/ as in (exam) /ɪɡ.zæm/ or (exist) /ɪɡ.zɪst/. At the beginning of a word, pronounce the sound /z/ as in (xylophone) /zaɪ.lə.fəʊn/ or (xenon) /zɛn.ɒn/.

## Common mistakes

Do not add an extra vowel sound before this letter at the start of a word. Many learners try to pronounce a stop sound first. Start smoothly with a buzzing hiss, exactly like the first sound in zoo. Keep the air flowing without stopping it.
articles.summary: Letter name: X. Example: exam.

articles.title: X
articles.body:
## Sound of letter X

You call this letter (X) /kʃ/. Its most common sound is heard in (fox) /fɒks/, which means a wild animal with red fur. The letter makes three different sounds in English words.

## How to say it

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to stop the air. Release it with a hissing stream behind your upper teeth without voice. For the second sound, make the same movements, but keep your voice buzzing. Touch your throat to feel that buzz. For the third sound, bring your teeth close together and blow air while humming.

## Spelling rules

At the end of a word or before quiet consonants, it sounds like the sound /ks/ in (six) /sɪks/. Before a stressed vowel, you say the sound /ɡz/ as in (exam) /ɪɡ.zæm/, or in (exist) /ɪɡ.zɪst/. At the beginning of a word, it takes the buzzing sound /z/ in (xylophone) /zaɪ.lə.fəʊn/, and in (xenon) /zɛ.nɒn/.

## Common mistakes

Do not drop the first stop sound when you say the ending combinations. Make sure your tongue touches the roof of your mouth before you hiss. At the start of a word, never add a stop sound before the buzz. Start smoothly with the sound /z/.
articles.summary: Letter name: X. Example: luxury.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## Letter sound

You call this letter (Y) /j/. Its main sound is heard in the word (yes) /jɛs/, which means yes. This letter can make four different sounds.

## How to say it

For the first sound, lift your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Smoothly glide into the next vowel with voice. For the second sound, open wide and then glide up to a smile. For the third sound, spread your lips and make a clear high voice. For the fourth sound, relax your tongue and mouth a little. Put a hand on your throat to feel each sound vibrate.

## Reading rules

Before a vowel at the start of a syllable, it makes the sound /j/ as in (yam) /jæm/. At the end of a short one-syllable word, it makes the sound /aɪ/ as in (my) /maɪ/. At the end of a longer word without stress, it makes the sound /i/ as in (happy) /hæ.pi/. Inside a closed syllable of Greek origin, it makes the sound /ɪ/ as in (gym) /dʒɪm/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the first sound into a hard friction. Keep the air flowing smoothly without any buzzing. At the end of short words, do not make a flat vowel. Remember to open your mouth wide first and then move your lips into a smile.
articles.summary: Letter name: Y. Example: yes.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## The letter Y

The letter (Y) /ɪ/ makes the sound /j/, as in (yes) /jɛs/, which means yes. This letter makes four different sounds in English. Sometimes it works as a consonant, and sometimes it works as a vowel.

## How to say it

Raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Let voiced air glide through smoothly. For the second sound, smile slightly and keep your tongue high at the front. For the third sound, open your mouth wide, then glide up to a smile. For the last sound, relax your tongue slightly lower. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz.

## Reading and spelling

At the start of a word before a vowel, it sounds like /j/, as in (yard) /jɑːd/. Unstressed at the end of a word, it sounds like /i/, as in (happy) /hæ.pi/. At the end of a short word or in an open stressed syllable, it sounds like /aɪ/, as in (my) /maɪ/. Inside a closed syllable, it sounds like /ɪ/, as in (gym) /dʒɪm/.

## Common mistakes

Do not turn the first sound into a hard friction sound like the start of judge. Keep the airflow smooth and open. Do not lengthen the short vowel sound into a long tense vowel. Keep your tongue relaxed and slightly low.
articles.summary: Letter name: Y. Example: myth.

articles.title: Y
articles.body:
## Letter sound

The letter (Y) /aɪ/ makes four different sounds. Its main sound is the sound /j/. You hear it at the start of (yes) /jɛs/, which means yes.

## Mouth shape

For the first sound, raise the middle of your tongue near the roof of your mouth. Push your voice out smoothly without touching the roof. For the second sound, smile slightly and hold your tongue high and forward. For the third sound, open your mouth wide, then glide your jaw up. For the fourth sound, drop your jaw slightly and keep your tongue relaxed. Feel your vocal cords vibrate for all four sounds.

## Reading rules

At the start of a word before a vowel, say the sound /j/ as in (yard) /jɑːd/. At the end of a word without stress, say the sound /i/ as in (happy) /hæ.pi/ or (city) /sɪ.ti/. In a stressed short word or open syllable, say the sound /aɪ/ as in (cry) /kraɪ/ or (style) /staɪl/. Inside a closed syllable, say the sound /ɪ/ as in (myth) /mɪθ/ or (system) /sɪs.təm/.

## Common errors

Do not press your tongue against the roof of your mouth when starting a word. If you push too hard, you make an English j sound instead of the sound /j/. Keep the air flowing smoothly like a vowel. Also, do not make the ending of two-syllable words too long.
articles.summary: Letter name: Y. Example: fly.

articles.title: kn-
articles.body:
## The letters kn

The letters kn sound like the sound /n/. In the word (knee) /ni/, they mean a knee. These two letters make only one single sound.

## Mouth shape

Press the tip of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Send the air smoothly through your nose. Turn on your voice. You can feel your throat buzz with your fingers.

## Reading the letters

The letters kn appear at the beginning of a word before a vowel. You never pronounce the first letter. You say only the sound /n/, as in (knot) /nɒt/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the first letter. A common mistake is saying an extra tapping sound at the start. Begin cleanly with the nose sound, exactly like the start of net.
articles.summary: Letter name: kn-. Example: knife.

articles.title: kn-
articles.body:
## The spelling kn

The letters kn make the sound /n/. You hear this sound in (knee) /ni/, which means the joint in the middle of your leg. This letter group makes only one sound in English words.

## How to say it

Press the tip of your tongue against the roof of your mouth, just behind your front teeth. Keep your lips slightly open. Push the air out through your nose while your voice hums. Touch your throat to feel the strong buzz. Do not let any air pop through your lips.

## When to use it

The letters kn appear at the beginning of words. The first letter stays completely silent, so you only say the sound /n/. You hear this in the word (knot) /nɒt/.

## Common mistakes

Learners often try to pronounce the first letter. Never make a hard clicking sound before the sound /n/. Start straight with your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Smoothly say the sound without any pause or extra push of air.
articles.summary: Letter name: kn-. Example: know.

articles.title: wr-
articles.body:
## The spelling wr

The letters wr sound like /r/. Together they make the sound in the word (wrist) /rɪst/, meaning wrist. This letter group makes only one sound.

## How to say wr

Curl the tip of your tongue backward near the roof of your mouth. Do not let your tongue touch the roof. Round your lips a little bit. Push air out gently while your vocal cords vibrate. Put a hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration.

## When wr sounds like r

The letters wr appear at the beginning of words before a vowel. They always make the single sound /r/, as in the word (write) /raɪt/. Another example is the word (wrong) /rɒŋ/. The first letter is silent.

## Common mistakes with wr

Learners often try to pronounce the first letter before the second letter. Do not close your lips tightly or push out a puff of air. Only make one smooth sound with your tongue curled back, just like in red.
articles.summary: Letter name: wr-. Example: write.

articles.title: gn-
articles.body:
## The letters gn

The letters gn sound as the sound /n/. Their main sound is the sound /n/, heard in (gnat) /næt/, which means gnat. These letters make only one sound.

## How to say it

Touch the roof of your mouth just behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Let the air flow freely through your nose. Turn on your voice. Feel your throat vibrate while your tongue stays in place.

## When to use it

The letters gn appear at the beginning of words before a vowel. They sound as the sound /n/, for example in (gnaw) /nɔː/.

## Common mistakes

Never say the first letter as a separate sound before the nasal sound. Do not add a hard consonant sound before the sound /n/. Drop the first letter entirely and start directly with the sound /n/.
articles.summary: Letter name: gn-. Example: gnome.

articles.title: -mb
articles.body:
## Sound of -mb

The letters -mb sound like /m/. You hear this in (lamb) /læm/, which means lamb. The letters make only one sound.

## How to say it

Close both lips together gently. Let air flow out through your nose. Turn on your voice box. Place a hand on your throat to feel it buzz.

## Spelling rules

The letters -mb appear at the end of a word or root. The second letter stays completely silent. The ending sounds as the sound /m/ in (comb) /koʊm/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the final consonant as a separate sound. Keep your lips closed quietly at the end. Do not pop your lips open as you finish the word.
articles.summary: Letter name: -mb. Example: lamb.

articles.title: -lk
articles.body:
## Sounds of lk

The spelling -lk sounds like the sound /k/. You hear it in (walk) /wɔːk/, which means to walk. This letter group makes two different sounds in English words.

## Making the sounds

For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof. Stop the air, then release it with a sharp burst. Your vocal cords stay still. For the second sound, first touch the roof with your tongue tip. Let air flow around the sides, then make that sharp burst.

## Reading the spelling

At the end of words where the first letter is silent, you say the sound /k/. You hear this pattern in (talk) /tɔːk/. After vowels where both letters are sounded, you say the sound /lk/. You hear this in (milk) /mɪlk/ and in (silk) /sɪlk/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the first letter in words where it stays quiet. Keep the sound simple and clean. Make the sharp burst at the very end.
articles.summary: Letter name: -lk. Example: walk.

articles.title: -lf
articles.body:
## The group lf

The letters lf sound like the sound /f/. You hear this in the word (calf) /kɑːf/, which means a young cow. This letter group makes two different sounds.

## Mouth movements

For the first sound, place your top teeth gently on your bottom lip. Blow air through the small gap without using your voice. For the second sound, touch the roof of your mouth with your tongue tip. Let voice flow, then move quickly to your bottom lip and blow air. Place your fingers on your throat to feel when voice starts.

## Reading the letters

In some everyday words, the first letter stays silent. The letters then make only the sound /f/, as in (half) /hɑːf/. In other words, you pronounce both letters together. The group then makes the sound /lf/, as in (gulf) /ɡʌlf/.

## Common mistakes

Do not force an l sound into every word you see. Saying an l sound in words where it is silent is an easy mistake. Check which words keep both sounds and keep your tongue low when the letter is silent.
articles.summary: Letter name: -lf. Example: half.

articles.title: -stle
articles.body:
## Sound of stle

The ending -stle is pronounced /səl/. Its main sound appears in (castle) /kɑː.səl/, which means a large stone stronghold. This spelling pattern always makes one single sound combination.

## How to say it

Blow air smoothly over your tongue tip near the roof of your mouth. Then touch the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Let the voiced air pass through the sides of your mouth. Put a hand on your neck to feel your throat vibrate at the very end.

## Spelling rules

At the end of a word, the group -stle sounds like /səl/. The letter t stays completely silent, as heard in (rustle) /rʌ.səl/.

## Common mistakes

Do not pronounce the letter t in this ending. Skip the t completely so it sounds like the middle of muscle.
articles.summary: Letter name: -stle. Example: castle.

articles.title: -gh(t)
articles.body:
## The group -gh(t)

The letter group -gh(t) makes no sound at all. In the word (night) /naɪt/, which means night, the middle letters stay silent. You hear only the surrounding sounds. This group has one single spoken pattern.

## How to say -gh(t)

Do not move your tongue or lips for these letters. Let the air pass straight to the final sound without pausing. You make no voice and no friction in your throat. Your vocal cords do not vibrate until the next letter.

## Spelling of -gh(t)

Before the letter t, the group gh is always completely silent. You see this pattern in common words like (light) /laɪt/ and (sight) /saɪt/. Just jump over the two middle letters when you read.

## Comparing -gh(t)

Learners often try to pronounce a rough scraping sound in their throat. Do not make any sound like the end of the Scottish word loch. Keep your throat open and silent, moving straight to the next spoken sound.
articles.summary: Letter name: -gh(t). Example: night.

articles.title: -bt
articles.body:
## The spelling bt

The letter group -bt sounds like the sound /t/. You hear this in the word (debt) /dɛt/, which means money you owe. This group has only one spoken sound.

## Producing the sound

Press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Stop the air for a moment. Then drop your tongue to release a small puff of air. Keep your vocal cords still. Touch your throat to feel that it does not buzz.

## Reading the letters

At the end of words, the letter b remains completely silent. The following letter sounds like the sound /t/. You can hear this clearly in the word (doubt) /daʊt/.

## Avoiding mistakes

The only common mistake is trying to pronounce both letters together. Do not close your lips to make a b sound. Move straight to the t sound, exactly like in the normal English word cat.
articles.summary: Letter name: -bt. Example: debt.

articles.title: -sland
articles.body:
## Sound of -sland

The letter ending -sland is called /lənd/. It makes the sound /lənd/, as in the word (island) /aɪ.lənd/, which means a piece of land surrounded by water. This letter group makes only one sound in standard English words.

## How to say -sland

Touch the tip of your tongue to the roof of your mouth for the first sound. Drop your tongue slightly into the center of your mouth for a brief vowel. Touch the tip to the roof again, and finish by closing both lips to stop the air. Your vocal cords vibrate all the way through.

## Spelling of -sland

This spelling pattern appears at the end of unstressed words and geographic names. The letter s is silent before the ending. It sounds like /lənd/ in every standard noun of this type.

## Comparing -sland

Do not pronounce the letter s in this ending. Saying an s sound is a common mistake. Keep the sound silent just like in the everyday word aisle. Touch your throat to ensure your voice hums continuously through the rest of the ending.
articles.summary: Letter name: -sland. Example: island.

articles.title: th
articles.body:
## The letters th

The letter pair th is spoken as the sound /θ/. Its main sound appears in the word (think) /θɪŋk/, which means to think. These two letters together make three different sounds.

## How to say th

Place the tip of your tongue lightly between your teeth. Blow air through the small gap without your voice. For the next sound, keep the exact same tongue position, but turn on your voice. Put a hand on your throat to feel the strong vibration. For the last sound, tap your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth.

## Spelling rules for th

The letters th make the sound /θ/ in most nouns, verbs and adjectives, like (thing) /θɪŋ/. You also hear this sound at the end of words, like (bath) /bɑːθ/. The letters make the sound /ð/ in grammatical words, like (this) /ðɪs/. They make that voiced sound between vowels, like (father) /fɑː.ðə/. In a few special words, they make the sound /t/, like (thyme) /taɪm/.

## Common mistakes with th

Do not replace the soft sound with the sound /s/ or /f/. Keep your tongue between your teeth so air slips through gently. Do not swap the voiced sound for the sound /d/ or /z/. If you hold your tongue behind your teeth, you will make the wrong sound.
articles.summary: Letter name: th. Example: think.

articles.title: th
articles.body:
## The letters th

The letters th make two sounds. The main sound is the sound /θ/. You hear it in the word (think) /θɪŋk/, which means to think.

## Making the sounds

Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your front teeth. Blow air softly over the tongue without voice for the first sound. Keep the tongue in the same place and add your voice for the second sound. Feel your throat with your hand to sense the buzz.

## Reading the letters

The letters th make the voiceless sound /θ/ in most everyday words and at the end of words, as in (bath) /bɑːθ/. They make the voiced sound /ð/ in small grammar words like (this) /ðɪs/, and between vowels as in (father) /fɑː.ðə/.

## Common mistakes

Do not replace these sounds with an s, z, t, or d sound. Keep your tongue right between your front teeth, not behind them. Let the air flow smoothly, without stopping it completely.
articles.summary: Letter name: th. Example: this.

articles.title: sh
articles.body:
## Sound of sh

The letters sh make the sound /ʃ/. You hear this main sound in the word (ship) /ʃɪp/, which means ship. These letters make only one sound in English.

## Mouth movements

Push your lips slightly forward into a soft circle. Raise the front of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Blow air smoothly over your tongue without using your voice. Place a hand on your throat to check that it does not buzz.

## Spelling rules

The letters sh always make the sound /ʃ/ in standard English words. You hear it at the end of the word (fish) /fɪʃ/.

## Common mistakes

Do not smile or place your tongue tip against your teeth. That mistake makes the sound /s/ as in see. Keep your lips pushed forward and keep your tongue away from your teeth.
articles.summary: Letter name: sh. Example: ship.

articles.title: ch
articles.body:
## The group ch

The letter group ch makes the sound /tʃ/. You hear it in the word (chin) /tʃɪn/, which means the chin on your face. This group has three different sounds across English words.

## How to say it
